name: Biology
topics: Variety of organisms: classification and the five kingdoms
Cell structure, organelles and levels of organisation
Cell properties: diffusion, osmosis, active transport, plasmolysis
Nutrition in plants: photosynthesis and mineral requirements
Nutrition in animals: food classes, digestion and enzymes
Transport in plants and animals: blood, heart, xylem and phloem, transpiration
Respiration: aerobic, anaerobic and respiratory organs
Excretion: kidney, skin, lungs and excretion in plants
Support and movement: skeleton, joints, muscles, plant support tissues
Reproduction in plants and animals
Growth and development, germination
Coordination: nervous system, reflex action and sense organs
Hormones in animals and plants
Ecology: ecosystems, food chains, food webs and energy flow
Nutrient cycles and ecological factors
Population ecology, adaptation and tropical biomes in Nigeria
Pollution, conservation and natural resources
Variation and heredity: Mendelian genetics, crosses and ratios
Sex determination, sex-linked traits, blood groups and genetic disorders
Evolution: theories and evidence
Diseases, parasites and immunity
Biotechnology and applied genetics

questions.q: Which of the following hierarchical classification categories contains the most closely related organisms?
questions.e: A species is the lowest and most specific taxonomic rank in biological classification, grouping individuals that can interbreed and share the most recent common ancestry.
questions.p: Species na the lowest and most specific rank for biology classification, and e dey group organisms wey resemble each other well well and fit mate.

questions.q: In the five-kingdom system of classification proposed by Robert Whittaker, prokaryotic organisms lacking a true membrane-bound nucleus are placed in the kingdom:
questions.e: Kingdom Monera comprises all prokaryotes, such as bacteria and blue-green algae, which do not possess a true membrane-bound nucleus or membrane-bound organelles.
questions.p: Kingdom Monera na where all prokaryotic organisms like bacteria dey, because dem no get true nucleus wey get membrane.

questions.q: Organisms that are heterotrophic, possess a cell wall made of chitin, and absorb their nutrients externally belong to the kingdom:
questions.e: Fungi are distinct from plants because they lack chlorophyll and have chitinous cell walls instead of cellulose, absorbing nutrients through saprophytic or parasitic nutrition.
questions.p: Fungi different from plants because dem no get chlorophyll and dia cell wall na chitin, plus dem dey absorb dia food from outside.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches a kingdom with its primary mode of nutrition?
questions.e: Members of the kingdom Plantae contain chlorophyll and manufacture their own food through photosynthesis, making them autotrophic.
questions.p: Na plants dey make dia own food through photosynthesis, so dem bi autotrophs, unlike fungi wey dey absorb food.

questions.q: According to the binomial system of nomenclature introduced by Carl Linnaeus, the scientific name of the domestic dog, Canis familiaris, indicates that:
o: Canis is the specific epithet and familiaris is the genus
Canis is the genus and familiaris is the specific epithet
Both words represent the family name
Familiaris is the phylum and Canis is the species
questions.e: In binomial nomenclature, the first name represents the genus (with a capital letter) and the second name represents the species or specific epithet (in lowercase).
questions.p: For binomial system, the first name na the genus and the second name na the species epithet, just like Canis familiaris.

questions.q: An organism is microscopic, unicellular, eukaryotic, and moves using cilia. In Whittaker's five-kingdom classification, this organism is best classified under:
questions.e: Kingdom Protista includes mostly unicellular eukaryotes, such as Paramecium, which moves using cilia, distinguishing them from prokaryotic Monera and multicellular eukaryotes.
questions.p: Kingdom Protista na house for single-celled eukaryotic organisms like Paramecium wey dey use cilia swim around.

questions.q: Which of the following features is used to distinguish members of the kingdom Plantae from members of the kingdom Animalia?
questions.e: Plant cells are enclosed by a rigid cell wall made primarily of cellulose, whereas animal cells completely lack cell walls.
questions.p: Na only plant cells get rigid cell wall wey cellulose make, but animal cells no get cell wall at all.

questions.q: In a biological survey of a freshwater pond in Ibadan, a teacher collects an organism that is multicellular, lacks chlorophyll, has no root system, and reproduces by spores. This organism most likely belongs to:
questions.e: Multicellularity combined with the absence of chlorophyll, lack of true roots, and spore reproduction are characteristic features of multicellular fungi such as moulds and mushrooms.
questions.p: Since the thing multi-cellular, no get chlorophyll, no get root, and dey produce spores, na proper fungus be that.

questions.q: Which of the following taxonomic ranks is immediately broader than a 'family' in the hierarchy of classification?
questions.e: The hierarchy from broad to narrow is Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. Therefore, the rank immediately broader than family is order.
questions.p: If you arrange am from top to bottom: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species. E clear say Order dey just above Family.

questions.q: A student examines an unknown microorganism in the laboratory and discovers it possesses a rigid cell wall, lacks organized membrane-bound organelles, and multiplies by binary fission. This organism should be placed in kingdom:
questions.e: The lack of membrane-bound organelles combined with binary fission clearly identifies the organism as a prokaryote belonging to kingdom Monera.
questions.p: Because the organism no get membrane-bound organelles and e dey divide by binary fission, na pure Monera (bacteria) be that.

questions.q: Why are viruses excluded from the five-kingdom classification system proposed by Whittaker?
o: They are acellular and lack metabolic machinery outside a host cell.
They are too large to be classified.
questions.e: Viruses are considered non-cellular particles that do not fit into cellular classification systems because they cannot carry out life processes independently outside of a living host.
questions.p: We no dey put virus inside the five kingdoms because dem no even get cell structure and dem no fit live on dia own without host.

questions.q: Which of the following organisms represents a typical link between plants and animals, possessing chlorophyll for photosynthesis in sunlight, yet able to feed heterotrophically in the dark?
questions.e: Euglena is a unicellular protist that exhibits plant-like characteristics (presence of chloroplasts for autotrophic nutrition) and animal-like characteristics (absence of cell wall and ability to ingest food in darkness).
questions.p: Euglena na stubborn protist because when sun shine, e dey do photosynthesis like plant, but when dark, e dey find food chop like animal.

questions.q: Which of the following cellular structures is primarily responsible for the packaging and secretion of synthesized proteins in a secretory cell like a mammalian exocrine pancreatic cell?
questions.e: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins received from the endoplasmic reticulum into vesicles for secretion. Ribosomes synthesize proteins, but do not package them. Lysosomes handle intracellular digestion, while centrioles are involved in cell division.
questions.p: Na Golgi apparatus dey package and send out proteins wey cell don make. Ribosome na im dey create the protein, but na Golgi dey ready am for export.

questions.q: A student examines a plant cell under a light microscope and notices green, oval-shaped bodies undergoing cytoplasmic streaming. These organelles are most likely containing which of the following pigments?
questions.e: The green, oval-shaped bodies inside plant cells are chloroplasts, which contain the green photosynthetic pigment chlorophyll. Anthocyanins are water-soluble vacuolar pigments giving red or blue colors, while fucoxanthin and carotene are accessory pigments found mainly in other groups.
questions.p: Those green, oval things wey you dey see inside plant cell na chloroplasts, and na chlorophyll pigment dey give them that green color.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly traces the path of carbon dioxide as it moves out of a respiring plant cell during the night?
o: Vacuole -> Mitochondrion -> Cytoplasm -> Cell membrane -> Intercellular space
Chloroplast -> Cytoplasm -> Cell wall -> Cell membrane -> Stoma
Cell wall -> Cell membrane -> Cytoplasm -> Mitochondrion -> Intercellular space
Mitochondrion -> Cytoplasm -> Cell membrane -> Cell wall -> Intercellular space
questions.e: During the night, respiration occurs inside the mitochondrion producing carbon dioxide. The gas diffuses through the cytoplasm, crosses the plasma membrane and cell wall into the intercellular air spaces before leaving the leaf.
questions.p: For night time, respiration dey happen for mitochondrion where carbon dioxide dey form. E go pass through cytoplasm, commot cell membrane and cell wall, enter space between cells before e finally escape.

questions.q: In an experiment, red blood cells placed in a concentrated salt solution shrink and develop a notched or crinkled surface. This process is known as:
questions.e: Crenation is the shrinkage and crinkling of animal cells when placed in a hypertonic solution due to exosmosis of water. Plasmolysis is the equivalent process in plant cells where the protoplasm pulls away from the cell wall.
questions.p: When animal cell like red blood cell shrink inside strong salt water because water dey commot body, we dey call am crenation. Plasmolysis na for plant cell.

questions.q: A cell biologist treats a eukaryotic cell with a metabolic poison that specifically halts ATP synthesis on the inner mitochondrial membrane. Which of the following cellular processes will be immediately arrested?
o: Simple diffusion of oxygen gas across the plasma membrane
Movement of carbon dioxide out of the cell
Active transport of sodium ions against their concentration gradient
Osmosis of water molecules through aquaporins
questions.e: Active transport requires metabolic energy in the form of ATP to move substances against a concentration gradient. Simple diffusion, osmosis, and gas movement are passive processes that do not require ATP.
questions.p: Active transport na the only process for option wey need ATP energy to work. Once ATP stop, active transport go stop immediately, but diffusion and osmosis fit still manage continue.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best describes the structural difference between rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) and smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER)?
o: RER is studded with ribosomes on its outer surface whereas SER lacks ribosomes
RER forms closed circular vesicles while SER forms long linear tubules
RER is found only in plant cells whereas SER is restricted to animal cells
RER is composed of lipids while SER is composed of proteins
questions.e: The rough endoplasmic reticulum is named 'rough' because its outer membrane surface is studded with ribosomes actively involved in protein synthesis. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum does not have ribosomes and is involved in lipid synthesis.
questions.p: Rough endoplasmic reticulum get small small particles wey be ribosome for body, na why e rough. Smooth endoplasmic reticulum no get ribosome, na lipid e dey produce.

questions.q: If a plant tissue is soaked in distilled water for two hours, the cells become firm and rigid. This turgidity is primarily maintained by the mechanical strength of which of the following structures?
questions.e: When water enters plant cells by osmosis, the protoplast swells, pressing against the rigid cellulose cell wall. The cell wall resists expansion, creating turgor pressure that keeps the plant tissue firm.
questions.p: When water enter plant cell, the cell go swell up. Na the strong cell wall dey hold am tight make e no burst, na im dey give the plant that rigid shape.

questions.q: During the examination of a thin slice of onion bulb epidermis under a light microscope, which of the following cell organelles is most unlikely to be observed clearly without special staining?
questions.e: Ribosomes are extremely tiny sub-microscopic organelles (about 20-30 nm in diameter) that cannot be resolved as individual structures using a standard light microscope. Cell walls, nuclei, and large central vacuoles are easily visible.
questions.p: Ribosome too small small, ordinary light microscope no fit show them clearly. But cell wall, nucleus and vacuole big small, you fit see them with ordinary microscope.

questions.q: Which of the following cellular components contains genetic material in a eukaryotic cell?
questions.e: In eukaryotic cells, DNA is primarily found in the nucleus, but semi-autonomous organelles such as mitochondria and chloroplasts also contain their own circular DNA molecules. Other listed options lack DNA.
questions.p: Eukaryotic cell get DNA for nucleus, but mitochondria and chloroplasts sef get their own personal DNA. Other organelles for the wrong options no get DNA at all.

questions.q: Which of the following processes requires a direct expenditure of metabolic energy by the cell?
o: Uptake of mineral ions by plant roots from a dilute soil solution
Spread of perfume scent in a closed room
Movement of water molecules into a fresh potato tuber
Movement of oxygen gas across the alveoli
questions.e: Active transport requires cellular energy (ATP) to move substances against a concentration gradient, such as mineral ion uptake from dilute soil. The other processes rely on kinetic energy and occur via passive transport.
questions.p: Active transport dey need energy (ATP) to carry mineral salt from where e small go where e plenty for soil. Na only that one need energy among the options.

questions.q: What happens when a fresh spirogyra filament is immersed in a 10 percent concentrated sodium chloride solution?
o: The cell remains unchanged because the cell wall is impermeable
Water enters the cell rapidly, causing it to burst
The protoplasm shrinks away from the rigid cell wall
Salt molecules move out through the cell wall by osmosis
questions.e: A 10 percent sodium chloride solution is hypertonic to the cell sap of spirogyra. Water leaves the cell via osmosis, leading to plasmolysis where the protoplasm shrinks away from the cellulose cell wall.
questions.p: That strong salt water dey hypertonic to spirogyra cell. Water go rush commot, make the protoplasm shrink commot from body of the cell wall, wetin we dey call plasmolysis.

questions.q: The net movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a selectively permeable membrane is known as:
questions.e: Osmosis is strictly defined as the movement of water or solvent molecules across a differentially permeable membrane down a water potential gradient.
questions.p: Osmosis na the movement of water molecules from where water plenty go where water small through membrane wey selective.

questions.q: A red blood cell placed in distilled water will eventually burst, whereas a plant cell placed in the same distilled water will become turgid but not burst. The primary reason for this difference is the presence of:
o: more hemoglobin in the red blood cell
an active transport mechanism in the animal cell
a rigid cellulose cell wall in the plant cell
a large central vacuole in the plant cell
questions.e: Plant cells have a tough, rigid cellulose cell wall that exerts wall pressure to counterbalance turgor pressure, preventing lysis. Animal cells lack this protective wall and burst when excess water enters.
questions.p: Plant cell get strong cell wall wey dey hold am make e no burst when water enter. Animal cell no get that wall, na im make red blood cell dey burst for distilled water.

questions.q: If a few crystals of potassium permanganate are dropped at the bottom of a beaker filled with clear water, the water eventually turns purple throughout. This phenomenon best demonstrates:
questions.e: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration due to their random thermal motion.
questions.p: As potassium permanganate particles dey spread enter everywhere for water, na diffusion dey happen. The particles dey move from where dem plenty go where dem small.

questions.q: Which of the following factors will decrease the rate of simple diffusion across a respiratory surface?
o: Increasing the thickness of the respiratory membrane
Increasing the concentration gradient of the diffusing gas
Increasing the temperature within normal physiological limits
Increasing the surface area of the membrane
questions.e: According to Fick's law, the rate of diffusion is inversely proportional to the diffusion distance (thickness of the membrane). A thicker membrane increases the distance and slows down diffusion.
questions.p: If the wall wey gas dey pass thick too much, diffusion go slow down. Distance wey the gas go travel don increase be that.

questions.q: A student soaked dried-up moi-moi bean seeds in water overnight. The next morning, the seeds were swollen and the water level in the beaker had dropped. Which combination of cellular properties caused this observation?
questions.e: Dry seeds take up water initially through imbibition (absorption by hydrophilic colloids in the seed coat) followed by osmosis as water enters the cells across cell membranes.
questions.p: Dry bean seed dey first soak water through imbibition because of dry protein and starch, then osmosis follow join as water enter inside the cell membrane.

questions.q: During an experiment, a strip of raw yam with a pocket cut into it was filled with concentrated sugar solution and placed in a trough of clean water. After two hours, the level of liquid inside the yam pocket rose. This was because:
o: air pressure inside the pocket increased due to evaporation
water molecules moved from the trough into the yam pocket by osmosis
yam tissues actively pumped water upward
sugar molecules moved out of the yam pocket into the trough
questions.e: The concentrated sugar solution inside the yam pocket has a lower water potential than the clean water in the trough. Water therefore moves through the living yam cells into the pocket via osmosis.
questions.p: Sugar solution wey dey inside yam pocket get low water potential pass water wey dey outside. Na im make water dey enter yam pocket through osmosis, make liquid level rise.

questions.q: Which characteristic is shared by both simple diffusion and facilitated diffusion?
o: Both require carrier proteins embedded in the membrane
Both transport substances against a concentration gradient
Both are passive processes that do not require cellular energy
Both have a maximum transport rate when all channels are saturated
questions.e: Both simple and facilitated diffusion are passive transport mechanisms where molecules move down their concentration gradient using kinetic energy, requiring no metabolic ATP.
questions.p: Both simple and facilitated diffusion no dey use energy at all. The molecules dey move down their gradient by their own body movement.

questions.q: Why is active transport critical for the survival of freshwater unicellular organisms like Amoeba?
o: To allow the rapid entry of oxygen gas into the cytoplasm
To expel excess water that continuously enters the cell by osmosis
To absorb essential nutrients from the surrounding pond water which is very dilute
To prevent the contractile vacuole from storing too much salt
questions.e: Pond water is hypotonic to Amoeba, causing water to enter by osmosis (which is managed by the contractile vacuole, not active transport). However, essential mineral nutrients are scarce in the pond and must be actively pumped in.
questions.p: Pond water no get plenty nutrient, so Amoeba must use active transport to pack important salt and food enter body from that dilute water.

questions.q: Plasmolysed plant cells can be restored to their original turgid state if they are promptly placed in:
o: distilled water or a hypotonic solution
questions.e: Putting a plasmolysed cell into distilled water or a hypotonic solution creates a steep water potential gradient, causing water to re-enter the cell by osmosis and reverse plasmolysis (deplasmolysis).
questions.p: If you put plasmolysed plant inside ordinary water (distilled water), water go enter back through osmosis, and the cell go regain im strength and turgidity.

questions.q: Which of the following cellular structures acts as the equivalent of a selectively permeable barrier during osmosis in a plant cell?
questions.e: The plasma membrane surrounding the cytoplasm and the tonoplast surrounding the vacuole are the actual selectively permeable membranes governing osmosis in plant cells, whereas the cell wall is fully permeable.
questions.p: Na plasma membrane and tonoplast dey control wetin dey enter or commot during osmosis for plant cell. Cell wall na just ordinary fence wey allow anything pass.

questions.q: Which of the following mineral elements is required by green plants in trace amounts and functions mainly as an activator of respiratory enzymes?
questions.e: Manganese is a micronutrient (trace element) that plays a vital role in photolysis during photosynthesis and acts as an enzyme activator in respiration. Nitrogen, phosphorus, and calcium are macronutrients needed in large quantities.
questions.p: Na manganese be the trace element wey plant need small, but e dey help activate enzyme for respiration. Nitrogen, phosphorus, and calcium na macronutrients wey plant need plenty plenty.

questions.q: During the light-dependent stage of photosynthesis, which of the following events directly provides the electrons needed to replace those lost by chlorophyll a in Photosystem II?
questions.e: During the light-dependent stage, water molecules are split by light (photolysis) into oxygen, protons, and electrons. These released electrons replace the ones excited and lost by chlorophyll a in Photosystem II.
questions.p: When light shine for the light stage, water dey break down (photolysis) to give electron, proton, and oxygen. Na dis electron go replace the one wey chlorophyll a lose for Photosystem II.

questions.q: A student set up an experiment to test for photosynthesis using a potted plant kept in a dark room for 48 hours. What is the primary purpose of this initial dark treatment?
o: To kill all the chlorophyll pigments in the leaves
To activate the stomata to remain permanently open
To destarch the leaves by removing stored carbohydrates
To cause the leaves to absorb maximum carbon dioxide
questions.e: Placing a plant in the dark for 48 hours stops photosynthesis and causes it to use up its stored starch, successfully destarching the leaves so that subsequent starch tests accurately reflect current photosynthesis.
questions.p: To put plant inside dark room for 48 hours na to make sure say all the starch wey e don store before don finish. Na so the plant go destarch, abi make test result come pure.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly pairs a macro-nutrient in plants with its primary deficiency symptom?
o: Phosphorus and premature yellowing of terminal buds
Magnesium and interveinal chlorosis in older leaves
Iron and complete necrosis of the stem apex only
Potassium and stunted root growth with dark green leaves
questions.e: Magnesium is a central component of the chlorophyll molecule; its deficiency leads to a lack of chlorophyll synthesis, resulting in yellowing between the veins (interveinal chlorosis) starting in older leaves.
questions.p: Magnesium na key part of chlorophyll, so if e small, leaf go yellow between the veins, especially the old ones. Na why we call am interveinal chlorosis.

questions.q: Which of the following products of the light-dependent reaction are directly utilized in the light-independent reaction (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis?
questions.e: The light-dependent reaction produces ATP and NADPH, which are energy carriers and reducing agents respectively. These are then transferred to the stroma to power the fixation of carbon dioxide during the light-independent reaction.
questions.p: Light stage dey produce ATP and NADPH. Na these two energy package plant dey carry go dark stage (Calvin cycle) to help join carbon dioxide make food.

questions.q: In an experiment to investigate the effect of light intensity on the rate of photosynthesis in Elodea, the number of oxygen bubbles released per minute is counted. What does this liberated gas originate from?
o: The respiration occurring within the plant cells
The photolysis of water molecules during the light stage
The carbon dioxide taken in from the water
The breakdown of glucose stored in the stem
questions.e: The oxygen gas given off as a bubble by aquatic plants during photosynthesis is a by-product derived strictly from the splitting (photolysis) of water molecules, not from carbon dioxide.
questions.p: The oxygen bubble wey water plant dey release na from water wey break down during light stage, no be from carbon dioxide at all.

questions.q: Which of the following structural adaptations of a typical dicot leaf maximizes the absorption of carbon dioxide for photosynthesis?
o: A loosely arranged spongy mesophyll with large air spaces
A tightly packed palisade mesophyll containing many chloroplasts
A high concentration of xylem vessels on the lower surface
A thick waxy cuticle on the upper epidermis
questions.e: The spongy mesophyll layer contains numerous intercellular air spaces that allow carbon dioxide to diffuse rapidly and circulate freely to all photosynthetic cells inside the leaf.
questions.p: Spongy mesophyll get plenty space inside am like sponge. Na dis air space make carbon dioxide quick free move reach every cell for inside leaf.

questions.q: What is the primary function of potassium in plant nutrition?
o: Direct synthesis of amino acids and proteins
Formation of the cell wall structure
Activation of enzymes and regulation of stomatal opening
Acting as the core metallic ion in chlorophyll
questions.e: Potassium plays a crucial role in regulating the opening and closing of stomata by controlling guard cell turgor pressure, and it also acts as an activator for numerous plant enzymes.
questions.p: Potassium work na to help open and close mouth of leaf (stomata) and also make sure say many enzyme for plant body dey work well.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes autotrophic nutrition?
o: The ingestion of solid organic matter followed by internal digestion
The symbiotic association between fungi and the roots of higher plants
The absorption of already manufactured food from dead organic matter
The synthesis of complex organic food from simple inorganic substances using external energy
questions.e: Autotrophic nutrition is the mode of nutrition where organisms (like green plants) manufacture their own complex organic food from simple inorganic raw materials like carbon dioxide and water using sunlight.
questions.p: Autotrophic nutrition mean say organism like green plant fit make their own food by themselves using simple things like water, sun, and carbon dioxide.

questions.q: During the dark reaction (Calvin cycle) of photosynthesis, carbon dioxide is fixed by combining with a 5-carbon compound known as:
questions.e: In the stroma of the chloroplast, incoming carbon dioxide molecules are accepted and fixed by a 5-carbon sugar called Ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP) with the help of the enzyme RuBisCO.
questions.p: For the dark stage, one 5-carbon sugar wey we dey call Ribulose bisphosphate (RuBP) na im dey catch and join with carbon dioxide so journey to make food go start.

questions.q: Which of the following nutrient elements is a constituent of proteins and nucleic acids, and its deficiency causes general chlorosis in older leaves?
questions.e: Nitrogen is a fundamental building block of amino acids, proteins, and nucleic acids (DNA/RNA). A deficiency in nitrogen leads to stunted growth and general yellowing (chlorosis) of older leaves.
questions.p: Nitrogen na major component for protein and DNA. If nitrogen lack for soil, plant leaf go yellow all over, starting from the old ones.

questions.q: Which of the following classes of food is primarily responsible for tissue repair and growth in a growing teenager?
questions.e: Proteins are complex organic compounds made of amino acids, which are essential for building new cells and repairing worn-out tissues. Carbohydrates and fats mainly provide energy, while vitamins are for metabolic regulation.
questions.p: Na protein be the main food wey dey help body grow and repair damage tissue. Carbohydrate and fat na energy giver, while vitamin dey protect body from sickness.

questions.q: During digestion in the human mouth, which enzyme begins the breakdown of complex carbohydrates?
questions.e: Saliva contains the enzyme ptyalin (salivary amylase), which acts on cooked starch and breaks it down into maltose. Pepsin acts in the stomach, lipase digests fats, and trypsin acts in the small intestine.
questions.p: Na ptyalin, wey dem still dey call salivary amylase, dey start to break down starch inside mouth. Pepsin dey work for stomach, lipase dey digest fat, and trypsin dey work for small intestine.

questions.q: An omnivore eating a local meal of 'garri' and bitterleaf soup ingests a large amount of cellulose. What is the primary role of this cellulose in the human digestive system?
o: It acts as roughage to stimulate peristalsis and prevent constipation.
It is hydrolyzed into glucose for rapid energy release.
It binds to vitamins to enhance their absorption.
It is converted into amino acids in the colon.
questions.e: Human digestive tracts lack the enzyme cellulase needed to break down cellulose. Therefore, it passes through the alimentary canal largely undigested, serving as roughage that adds bulk to food and eases bowel movement.
questions.p: Human body no get enzyme wey fit break down cellulose. So, e just dey serve as roughage wey dey help poo pass well and stop constipation.

questions.q: A student suffering from severe bleeding gums and slow wound healing was diagnosed with a deficiency disease. Which dietary component was most likely lacking?
questions.e: Bleeding gums and delayed wound healing are classic symptoms of scurvy, which is caused by a deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid). Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness, while Vitamin D deficiency causes rickets.
questions.p: If person gum dey bleed and wound take time to heal, na lack of Vitamin C cause am, and the sickness na scurvy. Vitamin A deficiency dey cause night blindness.

questions.q: In the human stomach, hydrochloric acid creates an acidic medium. What is the most critical function of this acid regarding digestion?
o: It breaks down peptide bonds directly into individual amino acids.
It absorbs digested glucose into the gastric blood vessels.
It emulsifies large fat droplets into smaller micelles.
It activates the precursor pepsinogen into active pepsin.
questions.e: Hydrochloric acid in the stomach provides the low pH (acidic environment) required to convert inactive pepsinogen into active pepsin, which then digests proteins. It also kills ingested bacteria.
questions.p: Hydrochloric acid for stomach dey provide acidic environment wey dey change pepsinogen to active pepsin so wey e fit digest protein. E still dey kill bad germs wey enter body.

questions.q: Which of the following describes the correct match of an extracellular enzyme and its final digestion product?
o: Lipase and glycerol plus fatty acids
questions.e: Lipase is an enzyme that hydrolyzes lipids (fats and oils) into their end products, which are glycerol and fatty acids. Maltase breaks maltose into two glucose molecules, not galactose.
questions.p: Na only lipase break down fat and oil into glycerol and fatty acid. Maltase dey break maltose to glucose, no be galactose.

questions.q: Bile is produced by the liver and stored in the gall bladder before being released into the duodenum. What is its specific mechanical role in digestion?
o: Oxidation of excess glucose into glycogen
Emulsification of fats to increase surface area
questions.e: Bile salts do not contain enzymes; instead, they lower the surface tension of fats, breaking large fat globules into tiny droplets (emulsification). This greatly increases the surface area for lipase action.
questions.p: Bile no get enzyme, but e dey scatter big fat droplets into tiny tiny pieces so that lipase go easily digest am. E dey increase the surface area for work.

questions.q: Which structural modification in the human small intestine is primarily responsible for maximizing the absorption rate of digested food nutrients?
o: The secretion of thick mucus by goblet cells
The contraction of longitudinal muscles for churning
The presence of numerous circular folds, villi, and microvilli
The dense population of symbiotic bacteria
questions.e: The inner wall of the small intestine has folds, millions of finger-like projections called villi, and microscopic microvilli on epithelial cells. This enormous surface area ensures efficient absorption of end products of digestion.
questions.p: Small intestine get plenty folds, villi, and microvilli wey dey make the surface area very large. Na this plenty surface area dey help body absorb food nutrients sharp sharp.

questions.q: During a prolonged fasting period, a healthy human body draws upon its energy reserves stored in the liver and adipose tissues. In what primary form are these reserves stored?
questions.e: Animals store excess carbohydrates as glycogen in the liver and muscles, and excess fats as triglycerides in adipose tissues. Plants store energy as starch.
questions.p: Animal dey store extra sugar as glycogen for liver and muscle, and extra fat as triglycerides for fat tissue. Na plant dey store starch.

questions.q: Why is the hepatic portal vein uniquely important in the post-absorptive digestive process?
o: It transports absorbed glucose and amino acids straight from the villi to the liver.
It carries deoxygenated blood directly from the heart to the lungs.
It removes urea from kidney nephrons back to the stomach.
It channels emulsified fats directly into the lymphatic system.
questions.e: The hepatic portal vein connects the capillary beds of the alimentary canal directly to the liver. This allows the liver to regulate blood nutrient levels, store excess glucose as glycogen, and detoxify substances before general circulation.
questions.p: Hepatic portal vein na the road wey carry digested food like glucose and amino acid straight from small intestine go liver. Liver go come check am, store excess, and clean am before e enter general body blood.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs correctly links a deficiency disease to the missing mineral element?
questions.e: Iodine is a vital trace element needed by the thyroid gland to manufacture thyroxine hormone; its shortage causes swelling of the thyroid known as goitre. Iron is needed for haemoglobin to prevent anaemia, while calcium and vitamin D prevent rickets.
questions.p: If person lack iodine, thyroid gland go swell up, and the sickness na goitre. Iron deficiency dey cause anaemia, while calcium and vitamin D deficiency dey cause rickets.

questions.q: An enzyme was extracted from the human stomach and placed in a test tube with starch solution at 37 deg C and pH 7.2. After two hours, tests for reducing sugars were negative. What is the most accurate conclusion?
o: The temperature was too high for the enzyme to function.
The enzyme denatured due to lack of cofactors.
Pepsin acts specifically on proteins and requires an acidic pH, not starch and neutral pH.
Starch was successfully converted into fats and glycerol.
questions.e: Enzymes are substrate-specific. The stomach enzyme is pepsin, which digests proteins in an acidic medium, not starch. Furthermore, starch digestion is carried out by amylase in a neutral to slightly alkaline medium, explaining the negative sugar test.
questions.p: Stomach enzyme na pepsin, and e dey digest protein for acidic environment. E no get business with starch, and pH 7.2 no be the acidic place wey e need to work.

questions.q: Which of the following plant tissues is primarily responsible for the translocation of manufactured organic food from the leaves to other parts of the plant?
questions.e: The phloem tissue, specifically the sieve tube elements, is specialized for transporting manufactured food substances like sucrose from source to sink. Xylem is strictly for water and mineral salt transport.
questions.p: Na phloem tissue dey carry food wey leaf don make go round di whole plant. Xylem naim dey carry water and mineral salt, so na phloem be di correct answer.

questions.q: During the process of transpiration in flowering plants, water vapor is lost to the atmosphere mainly through which of the following structures?
questions.e: Stomata are microscopic pores located mostly on the lower epidermis of leaves through which the vast majority of transpiration occurs. Cuticular and lenticular transpiration account for only a very small fraction.
questions.p: Na through di stomata wey dey leaf epidermis most water vapor dey waka go outside during transpiration. Cuticle and lenticels dey do small small, but na stomata carry di major work.

questions.q: Which of the following components of mammalian blood is directly responsible for the defense of the body against invading pathogens by producing antibodies?
questions.e: Lymphocytes are a type of white blood cell that produce specific antibodies to neutralize foreign antigens and pathogens. Erythrocytes carry oxygen, and thrombocytes aid in blood clotting.
questions.p: Na lymphocytes be di type of white blood cell wey dey produce antibodies to fight bad germs and disease. Erythrocytes na oxygen carrier, while thrombocytes dey help blood clot.

questions.q: In the human heart, oxygenated blood from the lungs is first received by which of the following chambers?
questions.e: Oxygenated blood returns from the lungs via the pulmonary veins and enters the left atrium before being pumped into the left ventricle. The right side of the heart handles deoxygenated blood.
questions.p: When blood get oxygen from lungs, e dey enter di left atrium first before e go enter left ventricle. Di right side dey deal with blood wey no get oxygen.

questions.q: A student set up a potometer experiment to measure the rate of transpiration in a leafy shoot under ambient laboratory conditions. Which of the following environmental changes would cause the rate of bubble movement in the capillary tube to increase significantly?
o: Directing a stream of cool air from an electric fan towards the leaves
Spraying the leaves with cold water to keep them moist
Moving the entire setup into a dark cupboard for two hours
Placing a transparent polythene bag tightly over the leafy shoot
questions.e: An electric fan increases air movement around the leaves, which sweeps away water vapor and steepens the water vapor concentration gradient, thus increasing the transpiration rate. Covering the shoot or putting it in the dark reduces transpiration.
questions.p: If you put fan to blow di leaf, air go move fast and carry water vapor away quick quick, so di transpiration rate go increase. If you cover am or put am for dark, transpiration go reduce.

questions.q: Which of the following anatomical features is characteristic of xylem vessels that enables them to withstand high negative pressure without collapsing during water transport?
o: Thin cellulose walls with active chloroplasts
questions.e: Xylem vessels have thick walls impregnated with lignin, which provides mechanical strength and prevents them from collapsing under the tension created by the transpiration pull. They are non-living at maturity.
questions.p: Xylem vessel walls get lignin inside am, and na dis lignin dey give am strong strength make e no collapse when water dey pull with high tension. Dem no even get cytoplasm when dem mature.

questions.q: In a double circulation system such as that found in mammals, blood passes through the heart twice for every complete circuit of the body. What is the primary physiological advantage of this arrangement?
o: It maintains high blood pressure to distribute oxygen efficiently to active tissues
It allows mixing of oxygenated and deoxygenated blood to maintain constant body temperature
It reduces the overall metabolic rate and energy requirement of internal organs
It prevents blood from entering the lungs during intense physical exercise
questions.e: Double circulation separates oxygenated and deoxygenated blood and allows the heart to boost blood pressure after it passes through the lungs, ensuring rapid delivery of oxygen to systemic tissues. This supports high metabolic rates.
questions.p: Double circulation dey make sure say oxygenated blood no mix with deoxygenated one, and e dey help pump blood with high pressure go everywhere. Naim make mammals active and maintain high energy.

questions.q: An experiment was carried out where a complete ring of bark, including the phloem, was peeled off the stem of a woody plant (ringing experiment). After a few weeks, which of the following observations would most likely be made above the ring?
o: The roots would grow tremendously while the upper stem wilts
Water transport to the leaves would stop completely within twenty-four hours
Swelling would occur as organic food accumulates above the removed region
New phloem tissues would instantly regenerate to bypass the cut area
questions.e: Removing the phloem disrupts downward food transport, causing manufactured food to accumulate just above the ring, leading to swelling. Water transport continues initially because the xylem is untouched.
questions.p: When you remove bark wey contain phloem, food wey dey come down from leaf go stop at dat place and pack there, make di stem swell up. Xylem still dey work, so water go still dey go up for small time.

questions.q: During vigorous physical exercise, chemical changes occur in the blood flowing through active skeletal muscles. Which of the following conditions promotes a greater release of oxygen from hemoglobin to the exercising muscle tissues?
o: Decreased temperature and absence of lactic acid in the plasma
Increased blood pH and decreased carbon dioxide concentration
Lowered partial pressure of carbon dioxide and high oxygen saturation
Increased carbon dioxide concentration, lower pH, and higher temperature
questions.e: According to the Bohr effect, higher carbon dioxide levels, lower pH (acidity), and elevated temperatures in active tissues decrease hemoglobin's affinity for oxygen, causing it to unload oxygen more readily.
questions.p: As person dey exercise tire, carbon dioxide dey plenty, acid dey increase, and temperature dey high. Dis conditions dey make hemoglobin loose oxygen quick make muscle use am well (Bohr effect).

questions.q: In an experiment to study transpiration, two identical plant shoots were used: Shoot X had Vaseline applied to both leaf surfaces, while Shoot Y had Vaseline applied only to the lower leaf surface. Both shoots were placed in identical conditions. What would be the expected relative rates of water loss?
o: Shoot X would lose water much faster than Shoot Y
Shoot Y would lose water much faster than Shoot X
Both shoots would lose water at exactly the same rate
Shoot X would show no water loss at all, while Shoot Y would lose water rapidly
questions.e: Most dicot plants have a higher density of stomata on the lower epidermis than on the upper epidermis. Applying Vaseline to both surfaces blocks almost all transpiration in Shoot X, whereas Shoot Y still has open upper stomata and a cuticle, leading to significantly higher water loss in Shoot Y compared to X.
questions.p: Most plant leaf get plenty stomata for down pass up. If you put Vaseline for both up and down like Shoot X, transpiration go almost stop. But Shoot Y wey get Vaseline only for down go still lose plenty water through di up side.

questions.q: A patient with a rare genetic disorder experiences a complete blockage of the lymphatic vessels draining the lower limbs. Which of the following physiological consequences is most likely to occur in the affected limbs?
o: Severe dehydration of the tissue cells due to excessive water reabsorption
Complete cessation of arterial blood supply to the toes
Rapid increase in erythrocyte count within the tissue capillaries
Massive accumulation of interstitial fluid resulting in significant localized swelling
questions.e: Lymphatic vessels are responsible for returning excess tissue fluid (interstitial fluid) back to the blood circulatory system. When blocked, this fluid accumulates in the intercellular spaces, causing edema (swelling).
questions.p: Lymphatic vessels naim dey pack excess water from body tissue back to blood. If block happen there, water go pack for leg and cause heavy swelling wey dem dey call edema.

questions.q: During strenuous physical activity, a secondary school student running a 100-meter race at a sports meeting in Enugu may experience muscle cramps due to the accumulation of:
questions.e: When oxygen supply is insufficient during rigorous exercise, human skeletal muscles undergo anaerobic respiration, converting pyruvate into lactic acid which causes fatigue and cramps.
questions.p: When person run race tire body, oxygen no reach muscle well, so e go do anaerobic respiration wey dey produce lactic acid wey dey pain body.

questions.q: What is the net gain of ATP molecules produced strictly from the glycolysis stage of cellular respiration per glucose molecule?
questions.e: Glycolysis produces a gross total of 4 ATP molecules, but consumes 2 ATP in the process, resulting in a net yield of 2 ATP molecules before entering the Krebs cycle.
questions.p: Glycolysis dey produce 4 ATP for total, but e dey spend 2 ATP inside, con remain net gain of 2 ATP.

questions.q: Which of the following anatomical features is NOT a structural adaptation of the mammalian lung for efficient gaseous exchange?
o: Moist respiratory surface for dissolving gases
A thick, muscular outer pleural membrane
questions.e: The pleural membrane protects the lungs and aids breathing mechanics, but a thick outer wall would hinder diffusion. Lungs require a thin epithelium, moisture, and a rich blood supply for efficiency.
questions.p: Na thick pleural membrane no be wetin dey help gas pass easy; lungs need thin wall, water, and plenty blood vessel to work well.

questions.q: In plant aerobic respiration, the complete breakdown of glucose into carbon(IV) oxide and water yields a theoretical maximum of how many ATP molecules?
questions.e: Complete aerobic respiration involving glycolysis, the Krebs cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation typically yields a maximum of 38 ATP molecules per molecule of glucose oxidized in eukaryotes.
questions.p: Full aerobic respiration for plant glucose breakdown fit produce maximum of 38 ATP molecules when everything complete.

questions.q: Which of the following respiratory organs is correctly matched with its specific animal group?
questions.e: Young amphibian tadpoles live in water and respire primarily using external or internal gills, whereas adults typically use lungs and skin.
questions.p: Na small tadpole wey dey stay water dey use gill breath, unlike adult wey dey use lung and skin.

questions.q: Which of the following substances is a common intermediate product formed in both alcoholic fermentation and aerobic respiration before entering the mitochondrion?
questions.e: Glycolysis breaks glucose down into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. This pyruvate is then either channeled into the mitochondrion for aerobic respiration or converted into ethanol/lactic acid during fermentation.
questions.p: Glycolysis dey break glucose to pyruvate first for cytoplasm before e enter mitochondrion or go fermentation.

questions.q: Why does anaerobic respiration in yeast yield ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide, whereas in human muscle it yields lactic acid?
o: Different enzymes are present in the organisms to channel pyruvate differently
Yeast cells do not undergo glycolysis
questions.e: Both pathways start with pyruvate from glycolysis, but different organisms possess specific enzymes (such as pyruvate decarboxylase and alcohol dehydrogenase in yeast) that drive distinct terminal reactions.
questions.p: Both of them start with pyruvate, but different enzymes for yeast and human body dey make yeast produce alcohol while human produce lactic acid.

questions.q: What primary role does the diaphragm play during inspiration in a human being?
o: It vibrates to produce vocal sounds during breathing
It contracts and flattens to increase the volume of the thoracic cavity
It relaxes and arches upward to decrease thoracic volume
It secretes mucus to moisten incoming air
questions.e: During inspiration, the diaphragm muscle contracts, causing it to flatten. This increases the volume of the thoracic cavity and lowers air pressure, drawing air into the lungs.
questions.p: When person wan breathe in, diaphragm go contract and straight down, make chest space big so air go enter lung.

questions.q: During the Krebs cycle stage of aerobic respiration, which important event occurs inside the mitochondrial matrix?
o: Oxygen is used to form the first molecules of water
High energy electrons are stored permanently as starch
Acetyl-CoA is broken down completely, releasing carbon(IV) oxide and reducing coenzymes
Glucose is split directly into two pyruvate molecules
questions.e: In the mitochondrial matrix, acetyl-CoA enters the Krebs cycle where it is systematically oxidized, releasing carbon(IV) oxide and loading up electron carriers like NADH and FADH2.
questions.p: For mitochondrion matrix, acetyl-CoA dey break finish, come release carbon(IV) oxide and load up energy carrier like NADH.

questions.q: Which of the following structures in flowering plants primarily facilitates the excretion of excess water in the form of liquid droplets during humid mornings?
questions.e: Hydathodes are specialized pores located at the leaf margins of certain plants that are responsible for guttation, which is the exudation of liquid water. Unlike stomata that primarily handle transpiration in vapor form, hydathodes function when root pressure is high.
questions.p: Na hydathodes be the special pores for leaf edge wey dey help plant push out excess water as liquid droplet when moisture high too much, e dey happen through guttation.

questions.q: During a hot afternoon in Owerri, Mr. Chinedu noticed that his body temperature remained relatively stable despite heavy sweating. Which part of the human skin is primarily responsible for the cooling effect through perspiration?
questions.e: Sweat glands (sudoriferous glands) produce sweat, which absorbs latent heat of vaporization from the skin surface and evaporates, thereby cooling the body. This is a vital homeostatic mechanism for temperature regulation.
questions.p: Na sweat glands dey produce the sweat wey dey cool body down when e evaporate because e dey carry heat comot from skin surface.

questions.q: In the mammalian kidney, ultrafiltration of blood takes place under high hydrostatic pressure within which of the following regions?
questions.e: Blood enters the glomerulus, which is enclosed by the Bowman's capsule, under high pressure due to the difference in diameter between the afferent and efferent arterioles. This forces small molecules out of the blood into the Bowman's capsule during ultrafiltration.
questions.p: Na inside Bowman's capsule where glomerulus dey, ultrafiltration dey happen because blood pressure high well well to push small particles enter the capsule.

questions.q: Which of the following metabolic waste products is primarily excreted by freshwater fish due to its high solubility and abundance of water in their habitat?
questions.e: Ammonia is extremely toxic and requires large amounts of water for dilution and excretion. Freshwater fish live in environments with abundant water, allowing them to continuously excrete ammonia directly across their gills with minimal energy cost.
questions.p: Freshwater fish dey throway ammonia because water plenty for their body area, and since ammonia toxic well well, they need plenty water to wash am comot quick.

questions.q: A student examining a cross-section of a woody stem under a microscope observed small raised openings on the periderm used for gaseous exchange and waste excretion. These structures are called
questions.e: Lenticels are porous tissues consisting of cells with large intercellular spaces found in the periderm of woody stems and roots. They allow for the interchange of gases and excretion of waste gases between the internal tissues and the atmosphere.
questions.p: Na lenticels be those small openings on woody stem bark wey dey help plant breathe and pass out waste gas since mature back don block normal stomata.

questions.q: Which segment of the mammalian nephron is primarily adapted for the active reabsorption of glucose, amino acids, and essential ions back into the blood capillaries?
questions.e: The proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) has a specialized lining of microvilli that creates a large surface area for the active transport and reabsorption of vital nutrients like glucose, amino acids, and sodium ions from the glomerular filtrate back into the bloodstream.
questions.p: Na proximal convoluted tubule be the main place where body dey pack back all the good things like glucose and amino acid enter blood instead make waste carry them go.

questions.q: In the human skin, which of the following layers is majorly composed of dead, keratinized cells that provide a tough, water-resistant barrier against mechanical injury and pathogen invasion?
questions.e: The stratum corneum is the outermost layer of the epidermis, consisting of dead, flattened cells filled with keratin. This layer prevents excessive water loss and acts as a barrier against physical and microbial damage.
questions.p: Stratum corneum na the top layer of skin wey full of dead cells and keratin; e dey protect body like shield make water no dry up and make germs no enter.

questions.q: Desert mammals, such as the kangaroo rat, survive in arid conditions by producing highly concentrated urine. This adaptation is structurally linked to an exceptionally long
questions.e: A longer Loop of Henle creates a steeper concentration gradient in the renal medulla, allowing for greater reabsorption of water from the filtrate back into the blood. This enables desert animals to conserve maximum water and produce highly concentrated urine.
questions.p: Desert animal get very long Loop of Henle so that their kidney fit soak back plenty water from urine, make water no waste since water scarce for desert.

questions.q: When a person runs a 100-meter race at the National Stadium in Lagos, the lungs play a dual role in respiration and excretion by eliminating which of the following primary metabolic waste products?
questions.e: During cellular respiration, carbon dioxide and water are produced as by-products. The lungs excrete gaseous carbon dioxide and some water vapor from the body during exhalation.
questions.p: When person run race, body dey burn energy and produce carbon dioxide plus water vapor; na lungs come help blow these two waste gas comot through mouth and nose.

questions.q: Antidiuretic hormone (ADH) plays a crucial role in osmoregulation by specifically increasing the water permeability of which part of the nephron?
o: Loop of Henle and vasa recta
Proximal convoluted tubule and descending limb
Distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct
questions.e: ADH targets the walls of the distal convoluted tubule and the collecting duct, making them more permeable to water. This allows more water to be reabsorbed into the bloodstream when the body is dehydrated, resulting in concentrated urine.
questions.p: When body need water, brain go release ADH make e go open door for distal convoluted tubule and collecting duct so that water go pass back enter blood instead of going out as pee.

questions.q: Which of the following plant tissues is primarily responsible for providing mechanical support and tensile strength to young, growing organs through uneven thickening of its cell walls?
questions.e: Collenchyma cells have unevenly thickened primary walls, especially at the corners, which give them the flexibility and strength needed to support young growing stems and leaves without restricting their growth.
questions.p: Na collenchyma tissue dey give young plant stem and leaf support because their cell wall thick for corner, so e dey flexible and strong.

questions.q: During vigorous running on a field in Government College, Ibadan, a student experiences muscle fatigue and cramps. This condition is primarily caused by the accumulation of which of the following substances in the muscle cells?
questions.e: During strenuous exercise when oxygen supply is insufficient, skeletal muscles respire anaerobically, converting pyruvic acid into lactic acid, which accumulates and causes fatigue and cramps.
questions.p: When person run well well and oxygen no reach body, muscle dey breathe without oxygen and turn pyruvic acid to lactic acid. Na this acid wey pack inside muscle dey cause pain and cramp.

questions.q: In the human appendicular skeleton, the pectoral girdle consists of which of the following paired bones?
questions.e: The pectoral girdle, which attaches the upper limbs to the axial skeleton, is made up of the clavicle (collarbone) and the scapula (shoulder blade) on each side.
questions.p: Pectoral girdle na im dey join hand to body framework. E get clavicle (collarbone) and scapula (shoulder blade) for each side.

questions.q: Which of the following structural adaptations specifically enables sclerenchyma fibres to provide rigid mechanical support in mature plant organs?
o: Thin cellulose walls permeable to water
Presence of large vacuole for turgidity
Lignified secondary cell walls with pits
questions.e: Sclerenchyma fibres are dead cells at maturity with heavily lignified secondary cell walls that provide high tensile strength and rigidity, containing pits for intercellular communication before protoplast death.
questions.p: Sclerenchyma fibre na dead cell wey get thick wall wey dem born lignin inside am. Na this strong lignin wall dey give mature plant hard support.

questions.q: Which type of movable joint is found between the atlas and the axis vertebrae, allowing the head to move from side to side in a shaking motion?
questions.e: The pivot joint between the atlas and axis vertebrae permits rotational movement, allowing the head to turn from left to right as in shaking the head.
questions.p: Pivot joint dey between first and second neck bone (atlas and axis). Na im dey make person fit shake head from side to side.

questions.q: Turgidity in herbaceous plants provides mechanical support mainly due to the action of water pressing outward against which cellular component?
questions.e: Water entering plant cells creates turgor pressure that pushes the protoplast against the rigid cellulose cell wall, making herbaceous stems firm and upright.
questions.p: When water enter plant cell, e dey press body against the strong cellulose cell wall. Na this turgor pressure dey make soft plant stand erect.

questions.q: During muscle contraction according to the sliding filament theory, which of the following zones or bands shortens while the A-band remains constant in length?
questions.e: During contraction, actin filaments slide over myosin filaments, causing the I-bands and H-zones to shorten, whereas the length of the A-band (representing myosin) stays unchanged.
questions.p: When muscle dey contract, actin filament dey slide enter myosin. As dem dey do so, I-band and H-zone dey short, but the length of A-band no dey change at all.

questions.q: What is the primary function of synovial fluid found within a diarthrotic joint cavity in mammals?
o: To anchor ligaments firmly to the periosteum of bones
To transmit nerve impulses across the articulating bones
To produce red blood cells for the skeletal system
To lubricate the joint and reduce friction during movement
questions.e: Synovial fluid acts as a lubricant and shock absorber inside movable joints, reducing friction between the cartilage-covered ends of bones during movement.
questions.p: Synovial fluid work like oil inside movable joint. E dey reduce friction so sey bone no go dey scratch each other when person dey move.

questions.q: Which of the following structural parts of a mammalian vertebra serves as the attachment site for muscles and ribs?
questions.e: The neural spine and transverse processes projecting from the vertebra act as levers and secure attachment points for back muscles and ribs.
questions.p: Neural spine and transverse process na those bone parts wey dey hook muscle and rib for back.

questions.q: In a herbaceous dicotyledonous stem, vascular bundles are typically arranged in a ring. What is the primary mechanical advantage of this peripheral ring arrangement?
o: It provides maximum resistance against bending forces exerted by wind.
It stores excess glucose directly as starch in the centre.
It completely eliminates the need for collenchyma and sclerenchyma.
It allows rapid lateral transport of mineral salts without support.
questions.e: Arranging vascular bundles in a peripheral ring places the strongest tissues near the outer edges, acting like an I-beam to resist bending and breaking forces from wind.
questions.p: If vascular bundle arrange for ring for edge, e dey make the stem strong like pipe. Wind no go easily break am because the strong tissue dey outside.

questions.q: Which of the following structures in a tropical flowering plant is formed directly from the fertilized ovule?
questions.e: Following fertilization in flowering plants, the ovule develops into the seed while the ovary develops into the fruit. The testa is merely the protective coat of the seed derived from the integuments.
questions.p: After pollination and fertilization for flower plant, na ovule dey turn to seed, while ovary dey turn to fruit. Na why the seed na correct answer.

questions.q: Which adaptation is most characteristic of flowers pollinated by nocturnal insects such as moths?
o: Bright red petals with no scent
White petals with a strong sweet scent
Small dry pollen grains produced in massive quantities
Dull green petals with heavy nectar guides
questions.e: Nocturnal pollinators like moths rely on their sense of smell and need flowers that stand out in the dark. Therefore, moth-pollinated flowers typically feature white or pale petals and strong sweet fragrances.
questions.p: Moth and other night insect dey use their nose well well to find food. Na why flower wey dem dey pollinate dey get white color wey person fit see for dark and sweet smell.

questions.q: During human spermatogenesis, which of the following cells is directly produced by the first meiotic division?
questions.e: The primary spermatocyte undergoes the first meiotic division to produce two haploid secondary spermatocytes. Secondary spermatocytes then undergo the second meiotic division to form spermatids.
questions.p: Primary spermatocyte dey undergo the first meiosis division to give us secondary spermatocyte. Na after this one the second division go happen to form spermatid.

questions.q: What is the primary function of the corpus luteum in the human female reproductive cycle?
o: To stimulate the maturation of the Graafian follicle
To facilitate the actual process of fertilization in the oviduct
To secrete progesterone for maintaining the uterine lining
To trigger the sudden surge of luteinizing hormone
questions.e: The corpus luteum develops from the ruptured follicle after ovulation and secretes large amounts of progesterone. This hormone prepares and maintains the endometrium for potential implantation of a fertilized egg.
questions.p: After egg don commot for ovary, the place wey remain dey turn to corpus luteum. Him work na to produce progesterone to keep womb wall strong for pregnancy.

questions.q: Which extra-embryonic membrane in human development is directly responsible for forming the fetal contribution to the placenta?
questions.e: The chorion develops finger-like projections called chorionic villi that interface with the maternal endometrium to form the placenta. The amnion cushions the embryo, while the yolk sac produces early blood cells.
questions.p: Na chorion membrane dey bring out those small finger-like parts wey dey join with mother body to form placenta. E dey help baby chop and breath.

questions.q: During wind pollination in grasses, which floral characteristic is typically absent?
questions.e: Wind-pollinated flowers do not need to attract animals, so they lack showy petals, nectar, and sweet scents. Instead, they produce large amounts of light pollen and have feathery stigmas to catch blowing pollen.
questions.p: Wind pollination flower no need fine petal or sweet smell because dem no dey wait for insect. Na wind dey carry their pollen, so dem no get scent at all.

questions.q: Which hormone is directly responsible for stimulating milk ejection from the mammary glands during lactation in humans?
questions.e: Oxytocin stimulates the contraction of myoepithelial cells surrounding the alveoli of the mammary glands, resulting in milk ejection. Prolactin, by contrast, is responsible for the actual synthesis and production of milk.
questions.p: Make una no confuse prolactin with oxytocin o. Prolactin dey make breast produce milk, but na oxytocin dey push the milk come out when baby dey suck.

questions.q: What type of fruit is a pineapple, considering it develops from the ovaries of multiple flowers fused together on an inflorescence?
questions.e: A multiple fruit, or syncarp, develops from the ovaries of an entire inflorescence where individual flowers fuse together, typical of pineapples and figs. An aggregate fruit comes from a single flower with multiple separate carpels.
questions.p: Pineapple na multiple fruit because na plenty flowers wey jam together for one stem come join body form one big fruit. E different from aggregate fruit wey come from only one flower.

questions.q: Where in the human female reproductive tract does fertilization of the secondary oocyte typically take place?
questions.e: Fertilization normally occurs in the ampulla of the Fallopian tube (oviduct) shortly after the secondary oocyte is released from the ovary. The fertilized zygote then travels down to the uterus for implantation.
questions.p: Fertilization of egg and sperm usually happen inside the Fallopian tube. Na after sperm meet egg there, the baby go come travel go enter womb.

questions.q: In seed germination, what is the primary role of the enzyme amylase mobilized within the endosperm?
o: To break down complex starches into soluble maltose sugars
To oxidize lipids into fatty acids for cellular respiration
To hydrolyze stored proteins into transportable amino acids
To soften the seed coat for easy radicle emergence
questions.e: During germination, gibberellin hormone stimulates the production of alpha-amylase in the aleurone layer, which converts stored starch into maltose. This provides the growing embryo with necessary soluble sugars for energy.
questions.p: When seed start to germinate, amylase enzyme go break down starch inside seed turn am to sugar. Na this sugar the small plant dey use chop energy to grow.

questions.q: Which of the following hormones is primarily responsible for apical dominance and cell elongation in the shoot of a flowering plant?
questions.e: Auxins, specifically indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), are produced in the shoot apex and promote cell elongation while inhibiting the growth of lateral buds, a phenomenon known as apical dominance.
questions.p: Na Auxin dey cause shoot make e grow long and e dey stop side branches make dem no quick grow, wey dem dey call apical dominance.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes primary growth in herbaceous dicotyledonous plants?
o: Increase in root diameter through secondary xylem formation
Increase in leaf surface area through intercalary meristem activity
Increase in stem length through apical meristem activity
Increase in stem girth through cork cambium activity
questions.e: Primary growth involves the increase in length of roots and shoots, which is brought about by the division of cells in the apical meristems located at the tips.
questions.p: Primary growth naim make root and stem dey long up and down, and na apical meristem for tip dey do the work.

questions.q: An experiment was set up to test seed germination. Dry bean seeds were placed in a flask with dry cotton wool, kept at room temperature, and tightly corked. After one week, no germination occurred. What is the primary missing factor for germination in this setup?
questions.e: Water is essential for seed germination to soften the testa, activate enzymes, and hydrate the tissues for metabolic activities. Dry cotton wool indicates an absence of moisture.
questions.p: Water na the number one thing wey seed need to soft body and wake up enzymes inside am. Dry cotton wool mean say water no dey at all.

questions.q: Which of the following changes typically occurs in the dry mass of a germinating seed before the emergence of the first green foliage leaves?
o: Initial decrease followed by an increase
questions.e: Before leaves emerge and photosynthesis begins, the seed relies entirely on stored food reserves. Respiration breaks down these stored reserves, releasing carbon dioxide and causing a net loss in dry mass.
questions.p: Before green leaf come out to start making food, the seed dey use the food wey e don store inside. As respiration dey happen, the dry weight go dey reduce.

questions.q: In an experiment on plant growth, maize seedlings were grown in total darkness for two weeks. The seedlings appeared tall, slender, and yellowish-white. This condition is known as:
questions.e: Etiolation is the abnormal morphological adaptation of plants grown in the absence of light, characterized by long weak stems, small unexpanded leaves, and a lack of chlorophyll (yellow color).
questions.p: Etiolation na wetin happen when plant grow for dark place; e go long pass normal, weak, and yellow because chlorophyll no form.

questions.q: Which of the following plant hormones delays leaf senescence and is commonly used in agriculture to keep vegetables green after harvest?
questions.e: Cytokinins promote cell division and delay aging (senescence) in plant leaves by mobilizing nutrients to the treated areas, keeping harvested vegetables fresh and green.
questions.p: Cytokinin na hormone wey dey help plant make e no quick old. Naim farmers dey use keep vegetable green after dem harvest am.

questions.q: Sigmoidal growth curves are characteristic of many multicellular organisms. Which phase of a sigmoid curve represents the period of exponential or logarithmic growth?
questions.e: The log (logarithmic or exponential) phase is the period where the rate of growth is rapid and accelerates as the number of dividing cells multiplies quickly.
questions.p: Log phase na that time when growth dey fast well well because plenty cells dey divide at the same time.

questions.q: Which of the following structural adaptations is crucial for gaseous exchange in a germinating hypogeal seed buried deep in damp soil?
o: General surface of the testa and micropyle
questions.e: For a buried seed undergoing aerobic respiration, oxygen enters and carbon dioxide leaves through the porous testa and specifically the micropyle before true leaves and stomata develop.
questions.p: For seed wey inside soil, oxygen dey enter and waste gas dey commot through small holes for the seed coat (testa) and the micropyle.

questions.q: Which plant growth regulator is a gas at room temperature and is heavily involved in fruit ripening and flower fading?
questions.e: Ethylene is a unique plant hormone that exists as a gas. It stimulates the conversion of starches to sugars, softening fruits and promoting ripening.
questions.p: Ethylene na the only plant hormone wey be gas. Naim dey make fruit ripe quick and soft.

questions.q: What is the primary role of the cotyledon in a non-endospermic dicot seed like a cowpea during early germination?
o: To protect the radicle from mechanical injury
To anchor the seed firmly into the soil
To store and supply food reserves to the embryo
questions.e: In non-endospermic (exalbuminous) seeds, food is stored directly in the thick cotyledons to nourish the developing embryonic axis (radicle and plumule) during germination.
questions.p: For cowpea (beans), the big seed leaves (cotyledon) na there food dey stored to feed small baby plant before e fit start to make him own food.

questions.q: A researcher treated dormant lettuce seeds with a specific plant hormone and exposed them to red light to break dormancy and induce germination. Which hormone was most likely applied?
questions.e: Gibberellins can substitute for light requirements in many photoblastic seeds, stimulating hydrolytic enzymes like alpha-amylase to break dormancy and trigger germination.
questions.p: Gibberellin hormone fit help break seed sleep (dormancy) even without light, by telling enzyme like amylase make e start work.

questions.q: Which of the following components of the human nervous system is directly responsible for controlling voluntary skeletal muscle movements during a 100-meter race at a inter-house sports competition?
questions.e: The somatic nervous system transmits signals from the central nervous system to skeletal muscles, enabling conscious control over voluntary movements like running. The autonomic system handles involuntary internal activities.
questions.p: Na somatic nervous system dey carry message from brain go body muscle make person fit run well during inter-house sports. Di autonomic system na im dey control things wey you no dey command like your heartbeat.

questions.q: In a simple reflex arc, the structural pathway followed by nerve impulses from the receptor organ to the effector organ is correctly represented as:
o: Sensory neurone -> Interneurone -> Motor neurone -> Effector
Motor neurone -> Interneurone -> Sensory neurone -> Effector
Effector -> Sensory neurone -> Interneurone -> Motor neurone
Receptor -> Motor neurone -> Sensory neurone -> Effector
questions.e: A reflex arc starts at the receptor, passes via a sensory neurone to the spinal cord (via an interneurone), and then travels along a motor neurone to the effector to produce a rapid response.
questions.p: Reflex arc dey start from where pain touch receptor, carry go sensory neurone, pass connector neurone for spinal cord, then use motor neurone reach effector like muscle make you withdraw your hand sharp-sharp.

questions.q: A student accidentally touches a hot stove at Mama Ngozi's food canteen and quickly withdraws her hand before feeling conscious pain. This rapid, automatic response is coordinated primarily by the:
questions.e: Reflex actions like withdrawing from a hot surface are processed rapidly by the spinal cord to protect the body from harm, bypassing the brain initially to save time.
questions.p: When person touch hot stove, na spinal cord dey quick direct di hand withdrawal before di brain even know wetin happen, just to protect di body from damage.

questions.q: During bright sunlight in an open field at Ahmadu Bello University, which of the following coordinated changes occurs within the human eye?
o: Suspensory ligaments tighten, causing the lens to become thicker
Circular muscles of the iris contract, causing the pupil to constrict
Radial muscles of the iris contract, causing the pupil to dilate
Ciliary muscles relax, causing the lens to become flatter
questions.e: In bright light, the circular muscles of the iris contract while radial muscles relax, making the pupil smaller (constrict) to reduce light entering the eye and protect the retina.
questions.p: If sun too shine, di circular muscle for eye iris dey tight/contract make pupil small so light no go pass too much enter retina and spoil am.

questions.q: Which specific part of the human brain is primarily responsible for maintaining body balance, posture, and smooth coordination of skeletal muscle movements during a traditional Bata dance?
questions.e: The cerebellum is the region of the hindbrain dedicated to coordinating balance, posture, and fine motor skills required during complex physical activities.
questions.p: Na cerebellum be di part of brain wey dey make sure say person balance well, maintain posture, and dance Bata without falling down anyhow.

questions.q: A patient is diagnosed with a condition where light rays from a distant object focus in front of the retina. To correct this visual defect, the ophthalmologist will prescribe lenses that are:
questions.e: Focusing in front of the retina describes myopia (short-sightedness). Diverging concave lenses are used to spread out incoming light rays so they focus directly on the retina.
questions.p: If person get short-sightedness (myopia), light dey focus before retina. Na concave lens dem go prescribe make e help spread di light rays make dem land direct on top retina.

questions.q: Which of the following cells in the human retina are responsible for high-acuity color vision under bright light conditions?
questions.e: Cone cells contain iodopsin pigments and function best in bright light to provide sharp vision and distinguish different colors, unlike rod cells which work in dim light.
questions.p: Na cone cells dey help person see different colors and sharp pictures when light bright well well. Rod cells na only for dim light dem dey work.

questions.q: An action potential is propagated along an axon. Which ionic movement across the nerve cell membrane causes immediate depolarization during the rising phase of the action potential?
questions.e: Depolarization occurs when voltage-gated sodium channels open, causing a rapid influx of positively charged sodium ions into the axoplasm, reversing the membrane potential.
questions.p: When nerve impulse dey travel, sodium ions (Na+) go rush enter inside di axon sharp-sharp. Na that rapid influx cause depolarization wey be say inside di nerve turn positive.

questions.q: Chemical transmission across a synapse from a presynaptic neurone to a postsynaptic neurone is achieved by the release of substances known as:
questions.e: Neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine are stored in vesicles and released into the synaptic cleft to chemically bridge the gap and trigger an impulse in the next neurone.
questions.p: Na neurotransmitters like acetylcholine chemicals dey cross di small gap (synapse) from one nerve cell reach another nerve cell make message continue to flow.

questions.q: Accommodation of the human eye for focusing on a close object, such as reading a text message on a smartphone, involves:
o: Flattening of the lens and dilation of the pupil
Relaxation of ciliary muscles and tightening of suspensory ligaments
