Active transport results in a net loss of water from the cell, while diffusion results in a net gain of water
Active transport requires a carrier protein, while diffusion never involves any membrane protein
Active transport occurs only in plant cells, while diffusion occurs only in animal cells
questions.e: Active transport uses metabolic energy (ATP) to move substances from a region of lower concentration to a region of higher concentration, against the gradient. Diffusion, on the other hand, is a passive process that moves substances down their concentration gradient.
questions.p: Active transport dey use energy like ATP to move things against concentration gradient. Diffusion na passive process wey no dey need energy, e dey move things from where dem plenty go where dem small.

questions.q: A student set up three identical pieces of fresh potato tissue of equal mass and placed them separately in sugar solutions of 0.0 mol/dm3, 0.5 mol/dm3 and 1.0 mol/dm3 for one hour. The masses of the tissues were measured before and after. Which of the following results would be expected if the cell sap of the potato has a concentration close to 0.5 mol/dm3?
o: All three tissues gain equal amounts of mass regardless of the sugar concentration
The tissue in 1.0 mol/dm3 gains the most mass because it has the highest solute concentration
The tissue in 0.0 mol/dm3 gains the most mass, the tissue in 0.5 mol/dm3 shows almost no change, and the tissue in 1.0 mol/dm3 loses mass
The tissue in 0.0 mol/dm3 loses the most mass while the tissue in 1.0 mol/dm3 gains the most mass
questions.e: Water moves into the potato cells from the more dilute 0.0 mol/dm3 solution, causing a mass gain, while water moves out into the more concentrated 1.0 mol/dm3 solution, causing a mass loss. At 0.5 mol/dm3, since the cell sap concentration matches the external solution, there is little or no net movement of water, so mass stays roughly the same.
questions.p: Water dey enter the potato for 0.0 mol/dm3 solution, so e go gain weight. For 1.0 mol/dm3, water go comot from the potato, so e go lose weight. For 0.5 mol/dm3, nothing go change because the concentration dey equal.

questions.q: The root hair cells of a maize plant absorb mineral ions such as nitrate from the soil even when the soil solution has a lower concentration of these ions than the cell sap. This process mainly depends on which of the following cell structures or features?
o: Large central vacuole for water storage
Mitochondria supplying ATP for carrier proteins in the cell membrane
Cellulose cell wall providing mechanical support
questions.e: Absorbing ions against their concentration gradient is active transport, which requires energy in the form of ATP. Root hair cells have many mitochondria that produce this ATP, which powers the carrier proteins moving the ions into the cell.
questions.p: To carry ions against concentration gradient, the cell need energy from ATP. Mitochondria for the root hair cells dey produce this ATP to help the carrier proteins move the ions inside.

questions.q: A thin strip of fresh carrot tissue weighing 5.0 g was placed in a salt solution for one hour. After the experiment, the strip weighed 4.2 g. What was the approximate percentage change in mass of the carrot strip?
questions.e: The mass lost is 5.0 g minus 4.2 g, which equals 0.8 g. Dividing 0.8 g by the original mass of 5.0 g and multiplying by 100 gives a 16% decrease in mass.
questions.p: The weight loss na 0.8 g. If you divide 0.8 g by the original 5.0 g and multiply by 100, you go get 16% decrease.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a fully plasmolysed plant cell appears to have a gap between the cell wall and the cell membrane when viewed under a microscope?
o: The cell membrane becomes more permeable and expands outward into the space
The cell membrane and cytoplasm shrink away from the rigid cell wall as water leaves the cell by osmosis
Active transport pumps the cell membrane away from the cell wall
The cell wall dissolves in the hypertonic solution, creating a visible space
questions.e: When a plant cell is placed in a hypertonic (concentrated) solution, water leaves the cell sap by osmosis. The cell membrane and cytoplasm shrink inward, but the rigid cellulose cell wall keeps its original shape, creating a visible gap between them.
questions.p: When plant cell dey inside concentrated solution, water go comot from the cell. The cell membrane and cytoplasm go shrink, but the cell wall go stay firm, so space go show between dem.

questions.q: Four beakers, each containing 100 cm3 of solution, were set up with a model cell made of visking tubing containing starch solution suspended in each. Beaker 1 contains distilled water, beaker 2 contains a dilute salt solution, beaker 3 contains a solution with the same concentration as the cell contents, and beaker 4 contains a very concentrated salt solution. In which beaker would the model cell most likely burst if its visking tubing were as weak as a red blood cell membrane?
questions.e: Distilled water has the highest water potential and no solutes, so water enters the model cell by osmosis fastest and in the greatest amount, creating the highest internal pressure. If the membrane is weak like a red blood cell membrane, this beaker is most likely to cause bursting, since the other beakers have progressively less or no net water entry.
questions.p: Distilled water get the highest water potential, so water go rush enter the bag pass other ones. If the membrane weak, the pressure go make the bag burst quick quick.

questions.q: A student used a variegated leaf (part green, part white) for a starch test experiment. The leaf was destarched, then exposed to light for several hours before testing with iodine solution. Which part of the leaf turned blue-black?
o: Only the white part, because it lacks chlorophyll
Only the green part, because it contains chlorophyll needed for photosynthesis
Both the green and white parts equally
Neither part, because the leaf was destarched
questions.e: Only parts of the leaf with chlorophyll can carry out photosynthesis and make starch. The white part has no chlorophyll, so it does not turn blue-black with iodine.
questions.p: Na only green part wey get chlorophyll go fit do photosynthesis and make starch. As the white part no get chlorophyll, iodine no go turn am blue-black.

questions.q: A bean seedling was grown in a complete culture solution containing all essential mineral elements except phosphorus. Which of the following symptoms would most likely be observed in the seedling?
o: Stunted growth with purplish discolouration of leaves and poor root development
Scorching of leaf margins with brittle stems
Yellowing of young leaves only, while old leaves stay green
Wilting of leaves due to excess water uptake
questions.e: Phosphorus is needed for root growth, energy transfer and healthy cell division. Its deficiency causes stunted growth, poor roots and a purplish tint on leaves due to pigment build-up.
questions.p: Phosphorus dey help root grow well and make energy. If e no dey, the plant go get stunted growth, bad root, and purple color for leaf.

questions.q: In an experiment, a green plant was enclosed in a transparent bell jar with a dish of lime water, under bright light for several hours. At the end of the experiment, the lime water remained clear. What is the best explanation for this observation?
o: The plant was respiring faster than it was photosynthesising
Lime water only turns milky in the absence of light
The plant was not photosynthesising and so was not releasing carbon dioxide
The rate of carbon dioxide uptake by photosynthesis exceeded the rate of carbon dioxide release by respiration
questions.e: In bright light, photosynthesis uses up carbon dioxide faster than respiration produces it, so there is a net removal of carbon dioxide from the air in the jar. With little or no carbon dioxide left, the lime water stays clear.
questions.p: For bright light, photosynthesis dey take carbon dioxide quick pass how respiration dey produce am. Because carbon dioxide no plenty for jar again, lime water go remain clear.

questions.q: A farmer in Benue applies a fertiliser rich in nitrogen to his yam farm. What is the main expected benefit of this nutrient to the yam plants?
o: Faster ripening of tubers before harvest
Formation of strong woody stems and thick cell walls
Promotion of vigorous vegetative growth through protein and chlorophyll synthesis
Improved resistance to fungal diseases only
questions.e: Nitrogen is a major component of amino acids, proteins and chlorophyll. Plenty of nitrogen therefore promotes leafy, vegetative growth.
questions.p: Nitrogen dey help plant make protein and chlorophyll wey e need. E dey make the leaves grow well and green.

questions.q: During an investigation, a scientist measured the rate of photosynthesis of a water plant at different temperatures while light intensity and carbon dioxide concentration were kept constant and non-limiting. The rate increased steadily up to 35°C, then dropped sharply at 45°C. What is the most likely explanation for the drop at 45°C?
o: The plant stopped absorbing water through its roots
Carbon dioxide became completely unavailable to the plant
Light intensity automatically reduced at higher temperature
Enzymes involved in photosynthesis became denatured by the high temperature
questions.e: Photosynthesis depends on enzymes, which work best within an optimum temperature range. Beyond this range, high temperature denatures the enzymes, causing the rate to fall sharply.
questions.p: High temperature dey spoil the enzymes wey dey help do photosynthesis. Once temperature reach 45°C, the enzymes go denature and the rate go drop sharply.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly describes the main role of magnesium in plant nutrition?
o: It is the central atom of the chlorophyll molecule, essential for light absorption
It activates enzymes involved in protein synthesis only
It is a major component of plant cell membranes as phospholipids
It strengthens cell walls by forming calcium-pectate compounds
questions.e: Magnesium forms the central atom of the chlorophyll molecule. Without enough magnesium, plants cannot make sufficient chlorophyll, leading to poor photosynthesis.
questions.p: Magnesium na the main center atom inside chlorophyll molecule. Without am, plant no go fit make chlorophyll to absorb light.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why plants grown in soils deficient in potassium often show poor resistance to drought and disease?
o: Potassium combines directly with carbon dioxide during the dark reaction
Potassium helps regulate stomatal opening and closing and activates many enzymes involved in plant metabolism
Potassium is required for forming the waxy cuticle that prevents water loss
Potassium is the main structural component of the cell wall
questions.e: Potassium controls the opening and closing of stomata by regulating guard cell turgor, and it activates enzymes needed for normal metabolism. A deficiency weakens these processes, making plants less able to cope with drought or disease.
questions.p: Potassium dey control how stomata dey open and close, and e dey help plant enzymes work well. If potassium no dey, plant body go weak for drought and sickness.

questions.q: Adaeze chews a piece of boiled yam for a long time and notices it begins to taste sweet. Which enzyme present in her saliva is responsible for this change?
questions.e: Saliva contains ptyalin, which breaks down starch into maltose, giving the sweet taste. Pepsin, trypsin and lipase act on proteins and fats, not starch.
questions.p: Saliva get ptyalin inside am wey dey break down starch to maltose, na hin make yam dey sweet for mouth. Pepsin, trypsin and lipase dey work for protein and fat, no be starch.

questions.q: A food scientist tests three solutions, X, Y and Z, with Sudan III stain. Solution X forms a scarlet-red layer, while Y and Z show no colour change. Which food class is most likely present in solution X?
questions.e: Sudan III stain turns red or forms a red layer in the presence of lipids. It does not react this way with proteins, sugars or starch.
questions.p: Sudan III stain dey turn red or form red layer if lipid dey present. E no dey react like dat with protein, sugar or starch.

questions.q: In the human digestive system, which pair of organs both secrete enzymes that digest proteins into smaller peptides?
questions.e: The stomach secretes pepsin and the pancreas secretes trypsin, both of which break down proteins into peptides. The liver and gall bladder produce and store bile, which has no enzymes, and the mouth has no protein-digesting enzyme.
questions.p: Stomach dey bring out pepsin and pancreas dey bring out trypsin, and both of them dey break protein down to peptide. Liver and gall bladder dey make and store bile wey no get enzyme, and mouth no get protein enzyme.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly matches a digestive enzyme with the site where it is secreted?
o: Pepsin - secreted by the salivary glands
Lipase - secreted by the stomach only
Amylase - secreted by the gall bladder
questions.e: Trypsin is produced by the pancreas and released into the duodenum to digest proteins. Pepsin comes from the stomach, amylase from the salivary glands and pancreas, and the gall bladder stores bile, not enzymes.
questions.p: Na pancreas dey produce trypsin and release am go duodenum to digest protein. Pepsin dey come from stomach, amylase dey come from salivary gland and pancreas, while gall bladder na to store bile, no be enzyme.

questions.q: A boy eats a meal containing boiled egg white, rice and vegetable oil. As the food passes through his digestive tract, which sequence correctly shows where protein digestion begins and is completed?
o: Begins in the stomach with pepsin, completed in the small intestine with trypsin and peptidases
Begins in the stomach with lipase, completed in the pancreas
Begins in the small intestine with bile, completed in the stomach with pepsin
Begins in the mouth with ptyalin, completed in the stomach
questions.e: Protein digestion starts in the stomach when pepsin breaks proteins into peptides, and is completed in the small intestine by pancreatic trypsin and intestinal peptidases, which produce amino acids. Ptyalin and lipase act on carbohydrates and fats, not proteins.
questions.p: Protein digestion dey start for stomach when pepsin break protein to peptide, and e dey finish for small intestine through pancreatic trypsin and peptidases. Ptyalin and lipase dey work for carbohydrate and fat, no be protein.

questions.q: A researcher removes the pancreas from an experimental animal but keeps the stomach, liver and small intestine functioning normally. Which process would be most severely affected as a result?
o: Absorption of digested food through the villi
Digestion of proteins and fats in the small intestine due to loss of trypsin and lipase
Emulsification of fats by bile in the duodenum
Breakdown of starch by salivary amylase in the mouth
questions.e: The pancreas supplies trypsin for protein digestion and lipase for fat digestion into the small intestine, so removing it would severely affect these processes. Salivary amylase, bile emulsification and villi absorption do not directly depend on the pancreas.
questions.p: Pancreas dey supply trypsin for protein digestion and lipase for fat digestion inside small intestine, so to remove am go affect these process well well. Salivary amylase, bile and villi absorption no depend directly on pancreas.

questions.q: Which pair of food classes are both classified as 'energy-giving foods' but differ in that one yields roughly twice as much energy per gram as the other?
questions.e: Carbohydrates and fats are both energy-giving food classes, but fats release about twice the energy per gram that carbohydrates do. Proteins are mainly body-building, while vitamins and minerals are protective, not energy sources.
questions.p: Carbohydrates and fats na energy-giving food, but fat dey give twice the energy wey carbohydrate dey give per gram. Protein na body-building food, while vitamins and minerals dey protect body.

questions.q: A Nigerian dietitian plans a weaning diet for a 2-year-old child recovering from malnutrition. Which combination of local foods would best supply first-class (complete) protein to support rapid growth?
o: Plantain and vegetable soup without meat
questions.e: Eggs, fish and milk are animal sources that contain all the essential amino acids in the right proportions, making them first-class proteins. Yam, garri and plantain are mainly carbohydrate sources and lack a full set of essential amino acids.
questions.p: Egs, fish and milk na animal protein wey get all the essential amino acids wey body need to grow well, na first-class protein be that. Yam, garri and plantain na carbohydrate and dem no get complete amino acids.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why enzymes are described as biological catalysts during digestion?
o: They change the chemical nature of food into a completely different class of nutrient
They are used up completely after digesting one molecule of food
They supply additional energy that is absorbed along with digested food
They increase the rate of breakdown of food substances without being permanently changed or used up
questions.e: Enzymes speed up digestive reactions by lowering activation energy, and they come out of the reaction chemically unchanged so they can be reused repeatedly. They do not get used up, nor do they convert one food class into another class.
questions.p: Enzyme dey help food break down quick-quick without make dem spoil or finish for body. Dem no dey turn to another food class, and dem dey ready to work again.

questions.q: An investigation was carried out to study the effect of temperature on the activity of a certain digestive enzyme using starch as substrate. Test tubes were incubated at 10°C, 20°C, 37°C, 50°C and 70°C, and the time taken for the starch to disappear (tested with iodine) was recorded. The enzyme worked fastest at 37°C, slower at 20°C and 50°C, and showed almost no activity at 10°C and 70°C. What is the best explanation for the complete loss of activity at 70°C?
o: The enzyme molecules moved too slowly to collide with the substrate
The enzyme was converted into a different type of protein at high temperature
The high temperature denatured the enzyme by permanently altering its active site
The substrate became too concentrated for the enzyme to act on
questions.e: At 70°C the heat energy disrupts the bonds holding the enzyme's three-dimensional shape, permanently changing the active site so the substrate can no longer bind; this is called denaturation. Slow molecular movement explains low activity at 10°C, not the loss of activity at high temperature.
questions.p: High temperature like 70°C dey spoil the shape of enzyme so the active site go scatter, wey we dey call denaturation. When this happen, food no fit bind with am again.

questions.q: A student set up an experiment with three test tubes each containing 5 ml of starch solution and 1 ml of saliva, buffered at pH 3, pH 7 and pH 9 respectively, then kept all three in a water bath at 37°C. After 10 minutes, iodine test showed that only the tube at pH 7 gave a brown colour (no starch left), while the other two tubes turned blue-black. What is the most reasonable conclusion from this result?
o: Temperature, not pH, was responsible for the differences observed
Salivary amylase works best in a neutral pH and is less active in acidic or alkaline conditions
Salivary amylase works best in strongly acidic conditions
The iodine solution reacted differently with each buffer used
questions.e: Since only the neutral pH 7 tube showed complete starch digestion while the acidic and alkaline tubes still contained undigested starch, the enzyme must work optimally around neutral pH. Temperature was kept constant at 37°C in all tubes, so it cannot explain the difference.
questions.p: Na only for neutral pH 7 the salivary amylase chop finish the starch, show say acidic and alkaline environment no good for am. Temperature con remain the same for all tubes.

questions.q: In an experiment, two identical pieces of visking (dialysis) tubing, A and B, were each filled with a mixture of starch solution and amylase, tied at both ends, and suspended in separate beakers of water. Tube A was left at room temperature while tube B was first boiled for 5 minutes before being set up the same way. After 30 minutes, the water surrounding tube A gave a positive Benedict's test, but the water surrounding tube B remained negative. What does this result demonstrate?
o: Visking tubing is impermeable to all molecules regardless of size
Boiling destroyed the amylase in tube B, so starch could not be digested into sugar that would diffuse out
Starch molecules are small enough to diffuse through visking tubing in both tubes
Benedict's test only works on starch, not on reducing sugars
questions.e: Boiling denatured the amylase in tube B, so the starch remained undigested and, being a large molecule, could not pass through the visking tubing to give a positive Benedict's test outside. In tube A the active amylase digested starch into small reducing sugar molecules that diffused out and were detected by Benedict's solution.
questions.p: Boiling don scatter the amylase inside tube B so e no fit digest starch again. Na only tube A wey active amylase dey break starch down to small sugar wey dey pass out to show positive Benedict's test.

questions.q: Chidinma set up a potometer with a leafy shoot and recorded the distance moved by an air bubble in 10 minutes under four different conditions: still air, a fan blowing air across the shoot, a humid plastic bag covering the shoot, and bright light. Under which condition would the bubble move slowest?
o: Still air with no additional treatment
Fan blowing air across the leaves
Shoot enclosed in a humid plastic bag
questions.e: High humidity around the leaf reduces the water vapour concentration gradient between the leaf and the air, so transpiration and water uptake slow down greatly. This makes the bubble move the least distance.
questions.p: When humidity dey high, water no dey quick evaporate from leaf. This one come make transpiration slow down, so the bubble no go move fast.

questions.q: Which blood vessel in the mammalian circulatory system carries deoxygenated blood away from the heart to the lungs?
questions.e: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated blood from the right ventricle to the lungs for gaseous exchange. It is the only artery in the body that carries deoxygenated blood.
questions.p: Na pulmonary artery dey carry blood wey no get oxygen from heart go lungs. Na only this artery dey carry deoxygenated blood for body.

questions.q: A gardener in Jos ring-barked a tree by removing a complete strip of bark around the trunk but left the wood intact. After some weeks, he observed swelling just above the cut. What is the most likely explanation for this observation?
o: Water movement in the xylem was blocked, causing wilting above the cut
Root pressure forced excess water to collect above the cut
Manufactured food accumulated above the cut because the phloem was removed
Mineral salts failed to reach the leaves, causing swelling
questions.e: Ring-barking removes the phloem, which transports manufactured food from the leaves downward. Since the food cannot pass the cut, it accumulates above the ring, causing swelling.
questions.p: Phloem na im dey carry food from leaf go down. If you cut the bark, food go stop for top and cause swelling because e no fit pass go down.

questions.q: In the mammalian heart, which structure separates the right atrium from the right ventricle and prevents backflow of blood into the atrium during ventricular contraction?
questions.e: The tricuspid valve lies between the right atrium and right ventricle and closes during ventricular contraction to prevent blood from flowing back into the atrium. The bicuspid valve performs this role on the left side instead.
questions.p: Tricuspid valve dey between right atrium and right ventricle. E dey close so blood no go flow back enter atrium when heart dey contract.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why root pressure alone cannot account for water rising to the top of very tall trees?
o: Root pressure pushes water only into the phloem, not the xylem
Root pressure only operates at night and stops during the day
Root pressure depends on transpiration, which does not occur in tall trees
Root pressure is too weak to overcome gravity and resistance in tall xylem columns
questions.e: Root pressure generates only a modest force, which is insufficient to lift water to the height of tall trees due to gravity and frictional resistance in the xylem. Instead, the cohesion-tension mechanism driven by transpiration pull is the main force responsible for water rising in tall trees.
questions.p: Root pressure no get power to push water reach top of tall trees. Gravity and friction too much, so na transpiration pull dey do the main work.

questions.q: A sample of mammalian blood was centrifuged and separated into layers. Which of the following components would be found in the straw-coloured liquid layer at the top?
o: Plasma containing dissolved proteins and salts
questions.e: Centrifuging blood separates it into plasma on top and cellular components below. Plasma is the straw-coloured liquid that carries dissolved proteins, salts, hormones, and other substances.
questions.p: When you spin blood, the top part wey be like straw na plasma. Na inside plasma all the protein and salt dey float.

questions.q: A student compared the walls of xylem vessels and phloem sieve tubes under a microscope. Which of the following is a correct structural difference between the two tissues?
o: Xylem vessels have lignified walls and no living contents at maturity, while phloem sieve tubes have thin walls and living cytoplasm
Xylem vessels possess companion cells, while phloem sieve tubes do not
Xylem vessels transport food substances, while phloem sieve tubes transport water
Phloem sieve tubes are lignified for strength, while xylem vessels remain unlignified
questions.e: Mature xylem vessels are dead, hollow, and lignified, which suits them for conducting water under tension. Phloem sieve tubes are living but lack a nucleus, and they rely on adjacent companion cells for metabolic support.
questions.p: Xylem get lignin for wall and e no get life again when e mature. Phloem still get living cytoplasm and e dey use companion cells to survive.

questions.q: A frog kept in a sealed jar with moist cotton wool but no water or pond was observed to survive for many hours even though it did not use its lungs actively. Which structure was mainly responsible for its gaseous exchange during this period?
questions.e: Frogs can exchange gases through their thin, moist, and highly vascularised skin, especially when inactive. This cutaneous respiration supplements the lungs and allows survival in moist but waterless conditions.
questions.p: Frog skin dey thin and e get plenty blood vessels wey dey help am breathe. Even if e no use im lungs, the moist skin go allow gas exchange make e survive.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct overall balanced word equation for aerobic respiration in living cells?
o: Glucose + oxygen -> carbon(IV) oxide + water + energy
questions.e: Aerobic respiration fully oxidises glucose using oxygen to release carbon(IV) oxide, water, and a large amount of energy. The other equations describe anaerobic processes or are incorrectly balanced.
questions.p: Aerobic respiration dey use oxygen to break down glucose completely. This one dey produce carbon(IV) oxide, water, and plenty energy for the body.

questions.q: A fish was removed from water and placed on a tray of wet grass for ten minutes. On examination, its gill filaments had collapsed together into a clumped mass. Which explanation best accounts for the fish's difficulty in breathing out of water?
o: The fish immediately switches to anaerobic respiration only
The collapsed filaments lose their large surface area needed for gas exchange
The operculum closes permanently once out of water
Water on the grass blocks the gill slits completely
questions.e: Gill filaments are supported by the buoyancy of water; out of water, they collapse and stick together, drastically reducing the surface area exposed to air. This makes efficient gas exchange impossible even though oxygen is present.
questions.p: When fish comot for water, the gill filaments dey stick together because water no dey support them again. This one come reduce the surface area wey the fish need to take breathe.

questions.q: An insect's tracheal system delivers oxygen directly to tissues through a network of air-filled tubes that open to the outside through small pores. What is the correct name of these external openings?
questions.e: Spiracles are the small external openings on an insect's body through which air enters and leaves the tracheal system. Stomata and lenticels are plant structures, while alveoli are found in mammalian lungs.
questions.p: Spiracles na the small holes wey dey for insect body wey air dey pass enter. Na through these holes the tracheal system dey get oxygen.

questions.q: A toad kept moist in a humid terrarium can exchange gases through its skin in addition to its lungs. Which of the following conditions is essential for this type of respiration to occur efficiently?
o: The skin must be thick and dry
The skin must remain moist and well supplied with blood capillaries
The skin must contain many sweat glands
The skin must be covered with scales
questions.e: Gases must dissolve in a moist film before they can diffuse across a respiratory surface, so the skin needs to stay moist and have a rich blood supply to carry the gases away. A thick or scaly dry skin would prevent diffusion.
questions.p: Gas must first dissolve for water before e go fit enter body. So, the skin must dey wet and get plenty blood vessels to carry the gas go round.

questions.q: Which pair of structures correctly represents the main respiratory organs used by a tadpole at the early larval stage and the adult frog it later becomes?
o: Gills in the tadpole; lungs and skin in the adult
Tracheae in the tadpole; gills in the adult
Lungs in the tadpole; gills in the adult
Skin only in the tadpole; tracheae in the adult
questions.e: A young tadpole breathes using external then internal gills like a fish, but as it metamorphoses into an adult frog, it develops lungs and also uses its moist skin for gaseous exchange. This change reflects its shift from fully aquatic to partly terrestrial life.
questions.p: Small tadpole dey use gills like fish to breathe inside water. When e grow reach adult frog, e go develop lungs and use e wet skin to breathe for land.

questions.q: A culture of yeast cells was grown under strictly anaerobic conditions in a glucose solution for several hours. Chemical tests on the medium would most likely confirm the presence of which two substances as end products?
questions.e: In the absence of oxygen, yeast carries out alcoholic fermentation, breaking down glucose into ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide gas. This process releases much less energy than aerobic respiration.
questions.p: When yeast no see oxygen, e dey break down glucose to produce ethanol and carbon(IV) oxide. This one na wetin we dey call alcoholic fermentation.

questions.q: A biology student set up an experiment to compare energy release from a measured mass of glucose broken down completely by aerobic respiration with the same mass broken down by anaerobic respiration in muscle cells. Which observation would correctly support the expected outcome?
o: Anaerobic respiration releases far more energy because glucose is only partly used
Aerobic respiration releases far more energy because glucose is completely oxidised to carbon(IV) oxide and water
Both processes release exactly the same amount of energy from the same mass of glucose
Anaerobic respiration releases more energy because no oxygen is needed to start the reaction
questions.e: Aerobic respiration completely breaks down glucose into carbon(IV) oxide and water, releasing a much larger amount of stored chemical energy than anaerobic respiration, which only partially breaks down glucose into lactic acid or ethanol. This is why anaerobic respiration is far less efficient.
questions.p: Aerobic respiration dey break glucose finish reach carbon(IV) oxide and water, so e dey give more energy. Anaerobic respiration no dey break glucose finish, so e no dey give plenty energy.

questions.q: During vigorous digging, an earthworm's moist cuticle becomes its main respiratory surface. A student argues that if the soil around the earthworm becomes completely dry for a long period, the worm will likely die from respiratory failure even though oxygen is still present in the air. Which reason best explains this?
o: The earthworm switches permanently to anaerobic respiration in dry soil
A dry cuticle increases the worm's surface area for gaseous exchange
Dry conditions increase the rate of diffusion of oxygen into the worm
Oxygen cannot dissolve in a dry cuticle, so gaseous exchange cannot take place
questions.e: The earthworm has no lungs or gills, so its cuticle must stay moist for oxygen to dissolve and diffuse into its blood vessels. If the cuticle dries out, gases can no longer be exchanged across it, leading to suffocation despite oxygen being available in the air.
questions.p: Earthworm skin must dey wet so oxygen go fit dissolve enter inside. If the skin dry, oxygen no go fit enter, and the worm go suffocate and die.

questions.q: A sprinter at an inter-house sports competition in Lagos continued running fast even after her breathing could no longer supply enough oxygen to her leg muscles. Which statement correctly describes what happens in her muscle cells at this point?
o: Her muscle cells increase the rate of the Krebs cycle to compensate for the oxygen shortage
Her muscles stop producing any form of energy until oxygen supply improves
Her muscle cells begin to convert glucose directly into carbon(IV) oxide and ethanol
Her muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration, converting glucose to lactic acid and building up an oxygen debt
questions.e: When oxygen supply cannot meet demand during intense exercise, muscle cells switch to anaerobic respiration, breaking down glucose into lactic acid and creating an oxygen debt that must later be repaid. Ethanol production only occurs in organisms like yeast and plants, not in human muscle.
questions.p: When oxygen no reach muscle well during running, the body dey switch to anaerobic respiration. This one dey turn glucose to lactic acid and create oxygen debt.

questions.q: A medical laboratory scientist examines a patient's urine and discovers an unusually high protein content. This observation most likely suggests damage to which part of the nephron?
questions.e: The glomerulus and Bowman's capsule form the filtration unit; large protein molecules should normally be retained in the blood. Damage here allows proteins to leak into the filtrate and appear in urine.
questions.p: Na glomerulus and Bowman's capsule dey do the filtration work, where big protein molecules suppose remain inside blood. If damage happen there, protein go leak enter urine.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the main excretory role of the skin in humans?
o: Regulation of blood sugar through sweat glands
Production of vitamin D as a waste product
Removal of excess water, salts and urea through sweat
Removal of carbon(IV)oxide and water vapour through pores
questions.e: The skin excretes excess water, mineral salts and small amounts of urea through sweat produced by sweat glands. Carbon(IV)oxide removal is mainly a lung function, not the skin's.
questions.p: Skin dey comot excess water, mineral salts, and small urea through sweat from sweat glands. Na lungs dey remove Carbon(IV)oxide, no be skin.

questions.q: During vigorous exercise on a football pitch in Enugu, a player's sweat glands become highly active. Which combination of conditions directly stimulates this increase in sweating?
o: Rise in body temperature and increased metabolic heat production
Decrease in blood glucose and increased insulin release
Fall in blood pressure and reduced oxygen supply
Rise in blood pH and reduced carbon(IV)oxide concentration
questions.e: Vigorous exercise raises body temperature due to increased metabolic activity, which stimulates sweat glands to produce more sweat for evaporative cooling. The other options are not the direct triggers for increased sweating.
questions.p: Hard exercise dey make body temperature rise because of too much metabolism, and this one dey trigger sweat glands to produce sweat for cooling. Na the main reason be that.

questions.q: A certain plant leaf, when examined, shows tiny pore-like structures on its lower epidermis through which water vapour and carbon(IV)oxide are lost or exchanged. These structures are called
questions.e: Stomata are tiny pores, mostly on the lower epidermis of leaves, that allow gaseous exchange and loss of water vapour through transpiration. Lenticels are found on woody stems, not leaves.
questions.p: Na stomata be those tiny pores for leaf epidermis wey dey allow gas exchange and transpiration. Lenticels dey for woody stem, no be leaf.

questions.q: A botanist studying waste disposal in plants notes that certain insoluble crystals of calcium oxalate accumulate permanently in specific leaf and stem cells rather than being transported out of the plant. Which of the following best explains why plants can tolerate storing such wastes internally?
o: Plants have highly efficient kidneys that later filter out the crystals
Plant wastes are always in gaseous form and simply diffuse out through roots
Plants have a lower metabolic rate than animals, so they produce fewer toxic wastes and can store the less harmful ones in cell vacuoles or dead tissues
Plants convert all metabolic wastes immediately into chlorophyll for reuse
questions.e: Unlike animals, plants have slower metabolism and produce less toxic waste, so they can safely store insoluble wastes like calcium oxalate crystals in vacuoles, old leaves, or dead tissues such as bark. Plants have no kidneys, and wastes are not always gaseous.
questions.p: Plants no get kidney, but dem get slow metabolism, so dem fit keep waste like calcium oxalate inside vacuoles or dead tissues safely. Dem no dey convert everything to chlorophyll.

questions.q: A renal patient has significantly reduced blood pressure due to severe bleeding after an accident. A doctor explains that this will reduce urine formation. Which stage of urine formation is most directly affected by this drop in blood pressure?
o: Secretion in the distal convoluted tubule
Reabsorption in the proximal convoluted tubule
Concentration of urine in the collecting duct
questions.e: Ultrafiltration at the glomerulus depends on high hydrostatic blood pressure forcing fluid out of the capillaries into Bowman's capsule. A severe drop in blood pressure reduces this filtration pressure, directly lowering the rate of urine formation at this stage.
questions.p: Ultrafiltration for glomerulus need high blood pressure to push fluid enter Bowman's capsule. If blood pressure drop well well, urine formation go reduce direct.

questions.q: The functional and structural unit of the mammalian kidney, which is responsible for both filtration and selective reabsorption of substances, is called the:
questions.e: The nephron is the basic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The glomerulus is only a part of the nephron, while the nephridium is the excretory unit found in earthworms, not mammals.
questions.p: Na nephron bi di main part wey dey do work for kidney. Glomerulus na just small part of am, and nephridium na wetin earthworm dey use do excretion.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly lists, in the right order, the pathway followed by urine from where it is formed to where it leaves the body?
questions.e: Urine is formed in the kidney, carried by the ureter to the bladder for temporary storage, and then expelled through the urethra. Mixing up the ureter and urethra is a common error candidates make.
questions.p: Urine dey start for kidney, go pass ureter enter bladder, before e comot for urethra. Many pipo dey confuse ureter and urethra, but dis order na correct one.

questions.q: During very cold harmattan weather in Jos, the tiny muscles attached to the hair follicles in the skin contract, causing the hairs to stand erect. What is the main survival advantage of this response?
o: It increases sweat production to warm the body
It increases blood flow to the skin surface to radiate more heat
It traps a layer of air close to the skin to reduce heat loss
It widens the pores to release more body heat
questions.e: When hairs stand erect due to contraction of the arrector pili muscles, they trap a layer of air which acts as insulation, reducing heat loss from the body. This is a heat-conserving response, not a heat-losing one, which rules out the sweat and blood flow options.
questions.p: Wen hair stand up, e dey trap air wey dey keep body warm. Dis one dey stop heat make e no comot for body, so e no get anything to do with sweat.

questions.q: A student represents the human urinary system as a filtering unit and notes that a certain blood vessel carries blood away from the glomerulus at a narrower diameter than the vessel that brought blood into it. This difference in diameter is important because it:
o: prevents reabsorption of water in the proximal convoluted tubule
creates the high pressure needed to force fluid out of the glomerular capillaries
reduces blood pressure in the glomerulus, stopping filtration
allows red blood cells to pass directly into the nephron
questions.e: The afferent arteriole is wider than the efferent arteriole leaving the glomerulus, and this difference builds up high hydrostatic pressure that pushes water and small solutes out of the blood into the Bowman's capsule. This pressure drives ultrafiltration; it does not stop it or allow red blood cells through, since these are too large to filter.
questions.p: Di vessel wey dey bring blood inside glomerulus big pass di one wey dey comot. Dis difference dey create high pressure wey dey force water and small things comot for blood.

questions.q: In a simple experiment, a fresh green leaf is enclosed in a transparent polythene bag and left in sunlight for about an hour. Tiny droplets of liquid are later observed on the inner surface of the bag. This liquid is best described as a product of which process?
questions.e: Transpiration is the loss of water vapour from the leaf surfaces, which condenses as liquid droplets on the inner wall of the polythene bag. Guttation instead produces liquid water directly from special pores at the leaf margins, usually under conditions of high humidity, not from vapour loss in a bag.
questions.p: Transpiration na wen plant lose water as vapour, wey come turn to water for inside di bag. Guttation different because e dey comot liquid water direct from leaf edge.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why urine formed in the kidney is usually more concentrated than the original glomerular filtrate?
o: Large plasma proteins are added to the filtrate as it passes along the tubule
Glucose is actively secreted into the filtrate in the collecting duct
Water is reabsorbed back into the blood along various parts of the nephron
The filtrate loses salts but gains an equal volume of water in the loop of Henle
questions.e: As the filtrate moves through the nephron, especially the proximal tubule, loop of Henle and collecting duct, large amounts of water are reabsorbed into the surrounding blood capillaries, concentrating the remaining fluid into urine. Proteins are not added to the filtrate, and glucose is reabsorbed rather than secreted under normal conditions.
questions.p: As filtrate dey waka pass nephron, body dey collect water back into blood. Dis one dey make di urine wey remain come concentrate pass how e start.

questions.q: A certain leguminous plant growing along a roadside in Minna sheds some of its old leaves even though the leaves are not diseased or damaged. Which of the following best explains this as a form of excretion in plants?
o: The leaves are shed only to reduce competition for sunlight with neighbouring plants
The plant sheds leaves purely as a response to physical damage by animals
The plant sheds leaves to increase the rate of photosynthesis in younger leaves
The leaves are used to store and later remove waste products such as tannins and metabolic by-products
questions.e: In many plants, waste substances such as tannins, resins and other metabolic by-products accumulate in ageing leaves, and leaf fall serves as a way of removing these wastes from the plant body. The other options describe ecological or growth-related reasons and do not directly explain excretion.
questions.p: Plants dey store waste like tannins inside old leaves. Wen dem comot di leaves, e be like say dem dey throway waste comot for body.

questions.q: A cartilaginous joint found between the vertebrae of the human backbone allows only slight movement. Which structure is responsible for this limited flexibility and shock absorption?
o: Yellow elastic cartilage of the pinna
questions.e: Intervertebral discs are pads of fibrocartilage between vertebrae that cushion shocks and permit slight bending movement. Synovial membranes and ligaments belong to freely movable joints, not this cartilaginous type.
questions.p: Intervertebral disc wey get fibrocartilage dey cushion shock and allow small movement between backbone. Synovial membrane and ligament dey for joint wey dey move well well, no be this one.

questions.q: An athlete's thigh bone (femur) fits into a cup-shaped socket on the pelvis, permitting movement in almost every direction, including rotation. Which type of joint is this?
questions.e: A ball and socket joint, like the hip joint, allows movement in many directions including rotation because a rounded bone end fits into a cup-like socket. Hinge joints only allow back-and-forth movement in one plane.
questions.p: Ball and socket joint like hip joint allow movement for all side including rotation because bone head fit cup-like socket. Hinge joint dey allow movement only for one direction.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why plant cells with thickened cellulose walls (collenchyma) can bend without breaking, unlike lignified sclerenchyma cells?
o: Collenchyma lacks cellulose entirely, relying only on turgor pressure
Sclerenchyma cells contain chloroplasts that stiffen the wall
Collenchyma cells are dead at maturity, giving them elastic properties
Collenchyma walls are thickened unevenly at the corners and remain flexible, while sclerenchyma walls are uniformly lignified and rigid
questions.e: Collenchyma has unevenly thickened, non-lignified walls (thicker at corners) which keep it flexible for bending support in young growing stems. Sclerenchyma walls are uniformly thickened with lignin, making them rigid and suited for fixed mechanical support rather than bending.
questions.p: Collenchyma wall thick for corner only and e remain flexible to support young stem, but sclerenchyma wall get lignin everywhere wey make am hard and rigid.

questions.q: In an experiment, a wilted vegetable leaf from a garden in Jos regains its firmness after being placed in water for some hours. Which process best accounts for this change in the plant cells?
o: Loss of water from cells by exosmosis, reducing turgor pressure
Entry of water into cells by osmosis, increasing turgor pressure against the cell wall
Breakdown of the cellulose cell wall by enzymes
Active transport of water out of the vacuole into the cytoplasm
questions.e: Water moves into the plant cells by osmosis, filling the vacuole and pushing the cytoplasm against the cell wall, making the cell turgid and firm. This restores support in herbaceous tissues, unlike water loss which causes wilting.
questions.p: Water dey enter plant cell through osmosis, make vacuole full and push cytoplasm against cell wall. This one dey bring back turgor pressure and remove wilting.

questions.q: A weightlifter's biceps brachii muscle is described as having its origin on the scapula and its insertion on the radius. If this muscle contracts strongly, which of the following correctly describes the resulting action at the elbow?
o: The forearm extends because the insertion bone moves away from the origin
The upper arm rotates at the shoulder while the forearm stays fixed
The forearm flexes because the insertion bone is pulled toward the origin
The triceps shortens simultaneously to produce the same flexion
questions.e: When a muscle contracts, it shortens and pulls the insertion bone toward the origin; for the biceps this pulls the radius upward, flexing the elbow. Extension would instead require the triceps to contract while the biceps relaxes.
questions.p: When muscle contract, e dey pull the insertion bone go meet the origin, so biceps go pull radius up to bend elbow. Extension na work for triceps.

questions.q: During a 400-metre race at a sports meet in Enugu, an athlete's leg muscles contract repeatedly using large amounts of ATP. If oxygen supply becomes insufficient, which process allows the muscle to continue producing some energy, though with a side effect that causes fatigue?
o: Direct conversion of fat to ATP without any respiration pathway
Complete breakdown of glucose to carbon dioxide and water without oxygen
Aerobic respiration using excess oxygen reserves in the blood
Anaerobic respiration producing lactic acid in the muscle cells
questions.e: When oxygen is insufficient, muscle cells respire anaerobically, converting glucose to lactic acid and releasing a small amount of ATP. The accumulating lactic acid causes the fatigue and cramps felt by the athlete.
questions.p: If oxygen no reach muscle well during race, energy go still come out through anaerobic respiration, but e go produce lactic acid. Na this lactic acid dey cause muscle fatigue and pain.

questions.q: A science student observes two bones connected at the shoulder, held together by a band of tough, slightly elastic connective tissue that stabilises the joint and limits excessive movement. What is this connective tissue called?
questions.e: Ligaments are tough, slightly elastic tissues that connect bone to bone, stabilising joints and preventing dislocation. Tendons instead attach muscle to bone, while cartilage and periosteum have different roles in the skeleton.
questions.p: Ligament na tough tissue wey dey connect bone to bone to hold joint strong and stop dislocating. Tendon na the one wey dey connect muscle to bone.

questions.q: Which pair of bones forms the pectoral girdle in man, serving as the attachment point for the bones of the upper limb?
questions.e: The pectoral (shoulder) girdle is made up of the scapula (shoulder blade) and the clavicle (collar bone). These bones attach the upper limb to the axial skeleton.
questions.p: Pectoral girdle na scapula and clavicle. Dem dey join upper limb to the axial skeleton.

questions.q: A fish uses blocks of muscle called myotomes arranged along its body to swim. These myotomes contract alternately on each side of the body. What is the main mechanical effect of this alternate contraction?
o: It stiffens the vertebral column to prevent any bending
It produces side-to-side bending that pushes water backward, propelling the fish forward
It pumps blood faster through the gills
It compresses the swim bladder to control depth
questions.e: Alternate contraction of myotomes on either side bends the body into waves. This wave motion pushes against the water, generating thrust that moves the fish forward.
questions.p: When myotomes dey contract side to side, e dey bend body to push water back. Dis one dey make fish move forward.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the structure and function of yellow elastic cartilage found in the human ear pinna and epiglottis?
o: It contains no cells and is formed entirely of collagen fibres
It is found at joint surfaces where it reduces friction during movement
It contains elastic fibres that allow it to bend and spring back to its original shape
It is heavily calcified, making it as hard and rigid as bone
questions.e: Yellow elastic cartilage has elastic fibres embedded in its matrix, giving it flexibility so it can bend and return to shape. This suits structures like the ear pinna that need to flex repeatedly without breaking.
questions.p: Yellow elastic cartilage get fibres wey dey allow am bend and come back to shape. E good well well for ear pinna.

questions.q: In the mammalian skeleton, red bone marrow found in the spongy bone of structures such as the sternum and ribs performs which important function?
o: Secretion of synovial fluid for joints
Formation of new cartilage at growth plates
questions.e: Red bone marrow is the site of haemopoiesis, the production of red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. It is found in spongy bone of flat and some long bones.
questions.p: Red bone marrow na im dey produce blood cells. E dey inside spongy bone of flat bones.

questions.q: A student compares two types of muscle under a microscope. Tissue X shows long, unbranched, striated fibres with many nuclei at the edge, under voluntary control. Tissue Y shows short, spindle-shaped, unstriated fibres with one central nucleus each, under involuntary control. Tissue Y most likely came from which part of the body?
o: Biceps brachii of the upper arm
Skeletal muscle attached to the jaw bone
questions.e: Tissue Y matches smooth muscle, which is unstriated, spindle-shaped with a single central nucleus and works involuntarily. Smooth muscle lines the walls of internal organs like the intestine, unlike skeletal muscle described as tissue X.
questions.p: Tissue Y na smooth muscle wey no get striations and dey work on im own. Na im dey form wall of small intestine.

questions.q: A patient's X-ray shows that the ball-shaped head of the humerus has slipped completely out of the shoulder socket after a fall. Which term correctly describes this condition?
questions.e: A dislocation occurs when a bone is forced out of its normal position at a joint. A fracture would instead mean a break in the bone itself, while a sprain involves ligament damage without the bone leaving the socket.
questions.p: Dislocation happen when bone commot from im normal socket for joint. E different from when bone break.

questions.q: In woody plants, secondary thickening produces annual growth rings that can be counted to estimate the age of a tree. These rings are formed mainly as a result of the seasonal activity of which tissue?
questions.e: The vascular cambium produces new xylem and phloem each growing season; it grows faster in the wet season and slower in the dry season, creating visible rings of differing wood density. Counting these rings gives the tree's approximate age.
questions.p: Vascular cambium dey produce new xylem and phloem every season to form annual rings. We fit use am count tree age.

questions.q: A placental mammal gives birth to young that have developed inside the mother's uterus and are nourished through a placenta. Which of the following is the main advantage of this mode of reproduction over external development in eggs?
o: It eliminates the need for fertilization to occur internally
It allows the embryo to develop in a more stable and protected environment
It increases the number of offspring produced at a time
It allows the young to be independent immediately after fertilization
questions.e: Internal development inside the mother's body protects the embryo from predators, temperature changes and desiccation, and allows continuous nourishment through the placenta. This greatly improves the chances of survival of the young.
questions.p: E dey protect di pikin well well inside mama body from danger and bad weather. E also dey give food direct through placenta make survival sure.

questions.q: Which of the following floral structures is responsible for producing pollen grains in a flowering plant?
questions.e: The anther is the part of the stamen that contains pollen sacs where pollen grains, containing the male gametes, are produced. The stigma receives pollen, while the style and ovule are parts of the female organ.
questions.p: Na anther be di part of stamen wey dey make pollen grains. Na inside am male gametes dey.

questions.q: A certain insect-pollinated flower produces large, sticky, spiny pollen grains in small quantities. Which of the following is the most likely reason for this characteristic?
o: To increase the rate of self-pollination within the same flower
To make the pollen light enough to be carried by wind over long distances
To prevent the pollen from germinating on the stigma of the same flower
To allow the pollen to easily stick to the body of visiting insects for transfer
questions.e: Insect-pollinated flowers usually produce sticky or spiny pollen so that it attaches firmly to the body of visiting insects and is carried to another flower. Wind-pollinated flowers, in contrast, produce light, smooth pollen in large amounts.
questions.p: Sticky and spiny pollen dey help am hold body of insect tight. Dis one dey make transport go another flower easy.

questions.q: In a Nigerian secondary school practical class, a student dissected a mature testis and observed coiled tubules where sperm cells are produced. What is the correct name of these tubules, and what other important cells are found between them?
questions.e: Sperm cells are produced in the seminiferous tubules of the testis, while the spaces between these tubules contain interstitial cells, also called Leydig cells, which secrete testosterone. The other options name structures involved in sperm transport or female reproduction, not sperm production.
questions.p: Na seminiferous tubules dey make sperm inside testis. Interstitial or Leydig cells dey between dem to produce testosterone.

questions.q: During the human menstrual cycle, a rise in the level of luteinizing hormone (LH) causes a surge that triggers a specific event around the middle of the cycle. What is this event?
o: Thickening of the endometrium in preparation for implantation
Rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the secondary oocyte
Formation of the corpus luteum from the ruptured follicle
questions.e: The LH surge in the middle of the menstrual cycle causes the mature Graafian follicle to rupture, releasing the secondary oocyte in a process called ovulation. The corpus luteum forms only after this rupture has occurred.
questions.p: Di LH surge for middle of cycle dey make Graafian follicle burst. Na dat time egg dey comot for ovulation.

questions.q: A farmer in Oyo State grows a crop whose flowers mature their anthers and release pollen several days before the stigma of the same flower becomes receptive. What is the biological significance of this arrangement?
o: It promotes cross-pollination by preventing self-pollination in the same flower
It increases the chance of self-pollination within the same flower
It ensures that pollination occurs only at night
It prevents the flower from producing viable seeds at all
questions.e: When anthers release pollen before the stigma of the same flower is ready to receive pollen, a condition called protandry, self-pollination within that flower is prevented. This favours cross-pollination, which increases genetic variation in the offspring.
questions.p: Dis one na protandry and e dey stop self-pollination. E dey encourage cross-pollination to bring better variation.

questions.q: A man and woman undergo a fertility test, and it is discovered that the woman's uterine tubes are completely blocked on both sides, although she ovulates normally and has a healthy uterus. Which of the following outcomes is most likely as a direct result of this condition?
o: She will be unable to menstruate at all
The egg will be unable to leave the ovary during ovulation
Implantation will fail even if fertilization occurs normally
Fertilization will not occur because the sperm cannot meet the egg
questions.e: Fertilization normally takes place in the uterine (Fallopian) tube, so if both tubes are blocked, sperm cannot reach the released egg and fertilization cannot occur. The ovary can still release an egg during ovulation and menstruation can still occur, since these processes do not require the tubes to be open.
questions.p: If uterine tubes block, sperm no go fit meet egg for fertilization. But ovulation and menstruation still dey happen normally.

questions.q: A gardener in Kano notices that a certain flower has a long tubular corolla, produces nectar deep at its base, and opens mainly in the evening with a strong sweet scent. Which agent most likely pollinates this flower?
questions.e: Long tubular flowers with deep nectar, evening opening and strong scent are adaptations to attract moths, which are active at night and have long proboscises to reach the nectar. Wind and water pollinated flowers do not need scent or nectar.
questions.p: Dis kind flower wey get long mouth, sweet scent and dey open for night na moth dey pollinate am. Na because moth dey active for night and get long mouth to drink the nectar.

questions.q: In the human male reproductive system, which structure is mainly responsible for producing the fluid that nourishes and activates sperm cells before ejaculation?
questions.e: The seminal vesicle secretes a fructose-rich fluid that nourishes sperm and forms a large part of semen. The testis produces sperm, while the epididymis stores and matures them, and the vas deferens only transports them.
questions.p: Na seminal vesicle dey produce the fluid wey dey give sperm food and make am active before e come out. Testis dey make sperm, epididymis dey keep and train am, while vas deferens na just road wey e dey pass.

questions.q: During implantation in human reproduction, the fertilized egg (blastocyst) embeds itself into which layer of the uterus?
questions.e: The endometrium is the inner lining of the uterus that thickens under hormonal control to receive and support the implanted blastocyst. The myometrium is the muscular layer, not involved in implantation.
questions.p: Na endometrium be the inner skin of womb wey the small belle (blastocyst) dey enter and gum body during implantation. Myometrium na just muscle layer, no be there belle dey stay.

questions.q: A certain flowering plant has small, dull-coloured flowers without petals, produces large amounts of light, smooth pollen, and has feathery stigmas that hang outside the flower. Which mode of pollination does this plant most likely use?
questions.e: Dull small flowers, light smooth pollen produced in large quantity, and exposed feathery stigmas are classic adaptations for catching pollen carried by wind. Insect-pollinated flowers are usually bright, scented and sticky-pollened instead.
questions.p: Flower wey no fine, no get petal, but get light pollen and feather stigma wey dey hang outside na wind dey carry hin pollen. Insect flower dey fine and get scent, but dis one na pure wind work.

questions.q: In a breeding experiment, a scientist removes the anthers of a flower before they mature and later transfers pollen from a different plant of the same species onto its stigma. What is this procedure called, and what is one likely benefit of it?
o: Self-pollination, which guarantees genetically identical offspring
Cross-pollination, which can introduce new genetic variation into offspring
Artificial vegetative propagation, which produces clones faster
questions.e: Transferring pollen from one plant to the stigma of a different plant of the same species is cross-pollination, and it increases genetic variation in the offspring because two different parents contribute genes. The other options describe different processes not matching the procedure described.
questions.p: If you carry pollen from one plant go put for another plant of the same kind, na cross-pollination. E dey help bring new gene join together so pikin go get better variation.

questions.q: A tall pawpaw tree in a school farm has flowers that are either strictly male (producing only pollen) or strictly female (producing only ovules), found on separate individual plants. This condition, where male and female flowers occur on different plants of the same species, is known as which term?
questions.e: Plants that bear male and female flowers on separate individual plants are described as dioecious, as seen in pawpaw. Monoecious plants bear both male and female flowers on the same plant, while hermaphrodite flowers have both sexes in one flower.
questions.p: If male flower dey one pawpaw tree and female flower dey another different pawpaw tree, we dey call am dioecious. Monoecious mean say male and female dey the same tree, while hermaphrodite mean say everything dey one single flower.

questions.q: During germination of a maize grain, the radicle emerges first before the plumule. What is the main biological advantage of this sequence of events?
o: It allows the seed coat to split open faster
It reduces the rate of respiration in the embryo
It prevents the young shoot from being eaten by soil insects
It allows the seedling to quickly anchor itself and begin absorbing water and mineral salts from the soil
questions.e: The radicle grows into the root, which anchors the seedling and absorbs water and minerals needed to support further growth. This early establishment of a root system supports the later emergence and growth of the shoot.
questions.p: Radicle dey grow first to turn to root, wey dey hold ground well and suck water and minerals for plant. Dis one make sure say water and food ready before plumule shoot come out.

questions.q: In a school biology practical, Amaka measured the length of a growing shoot every two days and plotted length against time. The resulting graph was S-shaped, rising slowly at first, then rapidly, before leveling off. What does the final flat portion of this curve represent?
o: The stationary phase, where growth rate has slowed down and nearly stopped
The exponential phase, where growth rate is highest
The death phase, where the organism begins to decompose
The lag phase, where cell division is just starting
questions.e: A sigmoid growth curve has a lag phase, a rapid exponential phase, and finally a stationary phase where growth levels off as the organism reaches maturity or resource limits are reached. The flat part at the end of the curve is this stationary phase.
questions.p: S-shaped growth curve dey get lag phase, rapid phase, and stationary phase when growth don nearly stop. Dat flat part for the end na the stationary phase as maturity don reach.

questions.q: A plant growth hormone is known to promote cell division in tissue culture, delay ageing of leaves, and stimulate the growth of lateral buds when applied in the right concentration. Which hormone has these effects?
questions.e: Cytokinins are well known for promoting cell division, delaying leaf senescence, and encouraging lateral bud growth, which is why they are widely used in tissue culture media. Auxin, abscisic acid, and ethylene have different major roles in plant development.
questions.p: Cytokinins na the hormone wey dey help cell division, make leaf no quick old, and ginger lateral bud growth for tissue culture. E dey different from auxin, abscisic acid, and ethylene.

questions.q: In an investigation, a student placed a potted seedling on its side in a dark cupboard for five days. On uncovering the pot, the shoot was observed to have curved and grown upward against gravity, while the root had curved and grown downward. What term best describes this pair of growth responses?
o: Phototropism in both shoot and root
Negative geotropism in the shoot and positive geotropism in the root
Positive geotropism in the shoot and negative geotropism in the root
Thigmotropism in both shoot and root
questions.e: A shoot growing upward, away from the pull of gravity, shows negative geotropism, while a root growing downward, towards the pull of gravity, shows positive geotropism. Since the cupboard was dark, light was not responsible for this response, so it cannot be phototropism.
questions.p: Shoot dey grow go up, away from gravity, meaning na negative geotropism. Root dey grow go down, follow gravity, meaning na positive geotropism because dark everywhere.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines growth in a living organism?
o: A reversible increase in the number of cells without change in form
The ability of an organism to respond to external stimuli
An irreversible increase in size, dry mass and cell number of an organism
A temporary swelling of tissues due to water uptake
questions.e: Growth is an irreversible permanent increase in size, dry mass and cell number of an organism. It is not reversible like swelling from water absorption, which only affects fresh mass temporarily.
questions.p: Growth na permanent increase for size, dry mass and cell number of living thing. E no dey reverse like when water make body swell up small time.

questions.q: A packet of garden egg seeds was sown in moist soil in Kano. Three days later, students dug up some seeds and observed that the seed coat had absorbed water and softened, but no root or shoot had yet emerged. Which stage of germination does this represent?
questions.e: Imbibition is the first stage of germination in which the seed absorbs water, causing the seed coat to soften and swell before any visible growth of root or shoot occurs. Food mobilisation and radicle emergence happen after this stage.
questions.p: Imbibition na the first stage where seed drink water so wey the coat go soft and swell up before root or shoot come out.

questions.q: Which external condition, if absent, would most directly prevent a viable groundnut seed from germinating even when soil moisture and warm temperature are adequate?
questions.e: Germinating seeds need oxygen for aerobic respiration to release the energy required for growth. Most seeds do not need light to germinate, so its absence or presence is less critical than oxygen supply.
questions.p: Seed need oxygen for aerobic respiration so wey dem fit get energy for growth. If oxygen no dey, seed no go germinat even if water and temperature good.

questions.q: A biology class compared two groups of maize seedlings. Group P was grown with adequate gibberellin activity, while Group Q had gibberellin synthesis blocked using a chemical inhibitor. After two weeks, Group Q seedlings were noticeably shorter with poor internode elongation. What does this experiment best demonstrate?
o: Gibberellin controls stomatal closure in leaves
Gibberellin inhibits germination of maize grains
Gibberellin promotes stem elongation by stimulating cell division and elongation
Gibberellin is responsible for root initiation in seedlings
questions.e: Gibberellins are known to promote stem elongation through increased cell division and cell elongation, so blocking them results in shorter seedlings with poor internode growth. The hormone is not primarily linked to root initiation or stomatal closure.
questions.p: Gibberellin dey help stem grow long through cell division and elongation. If you block am, the plant go short and internode growth go bad.

questions.q: In an epigeal type of germination such as in bean seeds, the hypocotyl elongates and arches above the soil before straightening. What is the main functional advantage of this hypocotyl hook formation?
o: It increases the rate of water absorption by the cotyledons
It prevents the seed coat from splitting too early
It allows the radicle to penetrate deeper into the soil
It protects the delicate plumule from mechanical damage while pushing through the soil
questions.e: The arched hypocotyl hook pulls the cotyledons and protects the tender plumule as it is dragged through the soil, preventing damage to the delicate shoot tip. Once above ground, the hook straightens and the plumule develops normally.
questions.p: The hypocotyl hook dey protect the tender plumule make e no scatter when e dey push pass sand. When e reach up, e go straight.

questions.q: A student set up two identical pots of millet seedlings. Pot X received adequate nitrogen fertiliser while Pot Y received none, both under the same light, water and temperature conditions. After three weeks, Pot X plants were taller, greener and had more leaves. Which conclusion is most valid from this observation?
o: Mineral nutrients such as nitrogen influence the rate of plant growth and development
Nitrogen has no effect on vegetative growth
Water availability determined the difference in growth observed
Light intensity was the main factor responsible for the difference
questions.e: Since light, water and temperature were kept the same for both pots, the only varied factor was nitrogen supply, showing that nitrogen as a mineral nutrient affects growth rate and leaf development. The other options ignore the controlled variables in the setup.
questions.p: As water and light sama for both pots, na nitrogen wey dey inside fertilizer make pot X grow tall and green pass pot Y.

questions.q: A scientist measured the fresh mass, dry mass and length of a batch of germinating cowpea seeds daily for ten days. She noticed that dry mass decreased steadily for the first four days before beginning to increase afterward. What best explains this initial decrease in dry mass?
o: Stored food reserves are being broken down and used up in respiration faster than new tissue is built
Water is being lost continuously from the seed during this period
Minerals are leaching out of the cotyledons into the soil
The seed coat is shedding mass as it ruptures
questions.e: During early germination, stored food reserves are respired to provide energy for growth before the seedling can photosynthesise, so dry mass falls as reserves are consumed. Dry mass rises again once photosynthesis begins to add new organic material faster than respiration removes it.
questions.p: For the beginning, seed dey use up him stored food for respiration to get energy, and that one dey make dry mass reduce before photosynthesis start.

questions.q: A plant physiologist plotted the growth curve of a sunflower plant from seed to maturity and obtained a sigmoid (S-shaped) curve. At which phase of this curve is the growth rate lowest and the plant approaching its maximum size, often due to limited resources and ageing?
questions.e: In the stationary or decline phase of a sigmoid growth curve, growth rate slows down and levels off as the organism approaches maximum size, limited by factors such as nutrients, space or age. The lag and exponential phases occur earlier when growth is slow then rapid respectively.
questions.p: For stationary phase, growth rate slow down well well as plant reach maximum size because food, space or age don catch up with am.

questions.q: A student cuts across a thin section of the spinal cord and observes a butterfly-shaped region in the centre. This central region, which contains mostly cell bodies of neurones, is best described as the:
questions.e: The butterfly-shaped central part of the spinal cord is grey matter, made up mainly of neurone cell bodies and synapses. White matter surrounds it and is made of myelinated axons.
questions.p: That butterfly-shaped part for inside spinal cord na grey matter, e dey full of neurone cell bodies and synapses. Na white matter dey surround am, and e contain myelinated axons.

questions.q: Which part of the human brain is mainly responsible for controlling involuntary activities such as heartbeat, breathing rate and blood pressure?
questions.e: The medulla oblongata, located in the hindbrain, controls vital involuntary activities like heartbeat and breathing. The cerebrum deals with thought and voluntary action, while the cerebellum controls balance.
questions.p: Na medulla oblongata dey control important involuntary work like heartbeat and breathing. Cerebrum dey handle thinking and voluntary action, while cerebellum dey control balance.

questions.q: A table tennis player at a Lagos sports club tracks a fast-moving ball with her eyes. Which structure in the eye adjusts automatically to control the amount of light entering so she can see clearly under the bright hall lights?
questions.e: The iris contains muscles that widen or narrow the pupil to regulate the amount of light entering the eye. The lens focuses light, while the retina detects the image formed.
questions.p: Na iris get muscles wey dey open or close pupil to regulate how light enter eye. Lens dey focus light, while retina dey see the image wey form.

questions.q: In the human ear, vibrations from sound waves are first converted into mechanical movement by which structure before reaching the inner ear?
questions.e: The eardrum vibrates when sound waves strike it, and these vibrations are passed to the ossicles and then to the cochlea. The pinna only collects sound, while the auditory nerve carries electrical impulses, not vibrations.
questions.p: Na eardrum dey shake when sound touch am, and e dey send the movement go ossicles then reach cochlea. Pinna just dey gather sound, and auditory nerve dey carry electrical signal, no be physical vibration.

questions.q: A doctor taps the tendon just below a patient's kneecap with a small hammer, causing the lower leg to jerk forward involuntarily. Which feature of this reflex action best explains why the patient cannot consciously prevent the immediate jerk?
o: The impulse must first travel through the cerebrum for interpretation
The sensory neurone connects straight to the motor neurone outside the body
The response is coordinated at the spinal cord without waiting for the brain
The muscle contracts due to direct stimulation by the hammer
questions.e: In a reflex arc, the spinal cord processes the signal directly, producing a fast automatic response before the brain becomes aware of it. This speed is what makes conscious prevention impossible.
questions.p: For reflex action, na spinal cord dey process the signal sharp sharp before brain even know wetin happen. E fast well well, na that one make am hard for person make e stop am with brain.

questions.q: A science teacher in Ibadan explains that some reflex arcs involve three neurones instead of just two. In such a reflex arc, what is the correct order of impulse transmission from the receptor to the effector?
o: Receptor to relay neurone to sensory neurone to motor neurone to effector
Receptor to motor neurone to relay neurone to sensory neurone to effector
Receptor to motor neurone to sensory neurone to relay neurone to effector
Receptor to sensory neurone to relay neurone to motor neurone to effector
questions.e: The correct pathway in a three-neurone reflex arc is receptor, sensory neurone, relay (intermediate) neurone in the spinal cord, motor neurone, then effector. This order ensures the impulse is properly relayed within the central nervous system.
