questions.p: The correct way wey impulse dey travel for three-neurone reflex arc na receptor, sensory neurone, relay neurone for spinal cord, motor neurone, then effector. This order make sure say message pass well inside central nervous system.

questions.q: Okon rubs his palms together vigorously on a cold harmattan morning in Jos. Which type of receptor in his skin is mainly responsible for detecting the resulting heat produced by friction?
questions.e: Thermoreceptors in the skin detect changes in temperature, such as the warmth generated from rubbing palms together. Mechanoreceptors respond to pressure or touch, not temperature changes.
questions.p: Na thermoreceptor for skin dey feel temperature change like that warmth from rubbing hand together. Mechanoreceptor dey answer touch or pressure, no be heat.

questions.q: A student is asked to distinguish between a sensory neurone and a motor neurone based on their functions in the nervous system. Which statement correctly describes this difference?
o: Sensory neurones carry impulses from receptors to the CNS, while motor neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors
Sensory neurones carry impulses from the CNS to effectors, while motor neurones carry impulses from receptors to the CNS
Both neurones carry impulses only within the brain and spinal cord
Sensory neurones connect directly to effectors without passing through the CNS
questions.e: Sensory neurones transmit impulses from receptors towards the central nervous system, while motor neurones carry impulses away from the CNS to muscles or glands (effectors). This distinction is fundamental to understanding reflex arcs and voluntary responses.
questions.p: Sensory neurones dey carry message from receptors go central nervous system, while motor neurones dey carry message commot from CNS go effectors like muscles. Dis difference very important to know how body dey respond.

questions.q: Which part of the brain forms the link between the cerebrum and the spinal cord, and also controls vital reflexes such as swallowing, coughing and vomiting?
questions.e: The medulla oblongata connects the brain to the spinal cord and regulates vital reflex actions like swallowing, coughing and vomiting. The cerebellum controls balance, not these reflexes.
questions.p: Na medulla oblongata dey connect brain join spinal cord, e still dey control important reflex like to dey cough, vomit and swallow. E correct well well.

questions.q: A student slices through the human eyeball from front to back and examines the layers. Which layer is correctly described as the tough, white, outer protective coat that is continuous with the transparent cornea?
questions.e: The sclera is the tough, white outer coat of the eyeball that protects the inner structures and is continuous with the clear cornea at the front. The choroid is the middle pigmented, vascular layer, while the retina is the innermost light-sensitive layer.
questions.p: Na sclera be that strong white cover wey dey protect eye for outside and join join with the transparent cornea for front. E correct die.

questions.q: A farmer in Kano accidentally steps on a sharp thorn with his bare foot and rapidly lifts the foot before feeling pain. Which sequence correctly shows the order of structures involved in this withdrawal reflex?
o: Effector -> sensory neurone -> relay neurone -> motor neurone -> receptor
Receptor -> relay neurone -> sensory neurone -> motor neurone -> effector
Receptor -> sensory neurone -> relay neurone -> motor neurone -> effector
Receptor -> motor neurone -> relay neurone -> sensory neurone -> effector
questions.e: In a typical spinal reflex arc, the receptor detects the stimulus, the sensory neurone carries the impulse to the spinal cord, a relay neurone processes it, the motor neurone then carries the impulse to the effector, which is the muscle that produces the withdrawal. This correct order matches the second option exactly.
questions.p: For reflex action, message must start from receptor, go through sensory neurone, enter relay neurone, pass motor neurone, before e reach effector. Na the correct arrangement be that.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why damage to the cerebellum, rather than the cerebrum, would most likely cause a person to walk with a staggering, uncoordinated gait even though the person can still think and move their legs?
o: The cerebellum controls voluntary decision-making about where to walk
The cerebellum regulates body temperature which affects muscle movement
The cerebellum stores long-term memory needed for walking patterns
The cerebellum coordinates muscle activity and maintains balance and posture during movement
questions.e: The cerebellum's main job is coordinating muscle activity, balance and posture so that movements are smooth; damage to it causes jerky, uncoordinated movement even though voluntary control from the cerebrum remains intact. The other options describe functions of other brain regions, not the cerebellum.
questions.p: Na cerebellum dey help person balance body and coordinate muscle movement. If e spoil, person gait go scatter even though him brain still dey think.

questions.q: A Biology teacher in Kaduna explains that the autonomic nervous system controls involuntary activities through two divisions that usually have opposite effects on the same organs. Which of the following correctly pairs these two divisions with their typical effect on heart rate?
o: Sympathetic division slows heart rate; parasympathetic division speeds it up
Sympathetic division speeds up heart rate; parasympathetic division slows it down
Both divisions always speed up heart rate equally
Both divisions have no effect on heart rate, only on digestion
questions.e: The sympathetic division prepares the body for stress or activity by increasing heart rate, while the parasympathetic division promotes rest and digestion by slowing heart rate. These two divisions of the autonomic nervous system generally act antagonistically on the same organs.
questions.p: Sympathetic division dey make heart beat fast for emergency, while parasympathetic division dey calm am down to normal. E correct as e be.

questions.q: A student investigating the human tongue notices that different regions seem more sensitive to particular tastes. Which of the following is the correct function of taste buds found on the tongue as sense organs?
o: They contain thermoreceptor cells that detect only the temperature of food
They contain photoreceptor cells that detect light intensity on food
They contain chemoreceptor cells that detect dissolved chemical substances in food
They contain mechanoreceptor cells that detect the texture and hardness of food only
questions.e: Taste buds contain chemoreceptors that are stimulated by chemical substances dissolved in saliva, allowing the tongue to detect tastes such as sweet, sour, salty and bitter. They are not photoreceptors, mechanoreceptors or thermoreceptors, though the tongue has separate receptors for texture and temperature.
questions.p: Taste buds carry chemoreceptor cells wey dey taste any chemical substance wey melt inside food. Na true talk be that.

questions.q: A student set up two identical bean seedlings, A and B. Seedling A was kept in a box with light entering from one side only, while seedling B was kept in total darkness. After five days, seedling A bent towards the light source. Which statement best explains this observation?
o: Gibberellin moves to the lit side, causing cells there to shrink
Light directly stimulates cell division only on the illuminated side
Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, causing more elongation on that side
Auxin is destroyed on the lit side, causing faster growth there
questions.e: Light causes auxin to migrate to the shaded side of the stem, where it stimulates greater cell elongation. This uneven growth makes the shoot bend towards the light.
questions.p: Light dey make auxin move go the side wey no get light. That side go come grow long pass the other side, so the plant go bend follow the light.

questions.q: Which pair of hormones act antagonistically to regulate blood glucose level in a healthy human?
questions.e: Insulin lowers blood glucose by promoting its uptake and storage as glycogen, while glucagon raises blood glucose by stimulating glycogen breakdown. These two hormones work opposite to each other to keep blood sugar balanced.
questions.p: Insulin dey reduce sugar for blood, but glucagon dey increase am. The two of them dey work against each other to make sure say blood sugar level dey normal.

questions.q: A farmer in Jos wants to prevent fruits from dropping off his citrus trees before they are fully matured for harvest. Which class of plant hormone would most likely help him achieve this?
questions.e: Auxins help to prevent premature fruit and leaf drop by delaying the formation of the abscission layer. Spraying auxin on fruit trees is a common method of reducing fruit fall before harvest.
questions.p: Auxin dey stop fruit from fall down quick before time. E dey delay the process wey dey make fruit or leaf comot from tree.

questions.q: During puberty, a teenage boy begins to develop a deeper voice, facial hair, and increased muscle mass. Which hormone is primarily responsible for these changes?
questions.e: Testosterone, produced by the testes, is the main hormone responsible for male secondary sexual characteristics such as deepening of the voice, facial hair, and muscle growth. It becomes active in large amounts during puberty.
questions.p: Testosterone na the main hormone wey dey bring out male features for boy pikin. E dey make voice deep, grow beard, and make muscle big during puberty.

questions.q: A nursing mother in Enugu notices that her baby's sucking action stimulates further release of milk from her breast each time she breastfeeds. Which hormone is responsible for this milk let-down reflex?
questions.e: Oxytocin causes contraction of the muscle cells around the milk glands, pushing milk out during suckling. Prolactin is responsible for milk production itself, not its release.
questions.p: Oxytocin na the hormone wey dey squeeze the milk gland make milk comot when baby dey suck. Prolactin na the one wey dey produce the milk, but oxytocin na the one wey dey release am.

questions.q: A gardener notices that cutting off the terminal bud of a young hibiscus plant causes several side shoots to sprout from the lateral buds within two weeks. This observation best illustrates which hormonal phenomenon?
o: Increased gibberellin production at the cut surface stimulating root growth
Abscisic acid build-up forcing the lateral buds to become dormant
Removal of auxin inhibition, allowing cytokinin to promote lateral bud growth
Apical dominance caused by high cytokinin from the shoot tip
questions.e: The terminal bud produces auxin that normally suppresses the growth of lateral buds, a condition called apical dominance. Removing the terminal bud cuts off this auxin supply, allowing cytokinin to stimulate the lateral buds to sprout.
questions.p: The top bud dey produce auxin wey dey stop side buds from grow. If you cut the top, the auxin go finish, so the side buds go come start to grow.

questions.q: A medical test on a Nigerian adult shows unusually low levels of parathyroid hormone. Which of the following conditions is the most likely direct consequence?
questions.e: Parathyroid hormone raises blood calcium level by stimulating calcium release from bones and reabsorption by the kidneys. A low level of this hormone therefore leads to reduced blood calcium concentration.
questions.p: Parathyroid hormone dey help increase calcium for blood. If the hormone low, the calcium level for blood go come drop down.

questions.q: An agricultural extension officer treats a set of seedless grape cuttings with a plant hormone spray to promote stem and leaf growth without affecting flowering. Which hormone group is most suited to this purpose based on its known effect of stimulating cell division in shoots?
questions.e: Cytokinins specifically promote cell division, particularly in shoots and young tissues, and are widely used to encourage vegetative growth. Auxins mainly control elongation and root initiation rather than cell division in shoots.
questions.p: Cytokinins na the hormone wey dey make cell divide well for shoot. E dey help plant grow leaves and stem fast.

questions.q: Which endocrine gland in the human body is often called the 'master gland' because it secretes hormones that regulate the activities of most other endocrine glands?
questions.e: The pituitary gland produces tropic hormones that control the thyroid, adrenal cortex and gonads, so it is called the master gland. The other glands act mainly on target organs, not on other glands.
questions.p: Pituitary gland na di master gland because e dey produce hormones wey dey control other glands. Other glands no get power to control their fellow glands like pituitary.

questions.q: A student notices that a potted maize seedling placed on a windowsill bends its shoot toward the sunlight entering from one side. Which plant hormone is mainly responsible for this bending response?
questions.e: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side of the shoot, causing cells there to elongate faster than those on the lit side. This unequal growth bends the shoot toward the light source.
questions.p: Auxin dey gather for the side wey no get light, so e dey make that side grow fast pass the other side. This one come make the plant bend go where the light dey.

questions.q: A 45-year-old man visits a clinic in Lagos complaining of excessive thirst, frequent urination of large volumes of dilute urine, and constant fatigue, even though his blood glucose level is normal. Tests reveal that his kidneys are not responding properly to a certain hormone. Which hormone deficiency or malfunction best explains this condition?
questions.e: Antidiuretic hormone normally makes the kidney tubules reabsorb more water, producing small amounts of concentrated urine. When the kidneys fail to respond to it, large volumes of dilute urine are passed, a condition known as diabetes insipidus, while blood glucose remains normal, ruling out insulin problems.
questions.p: Antidiuretic hormone dey help kidney hold water so urine no go too plenty. If the hormone no work, the person go dey pass plenty water even though sugar level dey normal.

questions.q: In a controlled experiment, a plant physiologist sprays a group of young tomato plants with a hormone that causes the internodes to lengthen rapidly, producing unusually tall, thin stems compared to untreated plants of the same age. Which hormone was most likely applied?
questions.e: Gibberellins are well known for stimulating stem elongation, especially increasing the length of internodes, which makes treated plants grow taller than normal. Abscisic acid and ethylene generally inhibit growth, while auxin alone mainly affects elongation at the tip region and root initiation.
questions.p: Gibberellin na the hormone wey dey make plant stem grow long quick-quick. E dey stretch the internodes so the plant go come tall pass normal ones.

questions.q: During examination period, a student becomes unusually anxious. Her heart beats faster, her pupils widen, and blood is diverted away from her digestive system to her skeletal muscles. Which of the following correctly describes the nature of the hormone responsible for these rapid changes compared to hormones that regulate long-term processes like growth?
o: It is stored in the gland and released continuously regardless of stimulation
It acts slowly over several days and produces permanent changes in body structure
It is released directly into the digestive tract and acts only on nearby cells
It acts rapidly, travels in the blood, and produces short-lived widespread effects that quickly reverse once the stressor is removed
questions.e: Adrenaline is released quickly in response to stress, travels through the blood to many organs at once, and its effects fade rapidly once the threat is gone. This is different from slow, long-term acting hormones such as growth hormone, which produce gradual, lasting structural changes.
questions.p: Adrenaline dey rush enter blood quick when person fear or get stress. E dey make body react fast, but once the fear finish, everything go come back to normal.

questions.q: A horticulturist in Jos wants to prevent the seeds in a batch of stored tomatoes from germinating prematurely before the rainy season. Which naturally occurring plant hormone, when present in high concentration in the seed, helps to maintain seed dormancy under these conditions?
questions.e: Abscisic acid is the hormone mainly responsible for maintaining dormancy in seeds and buds, preventing germination until conditions such as adequate water and temperature are favourable. Gibberellin actually promotes germination, which is the opposite effect needed here.
questions.p: Abscisic acid na the hormone wey dey make seed sleep and no germinate quick. E dey keep the seed dormant until the time wey rain come.

questions.q: A plant scientist removes the shoot tip from a young bean seedling and then applies a paste containing a synthetic hormone to the cut surface. He observes that root formation is stimulated at the base of a separate stem cutting treated with the same hormone. Based on this observation, which hormone is most likely present in the paste and what is its main classical role in whole plants?
o: Abscisic acid; it closes stomata during water stress
Cytokinin; it delays leaf senescence only
Auxin; it promotes cell elongation and stimulates root initiation in cuttings
Ethylene; it ripens fruits and promotes leaf fall
questions.e: Auxin is widely used commercially as rooting powder because it stimulates root initiation at the cut end of stem cuttings, in addition to its classical role in promoting cell elongation at the shoot tip. The other hormones listed have different primary functions unrelated to stimulating root formation in cuttings.
questions.p: Auxin na the hormone wey dem dey use for rooting powder to make stem grow roots. Apart from that, e still dey help plant stem grow long.

questions.q: A community of living organisms interacting with one another and with their non-living environment, with a continuous exchange of matter and energy, is best described as a/an:
questions.e: An ecosystem includes both living things and their physical surroundings interacting together. A population is only organisms of one species, while a habitat is just the place where an organism lives.
questions.p: Ecosystem na where living things and non-living things dey jam and interact together. Population na just one kind species alone, and habitat na just the place wey organism dey stay.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs correctly matches an ecological term with its correct meaning?
o: Habitat - the specific place where an organism normally lives
Biotic factor - rainfall amount in a habitat
Population - all the different species living in a forest
Abiotic factor - predation between a lion and an antelope
questions.e: A habitat is the natural place where an organism lives and can find its needs. Rainfall is abiotic, predation is a biotic interaction, and a population refers to one species, not many.
questions.p: Habitat na the correct natural place where organism dey normally live and find wetin e need. Rainfall na abiotic, predation na biotic, and population na for just one species, no be plenty species.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why only about 10% of energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next in an ecosystem?
o: Producers absorb most of the sun's energy before releasing any
Organisms use most of the energy for respiration, movement and heat loss
Consumers deliberately store excess energy without using it
Decomposers destroy energy before it reaches the next trophic level
questions.e: Energy is lost mainly as heat during respiration and through activities like movement and growth, so only a small fraction remains to be passed to the next feeding level. This is why food chains rarely have more than four or five trophic levels.
questions.p: Energy dey loss as heat when organism dey do respiration, move around, and grow. Na small fraction remain to pass go next level, dat is why food chain no dey pass four or five levels.

questions.q: In a Nigerian mangrove swamp ecosystem, algae are eaten by small crabs, which are eaten by mudskippers, which are eaten by herons. If the algae contain 20,000 kJ of energy and each trophic transfer follows the ten percent efficiency rule, approximately how much energy is available to the herons?
questions.e: Applying ten percent efficiency three times: crabs get 2,000 kJ, mudskippers get 200 kJ, and herons get 20 kJ. Each step loses ninety percent of the energy as heat and other losses.
questions.p: If we apply ten percent rule three times, crab go get 2,000 kJ, mudskipper go get 200 kJ, and heron go get 20 kJ. Every step dey lose ninety percent of the energy as heat.

questions.q: A food web in a Jos Plateau grassland includes grasses, grasshoppers, rats, snakes, hawks and lizards, with snakes and lizards both feeding on rats, and hawks feeding on both snakes and lizards. If a disease eliminates all rats in this web, which statement best describes the likely outcome?
o: Snakes and lizards will immediately go extinct since rats are their only food
Grasshoppers will decrease because rats no longer compete with them for grass
Snakes and lizards may survive by relying more on other available prey
Hawks will starve completely as they have no other source of food
questions.e: A food web has multiple feeding links, so when rats disappear, snakes and lizards can switch to other prey available in the web, unlike in a simple food chain. This flexibility makes food webs more stable than single food chains during disturbances.
questions.p: Because food web get plenty different food links, if rat vanish, snakes and lizards fit chop another prey. Dat flexibility make food web stable pass ordinary single food chain.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly distinguishes the flow of energy from the cycling of nutrients in an ecosystem?
o: Energy flows in one direction while nutrients are recycled repeatedly
Both energy and nutrients are recycled repeatedly within the ecosystem
Both energy and nutrients flow in one direction and are lost to space
Nutrients flow in one direction while energy is recycled repeatedly
questions.e: Energy enters an ecosystem from sunlight, passes through trophic levels, and is eventually lost as heat, so it cannot be reused. Nutrients like carbon and nitrogen, however, are used by organisms and returned to the environment through decomposition, allowing them to be reused repeatedly.
questions.p: Energy dey enter from sun, pass through levels, and comot as heat, so e no dey cycle back. But nutrients like carbon and nitrogen dey circulate round and round through decomposition.

questions.q: Which of the following is the correct trophic level classification of a hawk that feeds only on snakes which feed only on rats which feed only on grasshoppers that eat grass?
questions.e: Grass is the producer, grasshopper is primary consumer, rat is secondary consumer, snake is tertiary consumer, so the hawk that eats the snake is the quaternary consumer. Counting each feeding step carefully gives this answer.
questions.p: Grass na producer, grasshopper na primary consumer, rat na secondary consumer, snake na tertiary consumer, so hawk wey chop snake na quaternary consumer. When you count well well, you go see say na dis answer correct.

questions.q: A particular ecosystem is said to be self-sustaining mainly because it contains organisms that can:
o: Store large amounts of water in their body tissues
Trap and convert solar energy into chemical energy usable by other organisms
Migrate to other habitats when conditions become unfavourable
Reproduce very rapidly to replace members lost to predation
questions.e: Producers such as green plants trap sunlight and convert it into chemical energy through photosynthesis, which then supports all other organisms in the ecosystem. This ability to fix energy makes the ecosystem self-sustaining.
questions.p: Green plants wey be producers dey trap sunlight make dem turn am to chemical energy through photosynthesis, and dis energy dey support all other animals for inside the ecosystem. Na dis ability to make energy dey make the ecosystem self-sustaining.

questions.q: In a lake ecosystem, which of the following correctly lists components that would be classified together as the abiotic factors of the habitat?
o: Fish, algae, bacteria and water snails
Dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH and light intensity
questions.e: Abiotic factors are the non-living physical and chemical components of an environment, such as dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH and light intensity. The other options list living organisms, which are biotic factors.
questions.p: Abiotic factors na non-living physical and chemical things for environment, like dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH and light intensity. Other options na living things wey be biotic factors.

questions.q: A biology student studying a cocoa plantation in Ondo State recorded the following feeding relationships: cocoa leaves are eaten by leaf-eating caterpillars and by aphids; caterpillars are eaten by birds and by predatory wasps; aphids are eaten by ladybirds and by birds; birds are eaten by snakes. Which single statement below is best supported by this information?
o: Only one food chain exists in this habitat since all organisms depend on cocoa leaves
The organisms described form a food web because several interlinked food chains share common organisms
Birds occupy the same trophic level as snakes in this habitat
Ladybirds and predatory wasps must belong to the same species since they both feed on pests
questions.e: Since caterpillars, aphids and birds each have more than one feeding link, the separate food chains interconnect to form a food web. A food web simply shows many overlapping food chains in one community.
questions.p: Since caterpillars, aphids and birds get more than one way to chop food, the food chains join body to form food web. Food web just mean plenty food chains wey dey overlap for one community.

questions.q: The diagram of a pyramid of biomass for a particular pond was found to be inverted (narrow at the base, wider at higher levels). Which situation would best produce such a result?
o: A small mass of phytoplankton supporting a much larger mass of slow-reproducing zooplankton feeding heavily on them at any instant
Equal biomass existing at every trophic level in the pond
A large population of tiny, fast-reproducing phytoplankton supporting a smaller mass of bigger zooplankton
Producers having a longer lifespan than the consumers feeding on them
questions.e: An inverted pyramid of biomass occurs when small, fast-reproducing producers have low standing biomass at any moment but still support a larger standing biomass of longer-lived consumers. This is common in aquatic ecosystems where phytoplankton turnover is rapid.
questions.p: Inverted pyramid of biomass dey happen when small producers wey dey reproduce fast get small biomass for one moment but still fit support bigger biomass of consumers wey dey live longer. Dis one dey common for inside water environments.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes what happens to the energy that is not passed on to the next trophic level in a food chain?
o: It is transferred directly to decomposers without being used
It is converted into new biomass by the next consumer
It is lost mainly as heat through respiration, and used for movement and other life processes
It accumulates permanently in the bodies of producers
questions.e: Most of the energy at each trophic level is used up in respiration, movement, growth maintenance and other activities, and is lost as heat. Only a small fraction, about ten percent, is stored in biomass and passed to the next level.
questions.p: Ede energy wey dey each level, na im dem dey use for respiration, movement and other body work, and e dey komot as heat. Na only small part, like ten percent, dey enter the next level.

questions.q: In an ecological study of a forest reserve near Enugu, a researcher wants to represent an ecological pyramid that will NEVER appear inverted regardless of the ecosystem studied. Which type of ecological pyramid should the researcher use?
questions.e: The pyramid of energy is always upright because energy decreases progressively at each successive trophic level due to losses during respiration. Pyramids of numbers and biomass can sometimes be inverted depending on organism size and reproduction rate.
questions.p: Pyramid of energy dey always stand upright because energy dey reduce as e dey go high due to loss during respiration. Pyramids of numbers and biomass fit sometimes turn upside down depending on size and how dem dey born.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the role of decomposers in the flow of energy and matter within an ecosystem?
o: They occupy the topmost trophic level and therefore receive the largest share of energy
They store the total energy of an ecosystem permanently without releasing it
They manufacture new organic energy from inorganic materials for producers to use
They break down dead organisms and waste, releasing nutrients back to the soil while energy is lost as heat
questions.e: Decomposers break down dead matter and waste products, recycling nutrients like nitrogen and carbon back into the soil for producers to reuse, while the chemical energy in the matter is released as heat during respiration. This shows that nutrients cycle but energy does not, it is eventually lost from the system.
questions.p: Decomposers dey break down dead things and waste, return nutrients like nitrogen and carbon back to soil, while energy dey komot as heat. Dis one show say nutrients dey cycle round but energy dey loss.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the process of ammonification in the nitrogen cycle?
o: Nitrites are oxidised into nitrates by soil bacteria
Decomposers break down dead organisms and waste products, releasing ammonia into the soil
Plants absorb nitrates through their root hairs for protein synthesis
Bacteria convert atmospheric nitrogen gas into ammonia within root nodules
questions.e: Ammonification is the breakdown of proteins and other nitrogenous waste in dead organisms by decomposers, which releases ammonia into the soil. This is different from nitrogen fixation, nitrification, or nitrate absorption.
questions.p: Ammonification na wen decomposers break down dead tins and waste to release ammonia for soil. E different from nitrogen fixation or nitrification.

questions.q: In the carbon cycle, which pair of processes together ensures a continuous exchange of carbon dioxide between living organisms and the atmosphere?
questions.e: Photosynthesis removes carbon dioxide from the air to make organic compounds, while respiration returns it to the atmosphere. These two opposite processes form the main short-term cycling of carbon between organisms and their environment.
questions.p: Photosynthesis dey remove carbon dioxide from air, while respiration dey put am back. Dis two process dey make sure say carbon dey cycle between living tins and atmosphere.

questions.q: A pond in Oyo State receives runoff from a nearby poultry farm, and after some weeks, the water turns green and cloudy with a sharp drop in dissolved oxygen at night. Which sequence correctly explains this observation?
o: Excess nutrients cause algal bloom, algae later die and decompose, and decomposer bacteria use up oxygen
Nitrogen fixation increases, raising oxygen demand by legumes in the water
Increased carbon dioxide from respiration directly poisons the fish
Reduced sunlight penetration stops transpiration in pond organisms
questions.e: Nutrient-rich runoff causes algae to multiply rapidly (eutrophication); when they die, decomposers break them down and consume large amounts of oxygen, lowering dissolved oxygen especially at night when photosynthesis stops. The other options describe unrelated or incorrect mechanisms.
questions.p: Excess nutrients from farm dey make algae grow too much. Wen dem die, bacteria dey use oxygen break dem down, wey come make oxygen finish for water.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes the role of nitrogen-fixing bacteria found freely in the soil, such as Azotobacter, compared with those in root nodules?
o: They oxidise ammonia into nitrites for plant uptake
They depend entirely on legume roots for oxygen and nutrients to survive
They fix atmospheric nitrogen into compounds without living inside a host plant's roots
They convert nitrates back into atmospheric nitrogen gas
questions.e: Free-living bacteria like Azotobacter fix nitrogen directly in the soil independently, unlike symbiotic bacteria such as Rhizobium that live inside legume root nodules. This distinguishes free-living fixers from symbiotic nitrogen fixers.
questions.p: Free-living bacteria like Azotobacter dey fix nitrogen for soil by demsef. Dem no need plant root like Rhizobium wey dey live inside legume nodules.

questions.q: A student compares two farmlands in Benue State: one is heavily tilled and left bare after harvest, while the other retains crop residue as mulch. After heavy rainfall, the bare field shows more soil loss and reduced water infiltration. Which role of the water cycle best explains the better water retention in the mulched field?
o: Mulch prevents precipitation from reaching the soil surface
Mulch increases the rate of transpiration from exposed soil surfaces
Mulch speeds up condensation of water vapour above the field
Mulch reduces surface runoff and allows more water to infiltrate into the soil before evaporation
questions.e: Mulch cover reduces the speed of surface runoff and shields soil from direct sun, allowing more rainwater to infiltrate and be retained rather than being lost through evaporation or erosion. This improves water availability in the soil for plant use.
questions.p: Mulch dey stop water from running comot quick and e dey cover soil from sun. Dis one dey help water soak inside ground well well instead of evaporating.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why pH is considered an important ecological factor for organisms living in a freshwater stream?
o: It affects the solubility and availability of nutrients and the activity of enzymes in aquatic organisms
It determines the amount of dissolved oxygen produced by photosynthesis alone
It measures the depth to which light can penetrate the water
It controls the rate of transpiration of aquatic plants directly
questions.e: pH affects how soluble certain nutrients and minerals are, and extreme pH values can disrupt enzyme activity in organisms, making it a key ecological factor. It is not a direct measure of oxygen production, transpiration, or light penetration.
questions.p: pH dey affect how nutrients dey dissolve for water and e fit disturb enzyme work inside body of aquatic organisms. E be very important factor for how dem dey survive.

questions.q: A group of students studying an abandoned quarry site in Enugu notice that lichens first colonise bare rocks, followed later by mosses, then small herbs, and eventually shrubs over several years. Which ecological concept does this sequence best illustrate?
questions.e: The gradual, predictable replacement of one community of organisms by another over time, starting from bare rock, is called ecological succession, specifically primary succession. This is distinct from carbon fixation, leaching, or eutrophication, which describe different processes.
questions.p: Dis gradual change from lichens to shrubs for bare rock na wetin we dey call ecological succession. E be predictable process where one community dey replace anoda one over time.

questions.q: Which of the following correctly represents the sequence by which carbon locked in dead plant and animal remains is eventually converted into fossil fuels over long geological periods?
o: Fermentation of dead matter by yeast followed by immediate release as methane gas
Respiration, combustion, then photosynthesis acting over a few decades
Direct absorption of carbon dioxide by rocks through weathering within a few years
Decomposition, compaction and burial under sediment, then heat and pressure acting over millions of years
questions.e: Fossil fuels form when dead organisms are buried under layers of sediment and subjected to intense heat and pressure over millions of years, converting the trapped carbon into coal, oil or natural gas. The other options describe short, unrelated processes that do not lead to fossil fuel formation.
questions.p: Fossil fuel dey form when dead plants and animals bury under sediment for millions of years. Heat and pressure come change the carbon inside them to coal or oil. Other options no get sense for how fossil fuel dey form.

questions.q: A biology class in Jos set up two identical plastic bottles containing moist soil. Bottle X was sealed and left undisturbed, while Bottle Y was left open to the air. After two weeks, Bottle Y showed a higher rate of nitrate production in the soil than Bottle X. What is the most likely explanation for this difference?
o: Bottle Y lost water faster, which directly produces nitrates
Bottle Y allowed oxygen to reach nitrifying bacteria, which require it for converting ammonia to nitrates
Bottle X contained more nitrogen gas, which bacteria used directly to form nitrates
Bottle X received more sunlight, which sped up nitrification
questions.e: Nitrification is carried out by aerobic bacteria that need oxygen to oxidise ammonia into nitrites and then nitrates. Since Bottle Y was open to air, it had more oxygen available, allowing nitrifying bacteria to work more effectively than in the sealed Bottle X.
questions.p: Nitrifying bacteria need oxygen to change ammonia to nitrate. Because Bottle Y open to air, oxygen dey enter well well for them to work. Bottle X no get enough oxygen so the bacteria no fit work well.

questions.q: Two identical beakers of pond water are placed under the same light intensity. Beaker P is kept at 15°C while Beaker Q is kept at 35°C. After one hour, the algae in Beaker Q show a much higher rate of photosynthesis than those in Beaker P, up to an optimum point. Which ecological factor best explains this observation?
o: Light intensity, because warmer water transmits light faster
Humidity, because it is higher in warmer beakers
Temperature, because it affects the rate of enzyme-controlled reactions in photosynthesis
Wind speed, because it increases with temperature
questions.e: Temperature affects the activity of enzymes involved in photosynthesis, so a rise in temperature (up to an optimum) increases the rate of the reaction. Light intensity was kept constant in both beakers, so it cannot explain the difference seen.
questions.p: Temperature dey control how fast enzymes work for photosynthesis. When temperature increase, the reaction rate go increase until e reach the best point. Light intensity no change, so na temperature cause the difference.

questions.q: A population of tilapia in a fish pond at Oyo town was observed to increase slowly at first, then rapidly, and finally level off as food and space became limited, producing an S-shaped curve when plotted against time. What is this levelling-off value called?
questions.e: The point where population growth flattens out due to limited resources is the carrying capacity of the environment. It represents the maximum population the habitat can support.
questions.p: Di point wey population growth stop to increase sake of say food and space don finish na carrying capacity. E show di maximum number of animals wey dat place fit support.

questions.q: Which pair of factors correctly groups a density-independent and a density-dependent factor affecting a population of grasshoppers in a maize farm?
questions.e: Bush fire affects the population regardless of its size, making it density-independent, while predation intensifies as population size increases, making it density-dependent. The other pairs do not correctly separate the two categories.
questions.p: Bush fire no send weda grasshopper plenty or small, so e be density-independent. But predation dey increase as di population dey grow, so e be density-dependent.

questions.q: In the Guinea savanna region of Nigeria, grasses grow tall and form the dominant vegetation while trees are scattered and fire-resistant. Which feature best helps these savanna trees survive the annual bush fires common in the region?
o: Thin, smooth bark and shallow roots
Thick, corky bark and underground rootstocks
Buttress roots and thin waxy leaves
questions.e: Thick corky bark insulates the stem from fire damage, while underground rootstocks allow the tree to resprout after a fire destroys the above-ground parts. This is a common adaptation of savanna trees to recurrent bush fires.
questions.p: Thick corky bark dey protect di tree stem from fire. If fire burn di top, di underground rootstocks go still fit grow new branches again.

questions.q: A class of SS3 students sampled a 100 square metre plot of guinea savanna grassland in Kaduna State and counted 40 individual Andropogon grass plants. If the total grassland area being studied covers 5000 square metres, what is the estimated total number of Andropogon plants in the entire area?
questions.e: Density in the sample is 40 plants per 100 square metres, which is 0.4 plants per square metre. Multiplying 0.4 by the total area of 5000 square metres gives an estimated 2000 plants.
questions.p: If 40 plants dey for 100 square metres, e mean say 0.4 plants dey for one square metre. When you multiply 0.4 by 5000, you go get 2000 plants.

questions.q: Which of the following best distinguishes the tropical rainforest biome from the Guinea savanna biome in Nigeria in terms of vegetation structure?
o: Rainforest has stratified layers with a closed canopy while savanna has scattered trees in grassland
Rainforest trees are fire-resistant while savanna trees are not
Rainforest has a continuous grass layer while savanna has a closed canopy
Rainforest has fewer plant species than savanna
questions.e: The rainforest is characterised by distinct layers of vegetation, including emergent trees, canopy, and undergrowth, forming a closed canopy that blocks sunlight. The savanna, by contrast, has an open structure with scattered trees among continuous grass cover.
questions.p: Rainforest get many layers of trees wey join body form closed canopy. Savanna na open grassland wey get small-small trees scattered inside.

questions.q: A population ecologist found that a community of weaverbirds and a community of sunbirds in a Nigerian forest reserve both feed on the same type of insect found on flowering trees, leading to a reduction in food available to both species. This relationship is an example of which ecological interaction?
questions.e: Two different species competing for the same limited resource, in this case insects, is interspecific competition. Neither species benefits from the other; instead both are negatively affected by the shared demand for food.
questions.p: When two different species dey fight for di same food, we dey call am interspecific competition. Both of dem no gain anything, na stress e dey cause for both sides.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why population growth in a natural habitat eventually slows down and stabilizes rather than increasing indefinitely in an exponential manner?
o: Environmental resistance from limited resources, predation, and disease checks further increase
Migration always balances birth and death rates exactly
Natality permanently exceeds mortality in all seasons
Unlimited food supply and absence of predators allow continuous growth
questions.e: As a population grows, environmental resistance factors such as limited food, space, predation, and disease increase and reduce the rate of growth until it stabilises near the carrying capacity. Without such resistance, populations would grow exponentially forever, which does not happen in nature.
questions.p: As population dey grow, things like lack of food, sickness, and predators go start to limit dem. Dis environmental resistance na wetin dey make population growth stop to increase anyhow.

questions.q: A population of weevils was introduced into a sealed container of stored grain with no predators and unlimited food initially. Over 10 weeks, the population grew, overshot the carrying capacity of the grain supply, and then crashed sharply due to food exhaustion and waste accumulation. This type of growth curve is best described as
questions.e: A population that grows rapidly without levelling off at the carrying capacity, then crashes suddenly, follows a J-shaped curve typical of organisms without effective limiting controls until resources suddenly run out. The S-shaped curve instead shows a smooth levelling off, which did not happen here.
questions.p: Population wey grow quick-quick without stopping for carrying capacity and come crash down sharp-sharp dey follow J-shaped curve. E happen when limiting factors no dey until food finish scatter.

questions.q: In a Nigerian derived savanna ecosystem, biologists noticed that as the population of grasscutters increased, an outbreak of a contagious fungal disease spread quickly through the dense population, killing many individuals and reducing the population size. This factor regulating the population is best classified as
questions.e: Disease spreads faster and has greater effect when population density is high because individuals are closer together, making it a density-dependent factor. Its impact changes with population size, unlike density-independent factors such as weather.
questions.p: Sickness dey spread fast and kill people well well when population high because everybody dey close to body. Na density-dependent factor be that, unlike weather wey no send.

questions.q: Camels found in the semi-arid Sahel region of northern Nigeria possess broad, flat feet, the ability to tolerate large changes in body temperature, and the capacity to produce dry concentrated faeces. These features are examples of
o: physiological and structural adaptations to a hot, dry environment
questions.e: Broad feet (structural) and tolerance to temperature changes with reduced water loss in faeces (physiological) are both adaptations that help camels survive hot, dry conditions with scarce water. These are not related to migration, competition, or reproduction directly.
questions.p: Wide leg na structural adaptation, while body temperature control and dry shit na physiological adaptation. Dem all help camel survive hot dry area where water scarce.

questions.q: A forestry student wants to estimate the population density of a slow-moving land snail species in a 2000 square metre section of a Nigerian rainforest reserve. Using ten 5 metre by 5 metre quadrats randomly placed within the area, she counts a total of 60 snails across all quadrats. What is the estimated population density of the snail species per square metre?
questions.e: Each quadrat covers 25 square metres, so 10 quadrats cover 250 square metres in total. Density equals total count divided by total sampled area, which is 60 divided by 250, giving 0.24 snails per square metre.
questions.p: Ten quadrats wey be 5m by 5m each go give total area of 250 square metres. If you divide the 60 snails by 250 square metres, you go get 0.24 snails per square metre.

questions.q: The main vegetation zones of Nigeria, arranged from the coast in the south to the far north, follow which correct sequence?
o: Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna, tropical rainforest, mangrove swamp
Guinea savanna, mangrove swamp, tropical rainforest, Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna
Tropical rainforest, mangrove swamp, Sahel savanna, Sudan savanna, Guinea savanna
Mangrove swamp, tropical rainforest, Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, Sahel savanna
questions.e: Moving from the coast northward, Nigeria's vegetation changes from mangrove swamp forest along the coast, through tropical rainforest, into Guinea savanna, then Sudan savanna, and finally Sahel savanna in the extreme north. This order reflects decreasing rainfall from south to north.
questions.p: As person dey move from south coast go far north for Nigeria, vegetation dey change from mangrove swamp go tropical rainforest, enter Guinea savanna, Sudan savanna, and finally Sahel savanna.

questions.q: Two species of insectivorous birds in a forest reserve near Enugu feed on the same type of insect found in tree bark. Over several seasons, one species shifted to feeding mainly at the top of the canopy while the other remained near the forest floor, reducing direct competition between them. This outcome is best described as a result of
questions.e: When two species compete for the same limited resource, they may evolve to use different parts of the habitat or different resources, a process called resource partitioning, which reduces competition. This is different from mutualism, predation, or commensalism, which involve different types of relationships.
questions.p: When two animals dey fight for same food, dem fit divide their territory so dem no go dey jam wahala again. Na wet dem dey call resource partitioning.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes a key structural feature of trees in the tropical rainforest biome of southern Nigeria?
o: Trees have thick, water-storing stems and reduced leaves to survive long dry seasons
Trees are short, widely spaced, and have thick corky bark to resist annual bush fires
Trees shed all their leaves simultaneously each year to conserve water during drought
Trees form a multi-layered canopy with broad leaves and buttress roots for support in shallow, moist soils
questions.e: Tropical rainforest trees typically grow tall with broad leaves to capture sunlight under heavy competition, forming distinct canopy layers, and develop buttress roots because the soil is often shallow and waterlogged. The other options describe adaptations more typical of savanna or desert plants facing drought or fire.
questions.p: Rainforest trees dey grow tall with broad leaves and buttress roots because soil shallow and rain plenty. Na so dem dey struggle for sunlight.

questions.q: In a controlled laboratory experiment, a population of fruit flies was allowed to grow in a bottle with a fixed amount of food and no removal of waste. The population size was recorded weekly and plotted on a graph against time. Which feature of the resulting graph would confirm that the population had reached its carrying capacity for that bottle?
o: A sudden population crash to zero immediately after the peak
A continuous steep rise in population size with no sign of slowing
A levelling off of the curve where population size remains fairly constant over time
A population size that fluctuates wildly with no clear pattern
questions.e: Carrying capacity is reached when the environment can no longer support further growth, so the population size stabilises and the graph flattens out into a plateau. A continuous rise or sudden crash would instead show that carrying capacity has not been reached or has been exceeded.
questions.p: Carrying capacity mean say environment don reach im limit, so population size go come stable and flat for graph. E no go increase again or crash anyhow.

questions.q: A chemical factory in Kano discharges heated water used for cooling machines directly into a nearby stream. Fishermen later notice fewer fish species and reduced dissolved oxygen in the stream. This type of pollution is best described as
questions.e: Thermal pollution occurs when hot water from industries is released into water bodies, raising the temperature and lowering the amount of dissolved oxygen available to aquatic organisms. This differs from eutrophication, which is caused by excess nutrients, not heat.
questions.p: Thermal pollution dey happen when hot water enter river and make the temperature high, con reduce oxygen wey fish need to breathe. E different from eutrophication wey nutrient surplus dey cause.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why excessive use of chemical fertilizers on farmland, rather than organic manure, can degrade soil quality over a long period?
o: Fertilizers prevent leaching of nutrients into underground water
Fertilizers alter soil pH and kill beneficial soil microorganisms over time
Fertilizers increase soil organic matter and improve water retention
Fertilizers increase the population of earthworms and decomposers
questions.e: Continuous use of chemical fertilizers can make the soil too acidic or too alkaline, which harms useful soil microorganisms needed for decomposition and nutrient cycling. Organic manure, unlike chemical fertilizer, adds organic matter and supports microbial life.
questions.p: If person too use chemical fertilizer, e dey spoil soil pH and kill better microorganisms wey suppose help soil. Organic manure better because e dey add organic matter and help soil life.

questions.q: A town council in Enugu plans to reduce the volume of solid waste sent to landfill sites while also generating useful products from the waste. Which of the following waste management methods best achieves BOTH goals?
o: Incineration of all waste without separation
Open dumping of refuse at the outskirts of town
Composting of biodegradable waste to produce manure
Burying all waste types together in deep pits
questions.e: Composting breaks down biodegradable waste like food remains and plant matter into useful manure, reducing landfill volume while producing a beneficial product. Open dumping and mixed burial do not reduce waste volume meaningfully or produce useful output.
questions.p: Composting na to turn biodegradable waste to manure, wey dey reduce rubbish for landfill and still give farmers useful product. Open dumping no dey help reduce waste at all.

questions.q: In a game reserve, wildlife officers set a fixed maximum number of animals that can be legally hunted or harvested each year without causing the population to decline. This conservation practice is known as
questions.e: A quota system limits the number of animals or resources that can be harvested within a period, ensuring the population is not overexploited and can regenerate. The other options relate to soil and forest management, not hunting limits.
questions.p: Quota system na the fixed limit wey law set for how many animals dem fit hunt make the population no finish. Other options na for soil and trees, no be hunting limits.

questions.q: A lake used for irrigation has become heavily contaminated with lead from a nearby battery recycling plant. A scientist wants to determine if the lead has entered the food chain and is becoming more concentrated at higher trophic levels. Which organisms should be compared to best test this?
o: Soil samples from farmland far away from the lake
Small fish that feed on algae and large fish that feed on small fish
Algae and water at the lake surface only
Two samples of water taken from different parts of the lake
questions.e: To show biomagnification, one must compare organisms at increasing trophic levels, such as small fish and the larger fish that eat them, to see if the toxin concentration increases up the food chain. Comparing only water samples or distant soil would not reveal this trophic pattern.
questions.p: To check biomagnification, you need to compare small fish and big fish wey chop them to see how poison dey increase for body as food chain go high. Ordinary water sample no go show am.

questions.q: Which of the following is a major reason why mangrove swamps along the Nigerian coastline are considered important natural resources that must be conserved?
o: They serve as breeding grounds for fish and protect the coast from erosion
They produce large quantities of crude oil for export
They increase the salinity of nearby farmland, improving crop yield
They prevent all forms of rainfall from reaching the coastal region
questions.e: Mangrove swamps act as nurseries for many fish and aquatic species and their root systems hold the soil together, reducing coastal erosion. They are not a source of crude oil, and increased salinity would harm, not help, most crops.
questions.p: Mangrove swamp important because e be house where fish dey born and e dey protect coast from erosion. E no get anything to do with crude oil or spoiling farm crops.

questions.q: An industrial estate in Lagos wants to reduce the amount of particulate matter and toxic gases released into the air from its factories. Which of the following measures would most directly achieve this goal?
o: Increasing the height of chimneys without treating the gases
Reducing the number of trees planted around the factories
Relocating factories closer to residential areas
Fitting scrubbers and filters to chimneys before gases are released
questions.e: Scrubbers and filters trap particulate matter and harmful gases before they leave the chimney, directly reducing air pollution. Simply raising chimney height only spreads pollutants over a wider area instead of removing them.
questions.p: To put scrubbers and filters for chimney na direct way to catch bad gas and particles before dem enter air. Just making chimney tall only carry the smoke go far place.

questions.q: A community in the Niger Delta relies on a freshwater swamp for fishing and farming. Over several years, waste from a nearby factory causes the swamp to lose most of its fish species and plant diversity. This loss of variety of living organisms in the swamp is best described as a decline in
questions.e: Biodiversity refers to the variety of living organisms (plants, animals and microbes) in an area. A fall in the number of different species in the swamp shows reduced biodiversity, not the other listed terms.
questions.p: Biodiversity na the different different living things like plants and animals wey dey one place. When the fish and plants dey die finish because of waste, e mean say biodiversity don drop.

questions.q: A government agency wants to reduce air pollution from vehicle exhausts in a busy Nigerian city. Which measure would most directly reduce the amount of pollutant gases released by cars into the atmosphere?
o: Widening roads to reduce traffic jams only
Fitting vehicles with catalytic converters and enforcing use of unleaded fuel
Increasing the number of fuel stations in the city
questions.e: Catalytic converters change harmful exhaust gases into less harmful substances before they leave the vehicle, and unleaded fuel reduces lead pollution. The other options may ease traffic but do not directly cut the pollutant content of exhaust gases.
questions.p: Catalytic converter dey help change bad gas wey motor dey bring out to better gas before e enter air. Again, unleaded fuel dey stop lead pollution well well.

questions.q: In a certain forest reserve, selective logging is practised such that only matured trees of a particular girth size are cut, while young trees are left to grow and replace the harvested ones. This forestry practice is an example of
questions.e: Sustainable yield management means harvesting a resource at a rate that allows it to replenish itself naturally, which is exactly what selective logging of matured trees achieves. Afforestation means planting new trees, while deforestation and shifting cultivation involve clearing land rather than careful harvesting.
questions.p: Sustainable yield management na when you chop or cut tree for way wey go make ground still grow new ones back. E make sure say timber no finish for forest.

questions.q: A borehole in a farming settlement is found to contain excess nitrate from fertilizer runoff. Long term consumption of this water is of particular health concern for which group of people?
o: Infants, because nitrate can be converted to a compound that interferes with oxygen transport in their blood
Adult men, due to their larger body mass
Elderly farmers who drink little water
questions.e: In infants, nitrate in water can be reduced to nitrite in the gut, which converts haemoglobin to methaemoglobin that cannot carry oxygen properly, a condition called blue baby syndrome. Adults and older children are less affected because their digestive systems handle nitrate differently.
questions.p: Small pikin body fit turn nitrate to something wey go stop oxygen from moving well for their blood. Naim make water wey get plenty nitrate dangerous for babies.

questions.q: An environmental scientist studying a river downstream of a tannery notices that fish have disappeared, the water has an unpleasant smell, and chromium compounds used in leather processing are present in the sediment. Which type of pollution is primarily responsible for this observation?
questions.e: Chromium compounds discharged from tannery operations are industrial chemical pollutants that poison aquatic life and contaminate sediment, matching the described effects. Thermal, noise and radioactive pollution would not specifically introduce chromium compounds into the river.
questions.p: Chromium poison from leather factory na chemical pollution wey dey spoil water and kill fish. Na industrial waste cause this kind wahala for river.

questions.q: A wildlife park in Nigeria fences off a section of natural habitat, allows animals to roam freely within it, and controls human activities such as farming and logging inside the protected area while still keeping the animals in their natural environment. This method of conservation is called
o: captive breeding in a botanical garden
in-situ conservation using a game reserve
questions.e: In-situ conservation protects organisms within their natural habitat, and a game reserve that restricts harmful human activities while keeping animals in their original environment fits this definition. Ex-situ methods like zoos, seed banks and botanical gardens remove organisms from their natural habitat, which is not the case here.
questions.p: In-situ conservation na to protect animals and plants inside their own natural house like game reserve. E different from zoo where dem carry dem go another place.

questions.q: In tomato plants, tallness (T) is dominant over dwarfness (t). A tall tomato plant of unknown genotype was crossed with a dwarf plant, and the offspring were 48 tall and 52 dwarf plants. What is the genotype of the tall parent?
questions.e: A ratio close to 1 tall to 1 dwarf shows a test cross result. This only happens when the tall parent is heterozygous (Tt) crossed with tt.
questions.p: If you get about 1 tall to 1 dwarf for your pikin them, na test cross be that. E mean say the tall papa or mama na Tt, wey you cross with tt.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why a cross between two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt x Tt) produces offspring in the ratio of 3 tall to 1 dwarf?
o: Three out of four possible allele combinations contain at least one dominant allele
The dwarf allele is lost during fertilisation
The dominant allele doubles its effect in the heterozygous condition
Tallness and dwarfness blend to form intermediate plants
questions.e: The possible combinations from Tt x Tt are TT, Tt, Tt and tt. Three of these four combinations carry at least one dominant T allele, giving tall plants, while only tt is dwarf.
questions.p: Na TT, Tt, Tt and tt you go get when you cross Tt and Tt. Three out of these four join-join get at least one dominant T allele, na why you get 3 tall to 1 dwarf.

questions.q: A Nigerian farmer crosses a pure-breeding black-feathered chicken with a pure-breeding white-feathered chicken, and all the offspring have grey feathers, a colour between black and white. What type of gene action best explains this result?
questions.e: When the heterozygous offspring show a blended phenotype that is intermediate between both parents, this is called incomplete dominance. Neither allele completely masks the other.
questions.p: If black and white mating produce grey wey dey middle, na incomplete dominance be that. None of the allele fit cover the other one fully, so dem blend together.

questions.q: In a dihybrid cross between two pea plants heterozygous for seed colour and seed texture (YyRr x YyRr), what fraction of the offspring is expected to be homozygous recessive for both traits?
questions.e: A dihybrid cross gives a 9:3:3:1 ratio out of 16 total offspring. The genotype yyrr, which is homozygous recessive for both traits, makes up only 1 part out of the 16.
questions.p: For dihybrid cross, the last one for 9:3:3:1 ratio na yyrr. E dey represent only 1 part out of the 16 total offspring.

questions.q: A plant breeder wants to find out whether a tall pea plant showing the dominant phenotype is homozygous (TT) or heterozygous (Tt). Which cross would best help the breeder determine this?
o: Cross the tall plant with a heterozygous tall plant
Cross the tall plant with another tall plant of unknown genotype
Self-pollinate the tall plant and observe the F1 generation only
Cross the tall plant with a homozygous recessive dwarf plant
questions.e: Crossing an organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive individual is called a test cross. If any offspring show the recessive trait, the unknown parent must be heterozygous.
questions.p: To know whether plant na TT or Tt, you must cross am with recessive dwarf tt. If any dwarf pikin show face, you don know say na Tt.

questions.q: A pure-breeding round-seeded pea plant (RR) is crossed with a pure-breeding wrinkled-seeded pea plant (rr). What are the expected genotype and phenotype of the F1 offspring?
questions.e: Crossing RR with rr gives only Rr offspring in the F1 generation. Since round seed shape is dominant, all the F1 plants show round seeds.
questions.p: When you cross RR and rr, all the F1 pikin go carry Rr genotype. Because round seed dey dominant, everywhere go round.

questions.q: In the sex-determination mechanism of a certain bird species, the female is heterogametic (ZW) while the male is homogametic (ZZ). If a cross is made between a male and a female, what proportion of the offspring is expected to be male?
questions.e: A ZZ male produces only Z gametes, while a ZW female produces Z and W gametes in equal numbers. Fertilisation gives ZZ (male) and ZW (female) offspring in a 1:1 ratio, so 50% are male.
questions.p: Male ZZ go give only Z gamete, but female ZW go give Z and W. When dem join, you go get ZZ and ZW for 1:1 ratio, so 50% na male.

questions.q: A woman who is a known carrier of a certain X-linked recessive disorder marries a man who also suffers from the same disorder. What proportion of their daughters is expected to be affected by the disorder?
questions.e: The carrier mother is X^A X^a and the affected father is X^a Y. Daughters receive one X from each parent, giving X^A X^a (carrier) or X^a X^a (affected) in equal proportion, so half the daughters are affected.
questions.p: Mama na X^A X^a and Papa na X^a Y. Half of di daughters go get X^A X^a wey be carrier, and di other half go get X^a X^a wey be affected.

questions.q: Which of the following statements best explains why a man can never inherit an X-linked trait from his father?
o: X-linked genes are destroyed during the formation of sperm cells in the father
Genes on the Y chromosome mask the expression of X-linked genes in males
A man's X chromosome is always inherited from his father during fertilisation
A man receives his single X chromosome only from his mother, while his Y chromosome comes from his father
questions.e: A son's sex chromosome combination is XY, where the X comes from the mother's egg and the Y comes from the father's sperm. Since the father contributes only the Y chromosome to a son, he cannot pass on X-linked traits to him.
questions.p: Boy pikin dey get XY chromosome. Di X dey come from mama, and di Y dey come from papa, so papa no fit pass X-linked trait give im son.

questions.q: During a blood donation exercise at a Nigerian teaching hospital, a sample from a patient agglutinates with anti-A serum but not with anti-B serum. Which of the following blood groups does this patient most likely belong to?
questions.e: Agglutination with anti-A serum means the red blood cells carry the A antigen, while no reaction with anti-B serum means the B antigen is absent. This combination corresponds to blood group A.
questions.p: If blood agglutinate with anti-A, e mean say A antigen dey. Since e no react with anti-B, e mean say B antigen no dey, so na blood group A.

questions.q: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a mutant allele (Hb^S) that is co-dominant with the normal allele (Hb^A). Two parents, both of genotype Hb^A Hb^S, have four children. What is the expected number of children with the sickle cell trait (carriers) out of the four?
questions.e: A cross between two Hb^A Hb^S parents gives offspring in the ratio 1 Hb^A Hb^A : 2 Hb^A Hb^S : 1 Hb^S Hb^S. Hb^A Hb^S individuals are carriers, so half of the four children, that is two, are expected to carry the trait.
questions.p: When two Hb^A Hb^S parents born, di ratio na 1:2:1. Two out of every four pikin go be Hb^A Hb^S, wey be carriers of di sickle cell trait.

questions.q: A certain inherited disorder in human beings appears only when an individual inherits the defective allele from both parents, and it affects males and females with equal frequency. Which mode of inheritance does this disorder most likely follow?
questions.e: Because the gene is located on an autosome rather than a sex chromosome, both males and females are equally likely to be affected. The recessive nature means two copies of the faulty allele, one from each parent, are required for the disorder to show.
questions.p: If di gene dey for autosome, boy and girl get equal chance to get am. Because e be recessive, you must get two faulty allele before e show.

questions.q: A baby boy is born with an extra X chromosome, giving him a karyotype of 47 chromosomes including XXY, and he shows features such as reduced fertility and some feminised body characteristics. This condition arises from which of the following genetic events?
o: A point mutation in a single gene on the Y chromosome
Non-disjunction of sex chromosomes during gamete formation
Crossing over between the X and Y chromosomes during meiosis
Deletion of part of the X chromosome during meiosis
questions.e: The extra X chromosome results from non-disjunction, where sex chromosomes fail to separate properly during meiosis, producing a gamete with two sex chromosomes instead of one. Fertilisation of such a gamete gives the XXY karyotype described, which is known as Klinefelter syndrome.
questions.p: Non-disjunction mean say chromosome no separate well during meiosis. Dis one make gamete get extra chromosome, wey come lead to XXY condition.

questions.q: Chidi has blood group genotype I^A i, while his wife Amaka has blood group genotype I^B i. Considering the inheritance of the ABO blood group alleles, what is the probability that their next child will have blood group O?
questions.e: Crossing I^A i with I^B i gives offspring genotypes I^A I^B, I^A i, I^B i and ii in equal proportion. Only the ii genotype produces blood group O, so the probability is 1 out of 4.
questions.p: If you cross I^A i and I^B i, you go get I^A I^B, I^A i, I^B i, and ii. Only di ii genotype na blood group O, so di chance na 1 out of 4.

questions.q: A man with colour blindness (an X-linked recessive condition) marries a woman who is also colour blind. What proportion of their sons is expected to be colour blind?
questions.e: The father contributes Y to all sons, while the colour-blind mother is X^c X^c, so every son receives X^c from her. All sons will therefore be colour blind.
questions.p: Papa dey give Y chromosome to all im sons, but mama wey get colour blindness get X^c X^c. So, every son must collect X^c from mama, wey mean say all of dem go get colour blindness.

questions.q: During a genetics practical at a Nigerian secondary school, a teacher explains that in humans the sex of a baby is determined at the point of fertilization. Which statement correctly describes this mechanism?
o: The egg determines the sex because it carries either an X or a Y chromosome
Sex is determined only after birth by hormonal changes in the child
The sex chromosome carried by the fertilizing sperm determines the sex of the offspring
Sex is determined by the number of autosomes contributed by the mother
questions.e: In humans, every egg carries an X chromosome, but sperm can carry either X or Y. The sperm that fertilizes the egg therefore decides whether the baby is XX (female) or XY (male).
questions.p: For human, all egg get X chromosome, but sperm fit carry X or Y. Na the sperm wey reach the egg first dey decide if the baby go be XX for girl or XY for boy.

questions.q: A young man in Lagos is found to have a karyotype of 47 chromosomes with the sex chromosome constitution XXY. He has poorly developed testes and is usually infertile. This condition arises due to which of the following events?
o: Duplication of an autosome during mitosis after fertilization
Deletion of a segment of the X chromosome during gamete formation
Crossing over between the X and Y chromosomes
Non-disjunction of the X chromosomes during meiosis in a parent
questions.e: Klinefelter syndrome (XXY) results when sex chromosomes fail to separate properly (non-disjunction) during meiosis in one parent, producing a gamete with an extra X chromosome. Fertilization then gives an individual with 47 chromosomes instead of 46.
questions.p: Klinefelter syndrome (XXY) dey happen when sex chromosomes no separate well during meiosis. This one come make one gamete get extra X chromosome, so the pikin come get 47 chromosomes instead of 46.

questions.q: A pregnant Rhesus-negative woman, Mrs Bello, is married to a Rhesus-positive man. Their first child was Rhesus-positive and healthy, but in a later pregnancy the developing fetus is at risk of a condition in which the mother's antibodies attack the baby's red blood cells. What is this condition called?
questions.e: When an Rh-negative mother is sensitized by an Rh-positive fetus, she can produce anti-Rh antibodies that cross the placenta in later pregnancies and destroy the red blood cells of an Rh-positive baby. This condition is called haemolytic disease of the newborn.
questions.p: If Rh-negative mama carry Rh-positive pikin, e fit start to produce anti-Rh antibodies. For next pregnancy, these antibodies fit cross the placenta and destroy the red blood cells of the baby, wey we dey call haemolytic disease of the newborn.

questions.q: In the ABO blood group system, the gene has three alleles, I^A, I^B and i. A woman of genotype I^A I^B marries a man of genotype ii. What blood groups are possible among their children?
o: Group A, Group B and Group O
Group A and Group B only
questions.e: The mother can pass on I^A or I^B, while the father can only pass on i. This gives children of genotype I^A i (group A) or I^B i (group B), but no group O or AB child can be produced since neither parent supplies two recessive alleles together with an I^A I^B combination.
questions.p: Mama fit give I^A or I^B, but papa fit only give i. This one mean say the pikin dem go be either I^A i for group A or I^B i for group B.

questions.q: Haemophilia is an X-linked recessive disorder in which blood fails to clot normally. A woman whose father was haemophiliac but who herself shows no symptoms marries a normal man. What is the chance that one of their sons will be haemophiliac?
questions.e: Since her father was haemophiliac, the woman must be a carrier, X^H X^h, while the normal man is X^H Y. Crossing these gives sons who are X^H Y (normal) or X^h Y (haemophiliac) in equal numbers, so half of the sons are expected to be affected.
questions.p: Because the woman papa get haemophilia, she be carrier (X^H X^h). When she marry normal man, half of their sons go get the disease because they go collect the X^h from their mama.

questions.q: A particular genetic disorder in humans is caused by a single gene mutation that results in abnormally shaped, crescent-like red blood cells, reduced oxygen transport, and painful crises, especially under low-oxygen conditions. Which of the following best names this disorder?
questions.e: Sickle cell anaemia is caused by a mutant haemoglobin allele that makes red blood cells take on a crescent or sickle shape, reducing their ability to carry oxygen efficiently and causing painful crises.
questions.p: Sickle cell anaemia na condition wey one mutant haemoglobin gene dey change the shape of red blood cells to crescent. This one come make the blood no fit carry oxygen well and e dey cause serious pain.

questions.q: A couple seek genetic counselling before marriage. Both partners are blood group O and both have normal vision, but the woman's brother is colour blind (an X-linked recessive trait), and genetic testing shows the woman is a carrier. If the couple has children, what is the probability of having a colour-blind daughter?
questions.e: The father has normal vision, so he contributes a normal X allele to every daughter he has. Even though the mother is a carrier, a daughter needs two recessive alleles to be colour blind, and the father cannot supply one, so no daughter can be colour blind; only sons would have a 50% chance of being affected.
questions.p: The papa get normal vision, so all im daughters go collect one normal X from am. Because the daughter must get two recessive alleles to be colour blind, e no possible for any daughter to get the condition.

questions.q: A farmer in Kano noticed that a species of weevil found in his grain store existed in two forms: a reddish-brown form and a dark form. Over several years, the dark form became more common after the store was painted black inside. This change in colour proportion within the population over time is best described as a demonstration of which concept?
questions.e: A gradual change in the characteristics of a population over successive generations, such as the shift in colour proportions, is the basic definition of organic evolution. The other terms do not describe gradual change in a population.
questions.p: As small small change dey happen inside population over time, na im dem dey call organic evolution. Di way di colour shift show say evolution dey happen.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes the theory of biogenesis as opposed to the theory of spontaneous generation (abiogenesis)?
o: Living things can only arise from pre-existing living things
Life first appeared on earth as a result of chemical evolution in the oceans
Simple organic molecules formed spontaneously in the primitive atmosphere and later combined to form life
Living things can arise suddenly from non-living matter under suitable conditions
questions.e: Biogenesis states that life only comes from already existing life, unlike spontaneous generation which claims life arises from non-living matter. The other options describe ideas related to chemical or spontaneous origin of life, not biogenesis.
questions.p: Biogenesis dey talk say life dey only come from another life wey don dey before. E no be like spontaneous generation wey dey talk say life fit just burst up from ordinary dirt.
