questions.q: A student compares the bones in the forelimb of a lizard, the wing of a bird and the arm of a man and finds that all three have the same basic arrangement of bones, though modified for different functions. Which term best describes these structures?
questions.e: Structures that have the same basic origin and arrangement but are modified for different functions in different organisms are called homologous structures. Analogous and convergent structures refer to similar function but different origin, which is not the case here.
questions.p: If body part get di same original structure but dem dey do different work, na homologous structures we dey call am. Di bone arrangement show say dem get common ancestor.

questions.q: In a certain isolated bacterial population of 1,000,000 cells, a random mutation conferring resistance to a toxin arises in only one cell. Which condition would most favour this new allele becoming common in the population within a few generations?
o: The population size increases rapidly without any exposure to the toxin
The toxin remains present, strongly reducing survival of non-resistant cells
The toxin is completely removed from the environment immediately
The mutation provides no advantage under the existing conditions
questions.e: For a rare favourable mutation to spread quickly, there must be strong selective pressure that kills or reduces the non-resistant individuals, giving the resistant ones a survival and reproductive advantage. Removing the toxin or having no advantage would not favour the spread of the allele.
questions.p: For one new gene to quick spread, wahala must dey wey go kill di ones wey no get di gene. If di toxin dey ground, di resistant cells go survive and born plenty.

questions.q: According to Charles Darwin's theory of natural selection, which of the following best explains how long-necked giraffes became the dominant form in a population of giraffes with varying neck lengths?
o: Short-necked giraffes deliberately avoided mating to allow long-necked giraffes to dominate
All giraffes developed longer necks simultaneously in response to environmental need
Giraffes stretched their necks over their lifetime to reach high leaves and passed this acquired trait to offspring
Giraffes with longer necks already existed as natural variation and were better able to survive and reproduce when food was scarce
questions.e: Darwin proposed that variation already exists naturally in a population, and individuals best suited to the environment survive and reproduce more, passing on their traits. The idea of stretching necks and passing on acquired traits belongs to Lamarck's theory, not Darwin's.
questions.p: Darwin talk say natural variation dey already, and di ones wey fit survive di condition na dem dey live long to born pikin. Na nature select di long-necked ones, no be say dem stretch neck.

questions.q: Which of the following pieces of evidence for evolution relies specifically on comparing the geographical distribution of similar and related species across different continents and islands?
questions.e: Biogeography studies the distribution of organisms across different regions of the world and uses patterns such as related species on separate continents as evidence for common ancestry and evolution. The other options rely on structure, chemistry, or development rather than geographic distribution.
questions.p: Biogeography na di study of how animals and plants spread across different places for world. E dey show how related species land for different continents.

questions.q: A geneticist studying two groups of lizards separated for thousands of years on different islands finds that although they look slightly different, they can still interbreed and produce fertile offspring when brought together. Based on the biological species concept, what can be concluded about these two groups?
o: They have evolved into two completely new species
They are hybrids that cannot reproduce further
They are still considered the same species since they can interbreed and produce fertile offspring
They are separate species because they developed on different islands
questions.e: The biological species concept defines a species as a group of organisms capable of interbreeding and producing fertile offspring. Since the two lizard groups can still do this despite physical differences, they remain the same species, not separate or new species.
questions.p: According to biology, once two animals fit mate and born pikin wey fit also born, dem still be di same species. Even if dem stay different island, as dem fit reproduce together, dem still be one.

questions.q: A particular species of fish found only in the rivers of the Niger Delta shows unique features not seen in related species elsewhere in the world. This pattern of unique species occurring in specific geographical regions provides evidence for evolution based on which concept?
questions.e: Biogeography studies how species are distributed across different regions, and unique species confined to specific areas suggest they evolved independently after geographic isolation from ancestral populations. This supports the idea of divergence through evolution.
questions.p: Biogeography dey show how living things spread across different places. When unique species dey only one particular area, e mean say dem evolve by themselves after dem separate from their ancestors.

questions.q: In a breeding experiment, a Biology teacher in Jos crosses two groups of guinea pigs that have remained reproductively isolated in different cages for many generations due to a physical barrier. When the barrier is removed and individuals from both groups mate, all resulting offspring are fertile and healthy. Based on the biological species concept, what can be concluded about these two groups?
o: They belong to the same species despite being kept apart
They are hybrids incapable of further reproduction
They have undergone complete adaptive radiation
They represent two distinct species that cannot interbreed naturally
questions.e: According to the biological species concept, organisms that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring belong to the same species, regardless of temporary separation. Since the offspring were fertile and healthy, the two groups are still one species.
questions.p: According to biology, if two groups fit mate and produce healthy pikin wey fit born too, na the same species dem be. Even if dem stay apart before, the fact say their pikin healthy show say na one family.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the main idea behind the theory of 'special creation' regarding the origin of living things, as opposed to the theory of organic evolution?
o: All living things arose gradually from simple ancestral forms through natural processes over millions of years
New species constantly arise from existing ones through accumulated genetic mutations
Living things arose spontaneously from non-living matter under suitable environmental conditions
Each kind of living organism was created in its present form by a supreme being and has remained unchanged since
questions.e: Special creation holds that each type of organism was individually created in its current form and does not change over time, unlike evolution which proposes gradual change from common ancestors. This is a fundamental contrast tested in evolution theory topics.
questions.p: Special creation talk say God create every living thing for their present form and dem no dey change. E dey different from evolution wey say na small small change happen over millions of years.

questions.q: A population of 500 rabbits on an isolated hill near Jos has a recessive allele 'b' for a coat colour defect at a frequency of 0.2, while the dominant allele 'B' has a frequency of 0.8. Assuming the population is in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, how many rabbits are expected to show the recessive phenotype?
questions.e: The frequency of the recessive phenotype equals q^2, which is 0.2 x 0.2 = 0.04. Multiplying 0.04 by the population size of 500 gives 20 rabbits expected to show the recessive trait.
questions.p: To find the number of rabbits with the recessive trait, you go square the recessive allele frequency (0.2 x 0.2 = 0.04) and multiply am by the total population of 500 to get 20.

questions.q: Scientists studying marsupial mammals in Australia and placental mammals in other continents find that both groups independently evolved similar body forms, such as a wolf-like marsupial and a true wolf, despite having very different ancestry. What term best describes this evolutionary pattern?
questions.e: Convergent evolution occurs when unrelated organisms independently evolve similar traits because they adapt to similar environments or lifestyles, even though their evolutionary origins differ. The marsupial and placental wolves resemble each other due to similar ecological pressures, not shared ancestry.
questions.p: Convergent evolution happen when different animals wey no get same ancestors come dey look alike because dem dey live for similar environment. Na the same ecological pressure cause am.

questions.q: In a controlled laboratory experiment in a Nigerian university, a flask containing sterilized nutrient broth was sealed with a swan-necked flask design that allowed air in but trapped dust particles and microorganisms in the curved neck. After several weeks, no microbial growth was observed in the broth. This classic type of experiment was used to disprove which theory?
questions.e: This experiment, similar to Louis Pasteur's famous swan-neck flask experiment, showed that life does not arise spontaneously from non-living matter when microorganisms are prevented from entering a sterile medium. It supported the theory of biogenesis instead.
questions.p: Dis swan-neck flask experiment help to scatter the idea of spontaneous generation. E prove say living things no just dey come out from non-living matter if you block germs from entering.

questions.q: A trait that confers a slight survival advantage in a large, randomly mating population is most likely to increase in frequency over many generations mainly because of which process?
o: Genetic drift causing random changes in allele frequency
Natural selection favouring individuals with the advantageous trait
Gene flow bringing the trait in from neighbouring populations
Mutation introducing the trait repeatedly in each generation
questions.e: In a large population, natural selection is the main force that increases the frequency of traits giving a survival or reproductive advantage, since individuals with the trait leave more offspring over time. Genetic drift has a weaker effect in large populations compared to small ones.
questions.p: Natural selection na the main reason why good traits dey increase for big population. Those wey get the advantage go survive well well and born more pikin.

questions.q: In the human liver, the malaria parasite undergoes a stage of development before invading red blood cells. What is this liver stage called?
questions.e: After a mosquito bite, sporozoites travel to the liver and multiply asexually inside liver cells; this is called exo-erythrocytic schizogony. It occurs before the parasite enters red blood cells to cause symptoms.
questions.p: When mosquito bite person, the sporozoites dey go liver go multiply inside liver cells before dem enter red blood cells. We dey call dis liver stage exo-erythrocytic schizogony.

questions.q: A community health worker explains that a disease is caused by a tiny organism living inside or on a host, deriving nourishment from the host while causing it harm. Which term best describes this organism?
questions.e: A parasite is an organism that lives on or in another organism (the host), feeding off it and usually causing harm. Not all parasites are pathogens, and vectors merely transmit disease agents rather than living off the host.
questions.p: Na parasite be living organism wey dey stay inside or on top another organism (host), dey chop from am and dey cause am harm. E different from vector wey just dey carry disease come.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains why severe dehydration is the major cause of death in untreated cholera patients?
o: The bacterium invades the bloodstream and damages red blood cells
The bacterium destroys the lining of the small intestine completely
The toxin causes excessive loss of water and electrolytes through watery stool
The toxin paralyses the kidneys, stopping urine production
questions.e: Cholera toxin makes intestinal cells secrete large amounts of water and salts into the gut, producing profuse watery diarrhoea. This massive fluid loss leads to dehydration, which can be fatal if not replaced quickly.
questions.p: Cholera toxin dey make belle cells pour plenty water and salt comot for body, na im cause watery diarrhoea. If dem no replace the water sharp sharp, person fit die from dehydration.

questions.q: A baby born to an HIV-positive mother tests positive for HIV antibodies at birth but tests negative at 18 months without any treatment. What is the most likely explanation for this change?
o: The test used at birth was faulty and gave a wrong result
The baby developed active immunity that cleared the virus completely
The baby's white blood cells destroyed the HIV virus permanently
The antibodies detected at birth were maternal antibodies that gradually disappeared
questions.e: Maternal antibodies cross the placenta and can be detected in a newborn's blood even if the baby is not infected. These borrowed antibodies fade over time, so a later negative test at 18 months suggests the baby was never truly infected.
questions.p: Na mama antibodies cross enter pikin body before birth, na im make test show positive at first. As time dey go, those antibodies go clear, meaning say pikin no get HIV at all.

questions.q: Which statement correctly describes how a vaccine prepared from an inactivated (killed) pathogen protects the body?
o: It transfers antibodies from an already immune person to the recipient
It stimulates the body to produce memory cells without causing the actual disease
It supplies ready-made antibodies that directly neutralise the pathogen
It introduces antitoxins that destroy the toxins produced by the pathogen
questions.e: A killed-pathogen vaccine contains antigens that cannot cause disease but still trigger the immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells. This prepares the body to respond quickly if the real pathogen is encountered later.
questions.p: Vaccine wey contain dead pathogen no dey cause disease, but e dey make body produce antibodies and memory cells. E dey prepare body make e ready if the real sickness come later.

questions.q: During a malaria awareness talk in a secondary school in Ibadan, a teacher explains that only female Anopheles mosquitoes transmit malaria, not the males. What is the best biological reason for this?
o: Male mosquitoes are not attracted to the scent of human skin
Female mosquitoes have a longer lifespan than males, allowing more bites
Male mosquitoes do not fly long distances to find human hosts
Only female mosquitoes require a blood meal to develop their eggs
questions.e: Female Anopheles mosquitoes need the protein in blood to develop their eggs, so they bite humans and animals. Males feed only on nectar and plant juices, so they do not transmit the malaria parasite.
questions.p: Na only female Anopheles mosquito dey need blood protein to develop their eggs, na im make dem dey bite people. Male mosquito na only nectar and plant juice dem dey chop.

questions.q: A health official describes an immunity that is acquired naturally when a person suffers an infection, recovers, and produces antibodies and memory cells against the pathogen without receiving any external antibodies. Which type of immunity is this?
questions.e: When the body itself fights off an infection and forms its own antibodies and memory cells, this is naturally acquired active immunity. It is natural because no vaccine was given, and active because the body produced the response itself.
questions.p: When body fight sickness by itself and produce im own antibodies and memory cells, na naturally acquired active immunity be dat. E natural because nobody give you vaccine.

questions.q: A village in Niger State reported that most people above 40 years rarely show severe malaria symptoms despite living in a highly malaria-endemic area, while young children frequently fall seriously ill. Which explanation best accounts for this observation?
o: Adults have developed partial immunity from repeated exposure to the parasite over the years
The Plasmodium parasite cannot survive in adult blood due to higher body temperature
Children have weaker red blood cells that cannot carry oxygen properly
Adults are naturally resistant to mosquito bites due to thicker skin
questions.e: Repeated malaria infections over many years allow adults to build up partial immunity, reducing the severity of symptoms even though they may still carry the parasite. Young children have not had this repeated exposure, so they suffer more severe illness.
questions.p: As adults don chop malaria over and over for many years, their body don get partial immunity to fight am well. But small pikin never get that experience, na im make the sickness dey catch dem serious.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correct pairing of a disease with its causative agent?
questions.e: HIV is a retrovirus that causes AIDS by attacking the immune system. Malaria is caused by a protozoan, cholera by a bacterium and tuberculosis by a bacterium, so the other pairings are wrong.
questions.p: Na HIV be retrovirus wey dey cause AIDS by to attack our body defence system. Malaria na protozoan dey cause am, cholera na bacterium, and tuberculosis na also bacterium, so na only option C correct.

questions.q: A patient who recovered from an attack of malaria still has the Plasmodium parasites hidden in some liver cells, which can later multiply and cause a relapse. What term best describes this stage of the parasite in the liver?
questions.e: Hypnozoites are dormant forms of certain Plasmodium species that remain inactive in liver cells and can reactivate later to cause relapse. Sporozoites are the infective forms injected by mosquitoes, merozoites invade red blood cells, and gametocytes are the sexual forms taken up by mosquitoes.
questions.p: Hypnozoites na the sleep-sleep form of some Plasmodium wey dey hide inside liver cells without moving. Later, dem fit wake up to make person get malaria relapse again.

questions.q: During a cholera outbreak in a riverine community in Bayelsa State, health workers advised residents to always boil water before drinking and to wash hands properly before eating. This advice is most directly aimed at preventing which mode of disease spread?
o: Faecal-oral transmission through contaminated water and food
questions.e: Cholera bacteria spread mainly through water and food contaminated with faeces from infected persons. Boiling water and washing hands reduce this faecal-oral route, unlike the other transmission routes listed.
questions.p: Cholera germ dey pass enter body mostly through water and food wey faeces don contaminate. When you boil water and wash hand well well, you dey stop dat faecal-oral transmission.

questions.q: A student states that vaccination works because the vaccine itself immediately kills any pathogen that later enters the body. Which correction best explains the true mechanism of vaccine-induced protection?
o: The vaccine replaces damaged white blood cells with new ones permanently
The vaccine directly destroys pathogens on contact before they enter cells
The vaccine coats body cells so pathogens cannot attach to them physically
The vaccine stimulates memory cells that enable a faster, stronger antibody response on future exposure
questions.e: Vaccines work by exposing the immune system to antigens so that memory lymphocytes are formed. On real exposure to the pathogen, these memory cells allow a quicker and stronger antibody response, not by directly killing pathogens or coating cells.
questions.p: Vaccine dey train our body immunity to keep memory cells. When the real disease come later, those memory cells go produce antibodies quick quick to fight am.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an opportunistic infection in relation to a person living with untreated HIV/AIDS?
o: An infection that can only be transmitted through blood transfusion
An infection by an organism that rarely causes disease in a healthy person but thrives because the immune system is weakened
An infection caused directly by the HIV virus multiplying in the lungs
An infection that only affects people who have never been vaccinated
questions.e: Opportunistic infections take advantage of a weakened immune system, especially the reduced number of helper T-cells in HIV/AIDS patients. Such organisms, like certain fungi and bacteria, usually cause little harm in people with healthy immunity.
questions.p: Opportunistic infection na sickness wey dey catch person because im body defence don weak finish. Normal person body fit fight am, but HIV patient body no fit.

questions.q: A community in Kebbi State drains nearby stagnant ponds and introduces fish that feed on mosquito larvae as part of a malaria control programme. This approach mainly targets which stage of the malaria transmission cycle?
o: The gametocyte stage circulating in human blood
The schizont stage inside human red blood cells
The larval and pupal stages of the mosquito vector in water
The sporozoite stage inside the mosquito's salivary glands
questions.e: Draining stagnant water and introducing larvae-eating fish destroys mosquito larvae and pupae before they develop into adult mosquitoes. This reduces the vector population and interrupts transmission without directly affecting parasite stages inside humans.
questions.p: To remove stagnant water and put fish wey dey chop mosquito pikin na to kill the larval and pupal stages inside water. E dey stop mosquito make dem no come grow to adult.

questions.q: In an experiment, two groups of mice were injected with a toxin. Group X had earlier received antibodies produced by another mouse against the toxin, while Group Y had earlier received an injection containing a weakened form of the toxin-producing organism itself. After some weeks, both groups were exposed to the live toxin-producing organism. Which statement correctly compares the type of immunity in both groups?
o: Group X has active immunity while Group Y has passive immunity
Group X has passive immunity while Group Y has active immunity
Both groups have active immunity because antibodies were involved in each case
Both groups have passive immunity because neither group's own cells produced antibodies initially
questions.e: Group X received ready-made antibodies from another organism, which is passive immunity and usually short-lived. Group Y was exposed to a weakened organism, triggering its own immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells, which is active immunity.
questions.p: Group X collect ready-made antibody, so na passive immunity. Group Y make im own antibody and memory cells because dem give am weak form of the germ, so na active immunity.

questions.q: Biotechnology can be defined as the use of living organisms or their products to
o: modify or improve products for human use
convert light energy to chemical energy only
destroy pathogenic microorganisms in the soil
questions.e: Biotechnology involves using living things, their parts or processes to develop or modify products and processes for human benefit. The other options describe unrelated biological processes.
questions.p: Biotechnology na when person use living things or their product to change or make better product for human use. Na only this option correct because the other ones dey talk about different biology matter.

questions.q: In genetic engineering, restriction enzymes are mainly used to
o: replicate DNA strands during cell division
join two DNA fragments permanently together
cut DNA molecules at specific nucleotide sequences
questions.e: Restriction enzymes act like molecular scissors that recognise and cut DNA at specific base sequences. Joining DNA fragments is instead carried out by an enzyme called DNA ligase.
questions.p: Restriction enzymes dey act like scissor wey dey cut DNA for specific base sequence. Na DNA ligase dey join DNA together, no be restriction enzyme.

questions.q: A small circular piece of bacterial DNA that is commonly used as a vector to carry foreign genes into a host cell is called a
questions.e: A plasmid is a small circular DNA molecule found in bacteria that can be cut open, combined with a foreign gene, and reinserted into a host cell. Ribosomes, centromeres and nucleolus are cell structures, not DNA vectors.
questions.p: Plasmid na small circular DNA inside bacteria wey scientists dey use carry foreign gene enter host cell. Ribosomes and the rest na cell parts, no be DNA vector.

questions.q: During genetic engineering, after a desired gene has been inserted into a plasmid using restriction enzymes, which enzyme seals the gene into the plasmid to form a complete recombinant DNA molecule?
questions.e: DNA ligase joins the sticky ends of the foreign gene and the cut plasmid together, sealing the sugar-phosphate backbone to form recombinant DNA. The other enzymes are involved in replication or transcription, not joining DNA fragments.
questions.p: Na DNA ligase dey join the sticky ends of foreign gene and cut plasmid together to form recombinant DNA. The other enzyme dem dey do different work like replication.

questions.q: Dolly the sheep was produced by a cloning technique that involved
o: mixing sperm cells from two male sheep with one egg cell
doubling the chromosome number of a fertilised zygote
transferring the nucleus of a body cell into an egg cell whose nucleus had been removed
fusing two haploid gametes from different sheep
questions.e: Dolly was produced by somatic cell nuclear transfer, where the nucleus from an adult body cell was placed into an enucleated egg cell, which then developed into an embryo. This produces an organism genetically identical to the nucleus donor.
questions.p: Dolly the sheep na product of somatic cell nuclear transfer where body cell nucleus enter egg cell wey dem don remove nucleus. E dey make the animal look exactly like the person wey give the nucleus.

questions.q: A major advantage of genetically modified crops such as Bt cotton, which has been introduced to some Nigerian farmers, is that the crop
o: produces its own toxin that resists certain insect pests
grows only in hydroponic culture without soil
automatically converts to a different species after harvest
requires no sunlight to carry out photosynthesis
questions.e: Bt cotton contains a gene from a bacterium that enables the plant to produce a protein toxic to specific insect pests, reducing the need for chemical pesticides. The other statements are not true of genetically modified crops.
questions.p: Bt cotton get gene from bacterium wey make plant produce toxin to fight certain insect pests so farmer no go need plenty chemical pesticide. The other option dem no make sense for GMO crops.

questions.q: A farmer in Kano wants to use tissue culture to rapidly produce many disease-free plantlets that are genetically identical to a high-yielding parent cassava plant. Which feature of plant cells makes this technique possible?
o: Plant cells lack a cell wall, allowing easy division
Plant cells contain chloroplasts that divide independently
Plant cells have a fixed chromosome number that cannot change
Plant cells are totipotent and can regenerate a whole new plant from a single cell
questions.e: Totipotency means a single plant cell retains the genetic information needed to develop into a complete new plant under suitable conditions, which is the principle behind tissue culture propagation. Chloroplast presence and chromosome number do not explain this regenerative ability.
questions.p: Totipotency mean say single plant cell get capacity to grow and become full new plant under good condition. Na dis property tissue culture dey use.

questions.q: A molecular biologist wants to produce human insulin using bacteria. The human insulin gene is first isolated, cut out with a restriction enzyme, and inserted into a bacterial plasmid using DNA ligase. The recombinant plasmid is then introduced into a bacterium, which is allowed to multiply in culture. Which statement best explains why this method can supply large quantities of pure human insulin cheaply?
o: The bacterium multiplies rapidly, and each daughter cell carries a copy of the human gene that directs insulin production
The restriction enzyme itself manufactures insulin directly from glucose in the culture medium
The plasmid prevents the bacterium from producing its own proteins, leaving only insulin to be made
The bacterium converts its own DNA permanently into human DNA after one generation
questions.e: Because bacteria reproduce very quickly by binary fission, each new cell inherits the recombinant plasmid containing the human insulin gene, so a large bacterial culture can produce large amounts of insulin in a short time. The restriction enzyme only cuts DNA and does not manufacture insulin, and the bacterium's own DNA is not converted into human DNA.
questions.p: Because bacteria dey multiply fast fast, every new cell go carry human insulin gene to produce plenty insulin. Restriction enzyme na just for cutting DNA, e no dey manufacture insulin.
